We indeed acknowledge an irresistible force of the Spirit in the understanding, when God, illuminating the understanding, reveals his will; and in the heart, when he knocks at our hearts; but that grace by which our will is determined to good, and by which the Holy Spirit effects in us an act of faith and whatever work of obedience God demands of us in the gospel, this grace we call resistible, because a man can resist it by his own will and impede its action.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 191. Possumus Spiritui Sancto resistere, quū in homine operatur cum voluntate & proposito ipsum convertendi.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 191. We can resist the Holy Spirit when he works in a man with the will and purpose of converting him.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 193. Possumus DEO resistere, cum nos vult per gratiam suam convertere. Item. Hæc DEI voluntas nihil aliud est, quam quod DEUS velit ut homo seipsum convertat.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 193. We can resist God when he wishes to convert us by his grace. Likewise. This will of God is nothing other than that God wills man to convert himself.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 235. Gratia DEI non ubique, neque semper resistentiam omnem sperat in omnibus, in quibus efficaciter vult operari.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 235. The grace of God does not everywhere, nor always, expect resistance from all in whom he effectively wills to work.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 241. Pugnaret cum natura præceptorum divinorum, veraeque obedientiæ, si DEUS suum ipsius opus nobis præciperet, aut opus, ad quod voluntas nostra nihil confert, nec conferre potest.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 241. It would conflict with the nature of the divine precepts and of true obedience if God commanded us his own work, or a work to which our will contributes nothing and cannot contribute.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 247. Negamus omnibus ijs, quibus Spiritus Sanctus cor vult aperire, protinus reipsa aperiri. Nam ubicunque Spiritus pulsat, ibi & aperire vult & intrare: sed non ubicunque pulsat, ibi aperitur cor, nec quocunque vult intrare Spiritus, illuc intrat.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 247. We deny that all those whose heart the Holy Spirit wills to open are at once actually opened. For wherever the Spirit knocks, there he wills both to open and to enter; but wherever he knocks, the heart is not opened, nor does the Spirit enter wherever he wills to enter.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 269. Dicimus multos posse venire ad Christum, qui tamen reipsa non veniant.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 269. We say that many can come to Christ, who nevertheless in fact do not come.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 196: Fides & conversio non possunt vocari obedientia, si ab alio aliquo solo efficiantur, ita ut homo in eo se habeat mere passive.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 196: Faith and conversion cannot be called obedience, if they are effected by some other alone, so that man in this respect is related merely passively.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 243. Gratia DEI homines quidem prævenit, & efficaciter movet, ita tamen ut ipsi per DEI virtu-tem & gratiam cooperari debeant.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 243. The grace of God indeed goes before men and moves them effectively, yet in such a way that they themselves ought to cooperate through the power and grace of God.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 246. Ad cordis apertionem requiritur ho-minis cooperatio. Si enim homini a DEO præcipitur, ut in conversione cor suum aperiat, sequitur hanc apertionem a DEO sine voluntatis humanae cooperatione non effi-ci.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 246. Human cooperation is required for the opening of the heart. For if man is commanded by God to open his heart in conversion, it follows that this opening is not effected by God without the cooperation of the human will.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.254. Statuimus itaque hominem esse DEI co-operatorem in perficienda regeneratione sua.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 254. We therefore hold that man is God's co-worker in bringing about his own regeneration.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.275. Negamus fidem appellari donum DEI respectu actualis infusionis in corda nostra: sed ita appellatur respectu potestatis perveniendi ad ipsum.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 275. We deny that faith is called a gift of God with respect to the actual infusion into our hearts; but it is so called with respect to the power of coming to it.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.276. Fides & conversio talia sunt dona, quibus DEUS nos donare non vult, nisi interveniente voluntate nostra.
units.tr: Ibidem.pag.276. Faith and conversion are such gifts that God is unwilling to bestow them upon us except with our will intervening.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.279. Fides in Christum & conversio reipsa non efficiuntur in homine, sine interventu voluntatis humana.
units.tr: Ibidem.pag.279. Faith in Christ and conversion are not actually brought about in a man without the intervention of the human will.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.260. Posset quoque & hoc disputari, An non nobilissima sit actio ea circa hominem, quae sit per suasionem; &c, An conveniens sit alia aliqua circa hominem uti, servatis humanae naturae proprietatibus, ac proinde an non satis vehemens foret operatio, si talis esset, quali utitur Satan.
units.tr: Ibidem.pag.260. It could also be disputed whether the most noble action concerning man is not the one that takes place by persuasion, etc.; whether it is fitting to use some other means concerning man, while preserving the properties of human nature; and therefore whether the operation would not be sufficiently forceful if it were of the kind which Satan uses.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.261. Nihil esset ex eo absurdi, si eadem vis adhiberetur utrimque, & æque potens in se, ita tamen ut Diaboli & aliorum operatio esset resistibilis, DEI vero efficax, quia secundum DEI infinitam sapientiam, circa tale tempus, tales homines, in tali constitutione & statu administraretur.
units.tr: Ibidem.pag.261. There would be nothing absurd in it if the same force were applied on both sides, and equally powerful in itself, yet so that the operation of the Devil and of others were resistible, but that of God efficacious, because according to God's infinite wisdom it is administered at such a time, to such men, in such a condition and state.

units.la: A IAC. ARMINIO, Artic.perpend.pag.24. Vocatio interna etiam contingit iis, qui non assentiuntur vocationi.
units.tr: A IAC. ARMINIO, Artic.perpend.pag.24. The internal calling also happens to those who do not assent to the calling.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.25. Necessario ponenda est gratia sufficiens, quae effectum non sortitur, culpa ejus cui contingit: secus justitia DEI in condemnatione infidelium defendi non potest.
units.tr: Ibidem.pag.25. It must necessarily be posited that a sufficient grace, which does not obtain its effect, is due to the fault of the one to whom it comes; otherwise the justice of God in the condemnation of unbelievers cannot be defended.

units.la: Ibidem. Efficacitas gratiae salutaris non consistit in omnipotente actione DEI, quâ sic agit in mente & in corde hominis, ut cui illa actio imprimitur, non possit non assentiri DEO vocanti, seu quod idem est, gratia non est vis irresistibilis.
units.tr: Ibidem. The efficacy of saving grace does not consist in the omnipotent action of God, by which he so acts in the mind and heart of a man that the one upon whom that action is impressed cannot but assent to God calling; or, which is the same, grace is not an irresistible force.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.26. Qui vocationi DEI obtemperant, illi libere assentiuntur gratiae, ab eâ tamen excitati, impulsi, tracti, adjuti: & eo ipso momento, quo assentiuntur, poterant non assentiri.
units.tr: Ibidem.pag.26. Those who obey God's calling assent freely to grace, though they are roused, impelled, drawn and aided by it; and at the very moment in which they assent, they were able not to assent.

units.la: Ibidem. Ubi homo sentit gratiam mentem & cor afficientem, liberè assentitur, ita ut possit non assentiri.
units.tr: Ibidem. Where a man feels grace affecting his mind and heart, he assents freely, so that he is able not to assent.

units.la: A IOAN. ARNOLDO Contra Til. pag. 337. Arminij sententia hæc est, gratiam non ita instruere hominem viribus, quin semper maneat in potestate hominis ijs uti vel non uti.
units.tr: A IOAN. ARNOLDO Contra Til. pag. 337. The opinion of Arminius is this: grace does not so equip man with powers that it always remains in man's power to use them or not to use them.

units.la: Contra Bogerm. pag. 263. & 274. Positis omnibus operationibus gratiæ, quibus ad conversionem in nobis efficiendam DEVS utitur, manet tamen ipsa conversio ita in nostra potestate libera, ut possimus non converti, id est, nosmetipsos convertere vel non convertere.
units.tr: Contra Bogerm. pag. 263. & 274. With all the operations of grace, by which God uses to bring about conversion in us, conversion itself nevertheless remains so much in our free power that we are able not to be converted; that is, we are able to convert ourselves or not to convert ourselves.

units.la: A NIC. GREVINCHOVIO, Contra Amef. pag. 198. Dicimus gratiam in actuali efficacia liberi actus, seu potius effectum à gratia intentum, etiam pendere ab influxu arbitrij ex gratia operantis, quia gratia licet principalis sit causa, non tamen est totum principium proximum actionis, sed concausa ejus, postulans concomitantiam nostra voluntatis, sic ut ab utroque fluat, eoque & dependeat suo modo influxus actualis.
units.tr: A NIC. GREVINCHOVIO, Contra Amef. pag. 198. We say that grace in the actual efficacy of a free act, or rather the effect intended by grace, also depends on the influence of the will of the one who is operated upon by grace; for grace, although it is the principal cause, is not the whole proximate principle of the action, but its concause, requiring the concurrence of our will, so that the actual influence flows from both and depends in its own way on both.

units.la: Ibidem. Imò ut confidentius agam, dico effectum gratiæ ordinaria lege pendere ab actu aliquo arbitrij, ut præviâ conditione sine qua non.
units.tr: Ibidem. Indeed, to speak more boldly, I say that the effect of grace depends by ordinary law on some act of the will, as a prior condition without which it does not come about.

units.la: Item. Ut vocatio efficax pendet ab auditu, ita etiam ab arbitrio (à quo & auditus ipse dependet) tanquam ab eo in cujus potestate est audiendo acquirere vel non acquirere ea, sine quibus ordinariè vocatio ad fidem non est efficax.
units.tr: Likewise: just as effectual calling depends on hearing, so it also depends on the will (on which hearing itself depends), as on that in whose power it lies, by hearing, to acquire or not to acquire those things without which calling to faith is ordinarily not effectual.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 202. Negamus concursum arbitrij in Paulo esse effectum necessariò gratiam consequentem vi solius gratiæ prædeterminantis, ut causæ adæquatæ conversionis in ijs omnibus, qui hac gratia donantur.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 202. We deny that the concurrence of the will in Paul is an effect that necessarily follows grace by the power of grace alone predetermining, as the adequate cause of conversion in all those who are granted this grace.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 203. & 204. Nostrâ verò sententiam sic paucis accipe; Totius quidem simul complexi (quare scilicet. hæc gratia in Paulo aut Petro potius sit efficax, quam in alio)causam communem dari non posse aliam, præter li-bertatem voluntatis.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 203. & 204. But take our opinion briefly thus: of the whole complex taken together (namely, why this grace should be effectual in Paul or Peter rather than in another), no common cause can be given other than freedom of the will.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 204. Voluntas hominis gratia præveniente excitata est partialis causa conversionis.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 204. The will of man, roused by preceding grace, is a partial cause of conversion.

units.la: Item. Positis duobus adultis, fieri potest, ut æqualibus auxiliis gratiæ præVenientis hic convertatur, ille non convertatur
units.tr: Item. Given two adults, it can happen that with equal aids of preceding grace the one is converted and the other is not converted.

units.la: Ibidem.pag. 205. Voluntas pro sua libertate cooperatur in ipsa determinatione sui ipsius, & in effectione gratiæ cooperantis, atque ita est concausa, vel conditio necessaria, sine cujus concursu actiuo DEUS non influat in illam. Item. Gratia non determinat nisi arbitrio cooperante: qua ratione & modo quid ni dicamus, efficaciam quoque gratia quodammodo ab arbitrio pendere quoad eventum?
units.tr: Ibidem.pag. 205. The will, by its freedom, cooperates in the very determination of itself and in the effecting of cooperating grace, and so is a concause, or a necessary condition, without whose active concurrence God does not flow into it. Item. Grace determines only with the cooperating will. By what reason and manner, then, should we not say that the efficacy of grace too depends in some way on the will as to the outcome?

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 106. Dicimus eo sensu arbitrium determinare gratiam, quod arbitrium libere præstet concursum suum gratiæ cooperanti; vel quod arbitrium ita cooperetur, ut possit non cooperari, adeoque non cooperando impedire cooperationem gratiæ.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 106. We say that the will determines grace in that sense, that the will freely furnishes its concurrence to cooperating grace; or that the will so cooperates that it is able not to cooperate, and so by not cooperating hinders the cooperation of grace.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 208. Liquet arbitrium & gratiam simul esse causas partiales, partialitate causæ, seu causandi, sic ut neu-tra conversionem per se sola efficiat ea virtute qua influit in effectum.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 208. It is clear that will and grace are together partial causes, by partiality of cause or of causing, so that neither by itself alone effects conversion by the power by which it flows into the effect.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 210.& 211. Si pater & filius ambo unam eandemque navem trahant, & filius quidem agendi virtute sibi à Patre communicata; pater autem non modò ut pater, qui filio agendi virtutem dedit, sed etiam ut suasor, motor, atque impulsor filij; adeoque ut autor filio suo navem hanc unâ cum ipso trahendi; hic agnoscès, opinor, duas causas partiales unius effecti simultanei, quarum unaquaque totum effectum suâ virtute producit, etsi non totaliter. Item. Proprium est causæ partialis, virtute suâ, sive à se, sive ab alio accepta & mota, ad eundem actum concurrere cum aliâ causâ, sine quo concursu actus ille non existeret. Sic igitur gratiam & arbitrium conjungimus, ut causas partiales.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 210. & 211. If father and son both draw one and the same ship, and the son indeed by the power of acting communicated to him by the Father, but the father not only as father, who gave the son the power of acting, but also as persuader, mover, and impeller of the son, and thus as author to his son of drawing this ship together with him: here you will recognize, I think, two partial causes of one simultaneous effect, of which each produces the whole effect by its own power, though not totally. Item. It is proper to a partial cause, by its own power, whether received and moved from itself or from another, to concur to the same act with another cause, without whose concurrence that act would not exist. Thus we join grace and will as partial causes.

units.la: Ibidem.pag. 114. Auxilium efficax ordine causalitatis non anteceantecedit efficientiam voluntatis. Item. Auxilium Dei efficax non est in vi ad influxum arbitrij.
units.tr: Ibidem.pag. 114. Effectual help does not precede in the order of causality the efficiency of the will. Item. God's effectual help is not in its power for the influence of the will.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.243. Nego ad conversionem peccatoris concurrere motionem Dei praeviam, quâ voluntas sic determinetur ad consensum, ut non possit dissentire.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag.243. I deny that a prior motion of God, by which the will is so determined to consent that it cannot dissent, concurs in the conversion of a sinner.

units.la: Ibidem.pag. 253. Ego meipsum discerno, quum enim Deo ac praedeterminationi divinae resistere possem, non restiti tamen: atque in eo quid ni mihi liceat tanquam de meo gloriari? Quod enim potui, Dei quidem miserentis est, quod autem volui, cum possem nolle, id meae potestatis.
units.tr: Ibidem.pag. 253. I distinguish myself; for since I could have resisted God and divine predetermination, I did not resist; and in this, why should I not be allowed to boast as of my own? For what I could do is indeed of God who has mercy; but what I willed, when I could have been unwilling, that is in my power.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 271. Nobis certum est Deum multorum conversionem & salutem intendere, in quibus eam non assequitur.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 271. It is certain to us that God intends the conversion and salvation of many, in whom he does not attain it.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 272. Non omnes convertuntur, quos Deus serio atque ex animo voluit convertere.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 272. Not all are converted whom God seriously and from his heart willed to convert.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 279. Concedo in hoc operandi modo Deum etiam quodammodo a voluntate hominis pendere quoad actum determinationis liberae.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 279. I grant that in this mode of operating God too in some way depends on the will of man as to the act of free determination.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.294. Negamus ad conversionem hominis, ex parte Dei, praeter gratiam praevenientem, excitantem, adjuvantem, &c. opus esse gratia determinante.
units.tr: Ibidem.pag.294. We deny that for the conversion of man, on God's part, besides preceding, exciting, helping grace, etc., there is any need of determining grace.

units.la: Ibidem.pag. 297. Quid enim obstat, quo minus vel sola gratia moralis istos ψυχικὰς spirituales reddat?
units.tr: Ibidem.pag. 297. For what stands in the way of grace merely moral making those psychic [ψυχικάς] men spiritual?

units.la: A Conr. Vorstio, Parasc. ad Piscat.pag.4. Quæ Deus liberè prorsus & contingenter à nobis fieri vult, ea potentius aut efficacius, quam per modum voti & desiderij velle non potest.
units.tr: A Conr. Vorstio, Parasc. ad Piscat.pag.4. Those things which God wills to be done by us quite freely and contingently, he cannot will more powerfully or efficaciously than by way of vow and desire.

units.la: A Sim. Episcopio, Disp.de Dominio Dei, Thes.15. Dominium Dei eousque non potest extendi, ut Deus actum illum, quem lege sua ab homine postulat, per omnipotentiam & vim irresistibilem in eo ipse efficiat, & tanquam actum obedientiae praemio remuneretur.
units.tr: A Sim. Episcopio, Disp.de Dominio Dei, Thes.15. The lordship of God cannot be extended so far that God should himself effect in man, through omnipotence and irresistible force, that act which he demands from man by his law, and reward it as an act of obedience with a reward.

units.la: Ibidem. Iure supremi dominij sui dare quidem vitam æternam potest, cui vult, Deus, & si velit ad officium faciendum creaturam suam flectere potest infinitis modis, sed tanquam praemium dare vitam æternam, & tanquam obedientibus dare ijs, in quibus per vim irresistibilem omnia, quæ Lege præscribuntur, effecta sint, id vero DEVS pro jure ac dominio suo facere non potest.
units.tr: Ibidem. By the right of his supreme lordship God can indeed give eternal life to whom he wills, and if he wishes to bend his creature to performing its duty he can do so in infinite ways; but to give eternal life as a reward, and to give it to the obedient, in whom all things prescribed by the law have been brought about by irresistible force, this God cannot do by his right and dominion.

units.la: Disput.privat. 46. Thes. 11. An circa ipsum effectum & voluntatem etiam versetur actio Spiritus sancti, immediatè ei aliquid imprimendo, non audemus, nec necesse habemus asserere, aut negare. Certum est mentem hac ratione illustratam facilè affectum jam obsequendi studio, imò obsequio aliquantum inclinatum, ulterius impellere, eique aspirare vim & ἐνέργειαν [?], quâ correptus affectus voluntatem deinde movet ad actiones affectui similes exercendas, ita tamen, ut pro libertate sua in contrariam semper partem ferri possit.
units.tr: Disput. privat. 46, Thes. 11. Whether the action of the Holy Spirit also works on the effect and on the will itself, by impressing something on it immediately, we do not dare to assert or deny, nor do we need to. It is certain that a mind illuminated in this way is readily driven forward in its affection, which is already inclined by zeal for obedience, or indeed somewhat inclined to obedience, and that the Spirit breathes into it a power and energy [ἐνέργειαν] by which the affection, once seized, then moves the will to perform actions like itself, yet in such a way that, according to its freedom, the will can always be carried to the opposite side.

units.la: Ibidem.corol.1. An ulla actio Spiritus Sancti immediata in voluntatem necessaria sit, ut quis credere possit verbo? Negativam tuebimur.
units.tr: Ibidem, corol. 1. Whether any immediate action of the Holy Spirit upon the will is necessary, so that someone can believe the Word? We will defend the negative.

units.la: Disp.priv.7.de Prædest. Thes.11. Iniquissimum est ab eo exigere obedientiam, in quo actus ipse obediendi per potentiam efficitur.
units.tr: Disp. priv. 7, de Praedest., Thes. 11. It is most unjust to demand obedience from one in whom the very act of obeying is brought about by power.

units.la: Ibidem.thes.12. Quorsum enim postulatur serio id, quod potenter inseritur, atque inditur anima ejus, à quo postulatur.
units.tr: Ibidem, thes. 12. For why is that seriously demanded which is forcibly implanted and infused into the soul of the one from whom it is demanded?

units.la: Ibidem.Disp.8.thes.7. Absurdum est statuere DEVM aut efficere per potentiam, aut procurare per sapientiam, ut electi ea faciant, quæ ab ipsis, ut ipsi ea faciant, exigit & postulat.
units.tr: Ibidem, Disp. 8, thes. 7. It is absurd to hold that God either brings about by power, or secures by wisdom, that the elect do those things which he requires and demands of them, that they themselves should do them.

units.la: Ibidem.Disput.9.thes.3. DEVS nemini mortalium sufficientem gratiam, cujus beneficio salutem consequi potest, negare absoluta voluntate constituit.
units.tr: Ibidem, Disput. 9, thes. 3. God has determined, by his absolute will, to deny to no mortal sufficient grace, by the benefit of which he can obtain salvation.

units.la: ARTICULUS XV. De Peccato Originali.
units.tr: ARTICLE XV. Of Original Sin.

units.la: CRedimus Adami inobedientiâ 1. peccatum quod vocant Originis in totum genus humanum diffusum esse. 2. Est autem peccatum Originis corruptio totius naturæ, & vitium hæreditarium; 3. quo & ipsi infantes in matris utero polluti sunt: 4. quodque velut noxia quædam radix, genus omne peccatorum in homine producit: estque tam fœdum atque execrabile coram DEo, ut ad universi generis humani condemnationem sufficiat. 5. Neq; verò per Baptismum penitus aboletur aut radicitus evellitur; quandoquidem ex illo tanquam ex infaustâ ac corruptâ scaturigine perpetui rivuli assiduè exoriuntur atque effluunt: quamvis filijs DEi in condemnationem non cedat aut imputetur, sed ex purâ DEI gratiâ & misericordia illis remittatur: non ut huic remissioni confidentes obdormiant, sed ut sensus hujus corruptionis crebriores gemitus in fidelibus excitet, utque eo ardentius optent, ab hoc corpore mortis liberari. Hinc ergo Pelagianorum errorem damnamus, qui hoc peccatum originis nihil aliud esse asserunt, quam imitationem.6.
units.tr: We believe that through Adam's disobedience the sin called original has spread into the whole human race: 1. Original sin is a corruption of the whole nature and a hereditary vice, 2. by which even infants themselves are polluted in the mother's womb, 3. and which, like some harmful root, produces in man every kind of sin. It is so foul and abominable before God that it is enough for the condemnation of the whole human race. 4. Nor is it indeed wholly abolished or uprooted by baptism; for from it, as from an unhappy and corrupt spring, perpetual streams constantly arise and flow forth. Although it is not counted or imputed to the children of God for condemnation, but is forgiven them by the pure grace and mercy of God, this is not so that they should fall asleep trusting in that forgiveness, but so that the sense of this corruption may stir more frequent groans in believers, and that they may desire more ardently to be freed from this body of death. Hence we condemn the error of the Pelagians, who assert that this original sin is nothing else than imitation. 6.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this article it seems to be taught:

units.la: I. In ⌣[?]Adamo posteros ejus non peccasse; neq; inobedientiam in Paradiso a primis parentibus commissam illis imputari.
units.tr: I. That in Adam his posterity did not sin; nor was the disobedience committed by the first parents in Paradise imputed to them.

units.la: Ab HENR. WELSINGIO, De Offic.hom. Christ.sol.E.4.
units.tr: From HENRY WELSING, On the Duties of the Christian Man, sol. E.4.

units.la: Homines morti obnoxij sunt, non quidem quia inobedientia ista Adami illis imputetur: quid enim iniquius, nisi illi similiter inobedientes fuerint?
units.tr: Men are subject to death, not indeed because that disobedience of Adam is imputed to them: for what could be more unjust, unless they had likewise been disobedient?

units.la: Ibidem. Reatum mortis per propagationem ipsam, sine ullâ ipsius peccati imputatione, ab Adamo traximus, ut in conditionibus servilibus & vectigalibus evenire solet.
units.tr: Ibidem. We have derived the guilt of death from Adam through propagation itself, without any imputation of that sin itself, as usually happens in servile and tributary conditions.

units.la: Ab ADOL. VENATORE, Declar. pag. 172. Non pos-sum credere; Deum voluisse Adamum & Evam collocare tanquam stirpem totius generis humani: neque posteros eorum omnes, etiam illos, qui post aliquot seculorum myriades ab ipsis essent nascituri, in æternum reos esse mali illius, quod duo isti homines perpetrarunt, ac propter idipsum obnoxios esse igni infernali, ac si ipsi in Paradiso fuissent & peccatum hoc perpetrassent. Contr. Pastor. Dordr. pag. 106. Nos in Adamo non peccasse, ex eo colligi poterit; quod nemo in se deprehendat conscientiæ suæ accusationem, quod ante quinquies mille & quingentos annos in Paradiso hoc Adami peccatum perpetraverit. Ego saltem non deprehendi.
units.tr: From ADOLF VENATOR, Declaration, p. 172. I cannot believe that God willed to place Adam and Eve as the stock of the whole human race, nor that all their posterity, even those who would be born from them after some myriads of centuries, are guilty forever of that evil which those two men committed, and on account of that very thing are liable to hellfire, as if they themselves had been in Paradise and committed this sin. Against the Pastors of Dort, p. 106. That we did not sin in Adam may be gathered from this: that no one finds in himself an accusation of conscience for having committed this sin of Adam in Paradise five thousand five hundred years ago. At least I have not found it in myself.

units.la: II. Pronitatem ad peccandum, seu corruptionem humanæ naturæ non profluxisse ex Adami inobedientiâ, sed continuatis peccandi actibus attrahi.
units.tr: II. That the proneness to sin, or the corruption of human nature, did not flow from Adam's disobedience, but is drawn in by continued acts of sinning.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. E.3. Tertium errorem ejusdem generis statuimus, quod omninò Evan-gelici docent, hominis ad peccandum pronitatem ex illo primi hominis peccato profectam esse.
units.tr: From WELSING, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. E.3. We set down a third error of the same kind, which the Evangelicals altogether teach: that man's proneness to sin has proceeded from that first sin of man.

units.la: Ibidem. Pronitas ad peccandum, quæ in hominibus conspicitur, non à primo illo peccato, sive ab uno illo primi hominis peccandi actu, statim exorta est, sed continuatis, post peccatum illud, alijs peccandi actibus peccandi habitum paulatim homines attraxerunt, seque ipsi corruperunt, & sic corruptionis istius semina per propagationem ad posteros transmiserunt.
units.tr: Ibidem. The proneness to sin which is seen in men did not arise at once from that first sin, or from that one single act of sinning by the first man, but through continued, after that sin, other acts of sinning, men gradually drew in a habit of sinning, corrupted themselves, and so transmitted the seeds of this corruption to their posterity by propagation.

units.la: A VENATORE, Declar. pag. 172. Non possum credere propter hunc necessarium & à Deo decretum Adami lapsum, omnes homines ab ipsâ conceptione atq; ab utero matris esse maledictioni obnoxios, corpore & anima vitiatos, in intellectu plane occæcatos, & in voluntate necessariò ad malum proclives, adeò ut verum bonum non possint intelligere, & nihil aliud possint quam malum agere. Item. Atq; hi,si Dijs placet,fructus sunt peccati Adami, & peccati originis, quod peccatum produxerit, scilicet, æter-nam impotentiam ad bonum, & inevitabilem mali ope-rationem.
units.tr: From VENATOR, Declaration, p. 172. I cannot believe that, because of this necessary fall of Adam, decreed by God, all men, from conception itself and from the mother's womb, are liable to curse, vitiated in body and soul, plainly blinded in understanding, and necessarily prone to evil in will, so that they cannot understand the true good and can do nothing but evil. Likewise: And these, if it pleases God, are fruits of Adam's sin and of original sin, which sin produced, namely an eternal inability for good and an inevitable working of evil.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.175.Non possum credere, hominem propterea non habere vires,quibus salvus fieri possit,quoniam Adamus se-mel de vetito fructu ante quinquies aut ferè sexies mille an-nos comederit.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 175. I cannot believe that man therefore has no powers by which he can be saved, since Adam once ate of the forbidden fruit some five or nearly six thousand years ago.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.179. Credo nullos parentes dona sufficientia ad salutem pro liberis aut posteris posse amittere.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 179. I believe that no parents can lose the gifts sufficient for salvation for their children or posterity.

units.la: III. Pronitatem hanc ad peccandum non esse vitium, seu peccatum proprie dictum, sed ita metonymice appel-lari,quia sit caussa aut effectus peccati.
units.tr: III. That this proneness to sin is not a vice, or sin properly so called, but is so named only metonymically, because it is a cause or effect of sin.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic.hom. Christ. sol.E.4.Errant Evan-gelici, cum statuunt concupiscentiam esse peccatum, quam-vis ei nullo pacto assentiatur homo, sed statim & semper reprimat.
units.tr: From WELSING, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. E.4. The Evangelicals err when they hold that concupiscence is sin, although man in no way assents to it, but immediately and always represses it.

units.la: A IAC. ARMINIO, Artic. perpend. pag. 18. Perpenden-dum est, an peccatum originis sit tantum carentia justitiæ originalis, & sanctimoniæ primævæ, cum inclinatione ad peccandum, qua & antea in homine fuit.
units.tr: From JAMES ARMINIUS, Articles weighed, p. 18. It must be weighed whether original sin is merely the lack of original righteousness and primeval holiness, together with the inclination to sin which was in man before as well.

units.la: Contra Perkinsf.pag.170. Nullum est peccatum quod simul sit malum culpæ, & malum poenæ, seu poena peccati, & causa alterius peccati, si rectè & rigidè ista considerentur.
units.tr: Against Perkins, p. 170. There is no sin that is at once the evil of guilt and the evil of punishment, or the punishment of sin and the cause of another sin, if these things are considered correctly and strictly.

units.la: A IOAN. ARNOLDO, Contra Gomarum, pag. 4. 5. Arminius sentiebat transgressionem legis & peccatum actuale proprie peccatum appellari, atque interim rotundè agnoscebat, peccatum, quod causa aliorum peccatorum est, etiam peccatum appellari, quia peccatum hoc in nos venit ut poena peccati. Neque intelligere poterat quomodo illud, quod nobis ut poena infligitur, proprie loquendo possit peccatum esse.
units.tr: From JOHN ARNOLD, Against Gomarus, pp. 4, 5. Arminius held that transgression of the law and actual sin are properly called sin, and yet he frankly acknowledged that sin which is the cause of other sins is also called sin, because this sin comes upon us as the punishment of sin. Nor could he understand how that which is inflicted on us as a punishment can properly be sin.

units.la: Contra Tilenum, pag.388. Planè verum est quod Arminius docet loco à te citato, perversè dici peccatum originale reum facere mortis, cum peccatum hoc poena sit actualis peccati Adami: ex quibus verbis sequitur, quod dicis, scilicet Arminium docere, peccatum originis non esse proprie dictum peccatum.
units.tr: Against Tilenus, p. 388. It is quite true what Arminius teaches in the passage you cited, that it is wrongly said that original sin makes one liable to death, since this sin is the punishment of Adam's actual sin. From these words it follows what you say, namely that Arminius teaches that original sin is not properly called sin.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.389. Arminius negat peccatum originis esse peccatum proprie dictum.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 389. Arminius denies that original sin is sin properly so called.

units.la: A VENATORE, Contra Pasl.[?]Dordr. pag.109. Peccatum originis proprie non est peccatum, nec condemnationem meretur.
units.tr: From VENATOR, Against the Pastors of Dort, p. 109. Original sin is not properly sin, nor does it deserve condemnation.

units.la: IV. Infantes non nasci cum vitiositate hereditaria, per quam non sint idonei ad bonum, & proclives ad omne malum: sed nasci cum iisdem viribus ad bonum, cum quibus Adamus creatus fuit.
units.tr: IV. That infants are not born with a hereditary vice, by which they are unfit for good and prone to every evil; but are born with the same powers for good with which Adam was created.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. B. 4. Nunquam verum esse ostendent Evangelici, ac ne in speciem quidem id uspiam in S. literis indicatum fuisse, docere poterunt, humanas vires in vitandis peccatis nullas esse, & propter primi hominis peccatum atque inobedientiam universum humanum genus ipsius voluntatis libertate in bene agendo, DEoque obediendo,privatum esse.
units.tr: From WELSING, On the Duties of the Christian Man, B.4. The Evangelicals will never show that this is true, nor will they be able to teach that it has been indicated anywhere in Holy Scripture, even in appearance: that human powers for avoiding sin are nil, and that on account of the sin and disobedience of the first man the whole human race has been deprived of freedom of the will in doing good and in obeying God.

units.la: Evangelici addiderunt effectum primi peccati esse amissionem liberi arbitrij; qui ingens est error.
units.tr: The Evangelicals added that the effect of the first sin is the loss of free will, which is a huge error.

units.la: Quidquid aliud Theologi vulgo de originali peccato disputant, præter reatum necessariæ perpetuæque mortis, quem per propagationem ipsam sine ullâ ipsius peccati imputatione,ab Adamo traximus, id omne, ut apud ipsosmet incertum omninò ac varium,sic humani ingenij figmentum prorsus censendum est.
units.tr: Whatever else the theologians commonly argue about original sin, apart from the guilt of necessary and perpetual death, which we drew from Adam through propagation itself without any imputation of that sin, all of it, uncertain and varied even among themselves, must be regarded as a figment of human ingenuity.

units.la: Omnes infantes sunt simplices, & stantes in eodem statu, in quo Adam fuit ante lapsum, antequam Eva serpenti auscultassset, qui suadebat illis, ut comederent de vetita arbore scientiæ boni & mali.
units.tr: All infants are innocent, and stand in the same state in which Adam was before the Fall, before Eve listened to the serpent, who urged them to eat from the forbidden tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

units.la: Non possum credere propter hunc necessarium & à DEo decretum lapsum Adami omnes homines ab ipsâ conceptione atq; ab utero matris esse maledictioni obnoxios, corpore & animâ vitiatos, in intellectu plane occæcatos, in voluntate necessariò ad malum proclives,adeò ut verum bonum non possint intelligere, & nihil aliud possint quam malum operari.
units.tr: I cannot believe that, because of this necessary fall of Adam, decreed by God, all men from the very conception and from the mother's womb are liable to the curse, corrupted in body and soul, utterly blinded in understanding, and necessarily inclined to evil in will, so that they cannot understand the true good and can do nothing but evil.

units.la: Non possum credere hominem propterea non habere vires ad salutem sufficientes, quod Adamus semel de vetito fructu, ante quinquies aut penè sexies mille annos comederit; nec etiam hominem cum tali impotentia natum esse.
units.tr: I cannot believe that man lacks sufficient strength for salvation because Adam ate once of the forbidden fruit five or nearly six thousand years ago; nor that man is born with such impotence.

units.la: v. Peccatum originis non esse causam sufficientem ad universi generis humani condemnationem.
units.tr: v. Original sin is not a sufficient cause for the condemnation of the whole human race.

units.la: Perversè dicitur peccatum originale reum mortis facere.
units.tr: It is wrongly said that original sin makes a man liable to death.

units.la: Perpendendum est an peccatum originis homines faciat reos irae DEI.
units.tr: It must be considered whether original sin makes men liable to the wrath of God.

units.la: Subjeci & hoc disquiri pofse, an DEUS propter innatum nobis peccatum originale irasceretur.
units.tr: I have also suggested that this may be inquired into: whether God would be angry because of the original sin inborn in us.

units.la: Ab ADR. BORRIO, Resp. Armin. ad 31. Artic. pag. 117. Necesse est omnes salvos fore, qui actualia peccata nulla ipsi perpetrarunt, quales sunt infantes omnes, sine discri-mine. Quia DEUS universum genus humanum in reconciliationis gratiam assumpsit, & cum Adamo, omnibusq; ejus posteris in eo foedus gratiæ iniyit[?]: quumque infantes foedus illud transgressi non sint, non videntur condemnationi obnoxii. Et cum Deus ipsi Adamo, qui in propria persona peccavit, & voluntate sua libera, peccatum illud condonaverit, nulla est ratio cur Deus hoc peccatum infantibus imputare voluerit. Nam sic Deus videbitur cum infantibus rigidius agere quam cum ipsis Diabolis.
units.tr: From ADRIAN BORRIUS, Arminian Response to the 31 Articles, p. 117. It is necessary that all will be saved who have committed no actual sins, as all infants do, without distinction. For God has taken up the whole human race into the grace of reconciliation, and entered into a covenant of grace with Adam and all his posterity in him; and since infants have not broken that covenant, they do not seem liable to condemnation. And since God pardoned that sin to Adam himself, who sinned in his own person and by his own free will, there is no reason why God should wish to impute this sin to infants. For in that case God would seem to deal more harshly with infants than with the devils themselves.

units.la: A VENATORE, Contr. Pas[?]t. Dordr. pag. 98. Admodum absurdum mihi videtur statuere, quamvis peccatum Adami ante sex millia annorum perpetratum sit, tamen hoc non obstante, innocentes ipsos infantes nondum tres dies natos, imo in matris utero adhuc existentes, in æternum gravissimæ pœnæ infernali obnoxios esse.
units.tr: From VENATOR, Against the Dordrecht Pastor, p. 98. It seems to me utterly absurd to maintain that, although Adam's sin was committed six thousand years ago, nevertheless the innocent infants themselves, not yet three days old, or even still in the mother's womb, are liable to the most grievous punishment of hell for eternity.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.101. Non video quomodo conveniat fini creationis, DEI bonitati, justitiæ, & misericordiæ, & veritati verbi ipsius, ut DEUS creaturam propter parentum peccatum, & propter peccatum alienum, nasci vellet obnoxiam tantæ miseriæ, ut præstaret, imo longè præstaret nunquam fuisse, nunc non esse, nec unquam futurum, quam ita esse: adeo ut igne infernali propter Adami peccatum solum æternum sit punienda.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 101. I do not see how it agrees with the end of creation, with the goodness, justice, and mercy of God, and with the truth of his own word, that God should wish a creature to be born liable to so great a misery because of the sin of its parents and the sin of another, so that it would be better, indeed far better, never to have existed, than now to exist and to exist for ever as it does; so that because of Adam's sin alone it is to be punished eternally with infernal fire.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.112. Innatum peccatum punitur pœna tempora-li, sed actuale insuper etiam æterna. Item. Concessi homines propter peccatum Adami carere donis illis, quod non habeant arborem vitæ, qui in Paradiso erat, & quod ipsis nunc sit moriendum.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 112. Inborn sin is punished with temporal punishment, but actual sin moreover with eternal punishment. Likewise. I grant that men, because of Adam's sin, lack those gifts which they would have had if they had the tree of life that was in Paradise, and that they must now die.

units.la: Declarat.pag.172. Non possum credere omnes homines ab ipsa conceptione atque ab utero matris obnoxios esse maledictioni.
units.tr: Declaration, p. 172. I cannot believe that all men from the very conception and from the mother's womb are liable to the curse.

units.la: A IOAN. WTENBOGARDO, Defens.decr.pag.192. Hanc consequentiam solidè vellem videre refutatam, infantes morientes sine peccatis actualibus (posito hoc, quod verum sit eos in Adamo peccasse) non rigidius à D E o tractari, quàm ipsos diabolos, si tantum propter peccatum originale in Adamo perpetratum condemnarentur. Diaboli enim condemnantur propter actualia sua peccata, isti verò minimè.
units.tr: From JOHANNES WTENBOGAERT, Defence of the Decrees, p. 192. I would like to see this consequence solidly refuted: that infants who die without actual sins (granting that they truly sinned in Adam) are not treated more harshly by God than the devils themselves, if they were condemned only because of the original sin committed in Adam. For the devils are condemned for their own actual sins, but these infants certainly are not.

units.la: A IOAN. ARNOLDO, contra Tilenum,pag.388. Planè verum est, quod Arminius docet loco à te citato, perversè dici peccatum originale reum facere mortis.
units.tr: From JOHANNES ARNOLDUS, against Tilenus, p. 388. It is entirely true, as Arminius teaches in the passage you cite, that it is wrongly said that original sin makes a man liable to death.

units.la: VI. Adamum lapsu suo tantum speculum, exemplum, & antecessorem fuisse lapsuum reliquorum hominum.
units.tr: VI. Adam by his fall was only a mirror, an example, and a forerunner of the falls of the rest of mankind.

units.la: A VENATORE, Declarat. pag.176. Cum D E v s praevideret lapsum hominis, cujus Adamus speculum & quasi typus fuit, aliud foedus erexit.
units.tr: From VENATOR, Declaration, p. 176. When God foresaw the fall of man, of which Adam was a mirror and, as it were, a type, he established another covenant.

units.la: Contr.Past.Dordrac.pag.100. Adamum fuisse speculum & primum peccatorem, atque inde malam consuetudinem & inclinationem ad peccandum fuisse attractam, concedere possem.
units.tr: Against the Dordrecht Pastor, p. 100. I could grant that Adam was a mirror and the first sinner, and that from him an evil custom and an inclination to sin were drawn.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.110. Caeterum an Adamus ideo particeps factus est peccati Evae, quia ab illa post peccatum natus fuerit? Minimè. Illa enim post ipsum creata fuit, imò ex ipsius costâ. Ergo erat exemplum. Eodem etiam modo Adam suis liberis, atque illi iterum suis posteris, exemplum & antecessor ad peccandum fuit. Et quoniam ipse primus fuit, hinc fit ut per ipsum natura sit corrupta. Ibidem. Quod omnes nos in peccatis concipiamur & nascamur, non est quod omnes cum peccato originali nascamur, sed quod illi à quibus nascimur, in plerisque ipsorum operibus, etiam in concipiendo, gignendo, & patiendo, non sint sine peccatis: ut jam non dicamus, nos postea in ipsorum operibus multa mala, & peccatis inquinata exempla videre, quae sint humanae fragilitatis atque infirmitatis testimonia. Item. Videmus enim quam efficacia sint exempla parentum in liberis, praeceptorum in discipulis, & magistratuum in subditis. Et
units.tr: Ibid., p. 110. But was Adam made a partaker of Eve's sin because she was born of him after the sin? By no means. For she was created after him, indeed out of his rib. Therefore he was an example. In the same way Adam was an example and forerunner to his children in sinning, and they again to their posterity. And since he was the first, it follows that nature was corrupted through him. Ibid. That we are all conceived and born in sins does not mean that we are all born with original sin, but that those from whom we are born are not without sins in most of their works, including in conceiving, begetting, and bearing; not to mention that we afterwards see in their works many evil examples stained by sins, which are testimonies of human frailty and weakness. Likewise. For we see how powerful are the examples of parents in children, of teachers in pupils, and of magistrates in subjects.

units.la: Quantum boni potest exemplum bonum, ad mandatorum DEI observationem, tantum mali contra potest exemplum malum ad abstrahendum ab observatione illâ.
units.tr: As much good as a good example can do toward the observance of God's commandments, so much harm, on the contrary, can a bad example do toward drawing people away from that observance.

units.la: ARTICULUS XVI. De Prædestinatione divinâ.
units.tr: ARTICLE XVI. Of Divine Predestination.

units.la: CRedimus DEUM, postquam tota Adami soboles, sic in perditionem & exitium primi hominis culpâ præcipitata fuit, seipsum talem demonstrasse ac præstitisse, qualis est revera: nimirum misericordem & justum. Misericordem quidem eos damnatione & interitu liberando & servando, quos in æterno & immutabili consilio suo, 1. pro mera & gratuitâ suâ bonitate, per IESVM CHRISTVM Dominum nostrum elegit, 2. sine ullo [bonorum] operum ipsorum respectu. 3. Justum vero, alios in illo suo lapsu & perditione relinquendo, in quam sese ipsi præcipites dederunt. 4. [Hac ratione declarat se esse misericordem & clementem DEUM iis quos salvos facit, quibus nihil debebat: uti quoque se declarat justum judicem ostensione justæ severitatis suæ erga reliquos. Atque interim illis nullam facit injuriam. Nam quod nonnullos salvos facit, non propterea fit, quod isti alijs sint meliores, cum omnes in exitium certum prolapsi sint, donec DEUS eos discernat, & liberet secundum aeternum atque immutabile propositum suum, quod in IESU CHRISTO fundatum est, antequam mundus creatus fuit. Nemo itaque secun-dum hanc sententiam ad hanc gloriam per-venire per se ipsum potest, quoniam a nobis ipsis non sumus idonei ad cogitandum ali-quid boni, nisi Deus per gratiam ac meram bonitatem suam nos praeveniat: adeo natu-ra nostra est corrupta.]
units.tr: We believe that God, after the whole posterity of Adam had been thrown headlong into perdition and ruin by the fault of the first man, demonstrated and showed himself to be what he truly is: namely merciful and just. Merciful indeed, in freeing and saving from damnation and destruction those whom he chose in his eternal and unchangeable counsel, (1) out of his mere and free goodness, through Jesus Christ our Lord, (2) without any regard to their [good] works. (3) Just indeed, in leaving the others in that their fall and perdition into which they have cast themselves headlong. (4) [By this method he declares himself a merciful and gracious God to those whom he saves, to whom he owed nothing, just as he also declares himself a just judge by showing his righteous severity toward the rest. And yet he does no wrong to them. For that he saves some is not because they are better than others, since all have fallen into certain ruin, until God distinguishes them and sets them free according to his eternal and unchangeable purpose, which is founded in Jesus Christ before the world was created. Therefore, according to this teaching, no one can attain this glory through himself, since we of ourselves are not competent to think anything good, unless God goes before us by his grace and mere goodness; so corrupt is our nature.]

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this Article the following is taught.

units.la: I. Consilium DEI de salvando hoc homine non esse certum nec immutabile.
units.tr: I. God's counsel concerning the saving of this man is neither certain nor immutable.

units.la: Ab WELSINGIO, De Offic.hom.Christ.Fol.B.2. Lectorem monemus ex ipsis à nobis allatis testimonijs probari, DEUM velle & curare, ut vivant illi ipsi, qui pereunt, ac proinde posse perire eos, atque adeo evenire ut pereant, quos DEUS vult vivere.
units.tr: From Welsingius, On the Duties of a Christian Man, fol. B.2. We warn the reader that it is proved from the testimonies we ourselves have cited that God wills and takes care that those very people who perish should live, and therefore that those who perish may be lost, and so it comes about that those whom God wills to live should perish.

units.la: Ibidem. Ex quibus constat posse perire eos, quos DEUS salu-ti destinaverit.
units.tr: Ibid. From which it is clear that those whom God has destined for salvation may perish.

units.la: Ibidem.sol. B.3. Nihil mirum videri debet, ex electis aliquando reprobos, & vicissim ex reprobis electos effici.
units.tr: Ibid. sol. B.3. Nothing should seem strange, that from the elect some are at times made reprobate, and conversely that from the reprobate, elect.

units.la: A JAC. ARMINIO, Contra Perkinf. pag. 195. DEUS vult serio ut omnes homines salventur, at compulsus pertinaci & incorrigibili malitia nonnullorum, vult illos jacturam face-re salutis, hoc est, condemnari.
units.tr: From Jacobus Arminius, Against Perkins, p. 195. God seriously wills that all men be saved, but, compelled by the stubborn and incorrigible malice of some, he wills them to suffer the loss of salvation, that is, to be condemned.

units.la: A SIM. EPISCOPIO, Disp. de vol. DEI, thes. 21. Ineptum & ridiculum est dicere seriam & veram voluntatem DEI esse ne-quire, nisi effectum sortiatur.
units.tr: From Simon Episcopius, Disputation on the will of God, thesis 21. It is foolish and ridiculous to say that the serious and true will of God cannot be unless it attains its effect.

units.la: II. Per electionis decretum non intelligi propositum DEI, de certis aliquibus hominibus singularibus servandis, sed tantum de certo hominum genere servando, scilicet, fidelium perseverantium.
units.tr: II. By the decree of election is not meant God's purpose concerning certain particular individuals to be saved, but only concerning a certain kind of men to be saved, namely, of believers who persevere.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. B. 3. Decretum Electionis communiter loquendo non ad certos ac definitos homines, nominatim hos vel illos, sed ad certum potius homi-num genus, sive ad homines generatim quidem acceptos, sed qualitate aliqua, hoc est, obedientia vel inobedientia praeditos, omnino referri debet.
units.tr: From Welsingius, On the Duties of a Christian Man, sol. B.3. The decree of election, speaking in general, must be referred altogether not to certain and defined men, by name this or that, but rather to a certain kind of men, or to men taken generally, but endowed with some quality, that is, obedience or disobedience.

units.la: A JAC. ARMINIO, Artic. perpend. pag. 21. Secundum decretum est, quo DEUS statuit resipiscentes & fideles in gratiam recipere, eosque perseverantes salvare in Christo, & per Christum. Illud secundum decretum est praedestinatio ad salutem.
units.tr: From Jacobus Arminius, Examined Article, p. 21. The second decree is that by which God determined to receive the repentant and faithful into grace, and to save those who persevere in Christ and through Christ. That second decree is predestination to salvation.

units.la: A REMONSTRANTIBUS, Col. Hag. pag. 34. Nos aliam praedestinationem ad salutem in Evangelio revelatam non agnoscimus, quam quâ DEUS decrevit, credentes in Filium suum JESUM Christum, & in eadem fide perseverantes, salvos facere.
units.tr: From the Remonstrants, Colloquy at The Hague, p. 34. We do not acknowledge any other predestination to salvation revealed in the Gospel than that by which God decreed to save those who believe in his Son Jesus Christ and persevere in the same faith.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 57. Perseverantes fideles velle salvos facere, totum est decretum Praedestinationis ad salutem.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 57. That God wills to save the faithful who persevere is the whole decree of predestination to salvation.

units.la: A JOAN. ARNOLDO, contra Tilen. pag. 53. Decretum Electionis nihil aliud est, quam decretum, quo DEUS statuit, fideles in Christo justificare & salvare.
units.tr: From Johannes Arnoldi, against Tilenus, p. 53. The decree of election is nothing other than the decree by which God determined to justify and save the faithful in Christ.

units.la: A NIC. GREVINCHOVIO, contra Amef. pag. iii[?]. Uniformia & conformia mihi sunt Electionis & justificationis de-creta.
units.tr: From Nicolaus Grevinchovius, against Amesius, p. iii[?]. The decrees of election and of justification are uniform and conformable to me.

units.la: III. Caussam electionis singularis, seu quare DEUS hunc hominem præ illo ab æterno, saluti destinaverit, non esse merum Dei beneplacitum, seu meram ipsius & gratuitam bonitatem, sed fidem ac perseverantiam hominis, seu totam consummatam fidei obedientiam prævisam. Ac proinde Fidem ac perseverantiam hominis prævisam Electionem singularem præcedere, ut conditionem in eligendis requisitam, quæ DEUM ad eligendum moveat, non autem fructum esse, qui ex electione, tanquam primâ ejusdem causâ, promanet.
units.tr: III. The cause of particular election, or why God from eternity destined this man rather than that one to salvation, is not God's mere good pleasure, or his mere and free goodness, but the foreseen faith and perseverance of the man, that is, the whole completed obedience of faith. And therefore the foreseen faith and perseverance of man precede particular election, as a condition required in those to be chosen, which moves God to elect; they are not a fruit which flows from election as its first cause.

units.la: A IAC. ARMINIO, Declar.pag. 47. Decretum, quod DEUS decrevit, certas quasdam personas salvare, innititur præscientiæ DEI, qua ab æterno scivit, quinam juxta ejuscemodi administrationem mediorum ad conversionem & fidem idoneorum, ex præveniente ipsius gratiâ crediturî [?] erant, & subsequente gratiâ perseveraturi.
units.tr: From Jacobus Arminius, Declaration, p. 47. The decree by which God determined to save certain persons rests on the foreknowledge of God, by which he knew from eternity who, according to such an administration of the means fit for conversion and faith, were going to believe through his prevenient grace, and were going to persevere through his subsequent grace.

units.la: A REMONSTRANTIBVS, Collat.Hag.pag.35. Nos rotundè confitemur fidem in consideratione divinâ, in eligendo ad salutem præcedere : & non ut fructum electionis sequi.
units.tr: From the Remonstrants, Colloquy at The Hague, p. 35. We frankly confess that faith precedes, in the divine consideration, in choosing unto salvation, and does not follow as the fruit of election.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.82. Decretum ejusmodi absolutum, quo DEUS dicitur in eligendo non respexisse ad bonas cujusquam qualita-tes, quas ante prævidit, non potest vel cum naturâ Dei, vel cum Scripturis ipsius consistere.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 82. An absolute decree of this kind, by which God is said in electing not to have regarded any good qualities of anyone, which he foresaw beforehand, cannot stand either with the nature of God or with his Scriptures.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.86. Gratia illa, qua benignus DEUS hominem dignatur, cum verbum ipsi prædicari facit, & eum trahit per Spiritum suum ut credat,non manat ex decreto ipso electio-nis adsalutem. Item, Mittit verbum suum, quo ipsi visum fuerit, non secundum absolutum aliquod decretum, sed propter alias caussas in homine ipso latentes.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 86. That grace by which kind God deigns to favour a man, when he causes the word to be preached to him and draws him by his Spirit so that he believes, does not flow from the decree of election unto salvation itself. Likewise: he sends his word to whom it seems good to him, not according to some absolute decree, but on account of other causes lying hidden in the man himself.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 89. Electio ad salutem, innititur præscientiæ huic, secundum quam DEUS novit, quinam in ipsum crediturî sint, quinam non. Ibidem.pag.93. Quæritur an Fides sit fructus ex Electione ad salutem emanans? Fratres affirmant, Nos negamus.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 89. Election unto salvation rests on this foreknowledge, according to which God knows who will believe in him, and who will not. Ibid. p. 93. The question is whether faith is a fruit flowing from election unto salvation. The brethren affirm; we deny.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.94. Non possumus simpliciter concedere S. Scripturam non ponere aliam causam Electionis, quam Dei propositum & beneplacitum.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 94. We cannot simply concede that Holy Scripture does not posit any other cause of election than God's purpose and good pleasure.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 109. Absurdum est ponere absolutam Dei voluntatem in decreto Electionis pro causa prima, quæ reliquas causas, Christum puta, Fidem, aliasque omnes antecedat.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 109. It is absurd to posit God's absolute will in the decree of election as the first cause, which precedes the other causes, namely Christ, faith, and all the rest.

units.la: A NICOL.GREVINCHOVIO,contra Amef.pag.24. Fides est conditio prærequisita in hoc vel illo eligendo. Item. Naturæ legum ac conditionum præscriptarum omnino conveniens est,ut voluntas iudicis à conditione postulata & præstita moveatur ad præmium.
units.tr: From Nicolaus Grevinchovius, against Amesius, p. 24. Faith is a prerequisite condition in this or that person to be chosen. Likewise: it is altogether in keeping with the nature of laws and prescribed conditions that the will of the judge be moved to reward by the condition demanded and fulfilled.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.104. Thesin istam ex mente nostra sic informo: Fidem esse necessarium prærequisitum à Deo prævisum imo, qui ad vitam æternam eligitur.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 104. I frame this thesis in accordance with my own mind thus: faith is a necessary prerequisite, foreseen by God, of the one who is chosen to eternal life.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.111. Nego fidem esse medium electioni ad gloriam subordinatum. Ratio negationis in promptu est, quod scriptura fidem perpetuò describit ut conditionem requisitam à Deo, cujus præstationem Deus velit prius,quam gloriam aut salutem cuiquam præcise velit aut destinet.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 111. I deny that faith is a means subordinated to election to glory. The reason for the denial is ready to hand: Scripture always describes faith as a condition required by God, whose performance God wills before he precisely wills or destines glory or salvation for anyone.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 137. Electio peremptoria in objecto prærequirit totam consummatam fidei obedientiam.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 137. Peremptory election, in its object, presupposes the whole completed obedience of faith.

units.la: IV. DEVM neminem relinquere in illâ perditione, in quam sese ipsi præcipites dederunt, sed decrevisse omnes homines salvos facere, atque omnibus hominibus sufficientem gratiam ad salutem dare,
units.tr: IV. That God leaves no one in that perdition into which they have thrown themselves headlong, but has decreed to save all men, and to give sufficient grace to all men for salvation,

units.la: Ab ADOL. VENATORE, Declar. pag.175. Credo DEVM ab æterno decrevisse bonitatem suam declarare, atque eum in finem creaturas producere, ac imprimis hominem ad imaginem suam, ut eum beatitudinis suæ participem, atque omnes homines in æternum salvos faciat.
units.tr: From Adolphus Venator, Declaration, p. 175. I believe that God from eternity decreed to declare his goodness, and to that end to produce creatures, and above all man in his own image, so that he might share in his blessedness, and save all men forever.

units.la: A Sim. Episcopio, Disp.priv.9.de Repr.thes.3. DEVS nemini mortalium sufficientem gratiam, cujus beneficio salutem consequi potest, negare absoluta voluntate constituit.
units.tr: From Simon Episcopius, Private Disputation 9 on Reprobation, thesis 3. God, by his absolute will, has determined to deny to no mortal sufficient grace, by whose benefit he can obtain salvation.

units.la: A Ioan. Arnoldo, contra Tilen. pag. 379. DEVS ex voluntate & affectu generali ex æquo omnium hominum salutem desiderat, omnibus Mediatorem dedit, & salutem indiscriminatim ex fide obtinendam ordinat, ideoque omnibus salutem offert, pœnitentiam ac fidem mandat, & ad utramque media administrat.
units.tr: From Johannes Arnoldi, against Tilenus, p. 379. God, by his general will and affection, desires the salvation of all men alike; he has given a Mediator to all, and ordains that salvation be obtained indiscriminately through faith; and therefore he offers salvation to all, commands repentance and faith, and provides means for both.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.121. Hæc est Arminij sententia, quæ huc redit, ut neget DEVM præcisa voluntate aliquos in Adæ lapsu voluisse relinquere, quia scilicet hoc ipsum Scripturis, & constant affectui, quo Deus omnium salutem & conversionem se desiderare testatur, planissimè adversatur.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 121. This is the view of Arminius, which comes to this: he denies that God, by a precise will, wished to leave some in the fall of Adam, because this very thing plainly conflicts with Scripture and with that constant affection by which God testifies that he desires the salvation and conversion of all.

units.la: ARTICULUS XVII. De reparatione generis humani per Filium Dei.
units.tr: ARTICLE XVII. On the restoration of the human race through the Son of God.

units.la: CRedimus etiam DEVM nostrum Opt. Maxim. quum cerneret hominem sese ita in mortis & corporeæ & spiritualis damnationem conjecisse, & prorsus miserum atque maledictum effectum esse, mirabili suâ tum sapientiâ, tum bonitate, adductum, ut illum abs se præ timore fugientem & quæreret, & benignè consolaretur: promisso illi Filisuo, ex muliere nascituro, qui serpentis caput contereret, & illum beatum redde-ret.
units.tr: We also believe that our God, most good and most great, when he saw that man had thrown himself into death, both bodily and spiritual damnation, and had become utterly wretched and accursed, was moved by his wonderful wisdom and goodness both to seek him, as he fled from him in fear, and to comfort him kindly, promising him his Son, who was to be born of a woman, who would crush the serpent's head and make him blessed.

units.la: ARTICULUS XVIII. De Incarnatione Filii DEI.
units.tr: ARTICLE XVIII. On the incarnation of the Son of God.

units.la: Confitemur itaque DEUM promissio-nem Patribus per os sanctorum Prophetarum factam implevisse, quum constituto ab se tempore Filium suum unicum & æternum in hunc mundum misit : qui formam servi assumpsit, similis hominibus factus, & veram naturam humanam cum omnibus ipsius infirmitatibus, excepto peccato, vere assumpsit, dum conceptus est in utero beatæ Virginis Mariæ, virtute Spiritus Sancti, absque ullâ maris operâ. Eam porrò naturam humanam non quoad corpus tantum induit, sed etiam quoad animam : fuit enim vera animâ humanâ præditus, ut verus esset homo. Etenim cum anima non minus quam ipsum
units.tr: We therefore confess that God fulfilled the promise made to the Fathers through the mouth of the holy Prophets, when at the time he had appointed he sent into this world his only and eternal Son, who took the form of a servant, made like unto men, and truly assumed a true human nature with all its infirmities, apart from sin, when he was conceived in the womb of the blessed Virgin Mary by the power of the Holy Spirit, without any work of a man. Moreover, he put on this human nature not only as to the body but also as to the soul; for he was endowed with a true human soul, so that he might be a true man. For since the body itself, no less than the soul, was subject to condemnation, it was necessary that he assume both the one and the other, so as to save both together.

units.la: Sunt inter REMONSTRANTES, qui in controversiam aliquando vocarunt, an per semen mulieris, contriturum caput serpentis, promissum Gen. 3. 15. sit intelligendus DEI Filius ex muliere nasciturus. ipsum corpus damnationi esset obnoxia, ne-cesse fuit illum & hoc & illam assumere, ut utrumque simul servaret. Idcirco contra A-nabaptistarum hæresin, qui negant Chri-stum carnem humanam assumpsisse, confite-mur Christum participem ejusdem carnis & san-guinis fuisse, sicut & pueri : ex lumbis Davidis secundum carnem :factum ex semine Davidis, se-cundum eandem carnem ; fructumque ex utero virginis Mariæ, natum ex muliere : germen Davidis : surculum è radice Jesse : è tribu Juda, atque à Judæis ipsis ortum secundum carnem, & in summâ, verum semen Abrahæ & Davidis, quandoquidem Abrahæ semen assumpsit, & fratribus suis per omnia similis factus est, excepto peccato [genitus ex Mariâ] adeò ut [hac ratio-ne] factus sit revera noster Emmanuel, id est, DEVS nobiscum.{2} cujusdam alterius essentia, quam ipse habeat, consideratione, esse unicum DEI Filium.
units.tr: Some among the REMONSTRANTS have at times raised the question whether the seed of the woman, who was to crush the serpent's head, promised in Gen. 3:15, is to be understood as the Son of God to be born of a woman. Therefore, against the heresy of the Anabaptists, who deny that Christ assumed human flesh, we confess that Christ was a partaker of the same flesh and blood as the children, according to the flesh from the loins of David; made of the seed of David according to the same flesh; the fruit of the womb of the Virgin Mary, born of a woman; the branch of David; the shoot from the root of Jesse; of the tribe of Judah, and descended from the Jews themselves according to the flesh; and in sum, the true seed of Abraham and David, since he took on the seed of Abraham, and was made like his brethren in all things, apart from sin [born of Mary], so that [in this way] he has truly become our Emmanuel, that is, God with us. (Of some other essence which he himself has, by consideration, he is the only Son of God.)

units.la: Concludendum est igitur, Filium Dei u-nigenitum non esse substantiam quandam divinam, ex ipsâ substantiâ DEI genitam, quæ humanam naturam induerit.
units.tr: It must therefore be concluded that the only-begotten Son of God is not some divine substance, begotten from the very substance of God, which put on human nature.

units.la: Inter REMONSTRANTES sunt qui contendant, nomen Emmanuel Christo attribui, non respectu Personæ, quia constet ex duabus naturis, Divina & Humana, sed tantum respectu officij, quia DEVM nobis sit reconciliaturus.
units.tr: Among the REMONSTRANTS there are some who contend that the name Emmanuel is attributed to Christ not with respect to his Person, as if he consisted of two natures, divine and human, but only with respect to his office, because he was to reconcile us to God.

units.la: ARTICULUS XIX. De Unione Hypostatica, seu Personali, duarum Naturarum in Christo.
units.tr: ARTICLE XIX. On the hypostatic or personal union of the two natures in Christ.

units.la: CRedimus etiam per hanc conceptio-nem, Personam Filij conjunctam atque unitam fuisse inseparabiliter cum humanâ naturâ, ita ut non sint duo Filij Dei, nec duæ Personæ, sed duæ Naturæ in unâ eâdemq; personâ unitæ, quarum utraq; proprietates suas retineat, adeo ut sicut Divina natura semper increata & absque initio dierum & sine fine vitæ remansit; cœlumq; & terram implens : sic natura Humana proprietaproprietates suas non amiserit, sed creatura remanserit, initium dierum & finem vitæ habens, finitæ ac circumscriptæ naturæ exi-stens, atque omnia quæ vero corpori competunt, retinens. Et quamvis illi immortalitatem resurrectione suâ dederit, veritatem tamen humanæ naturæ illi neque ademit, neque commutavit. Salus enim & resurrectio nostra à veritate corporis ipsius dependet. Cæterum duæ istæ naturæ ita sunt simul unitæ & conjunctæ in unam personam, ut ne morte quidem ipsius separari potuerint. Quod igitur Patri suo moriendo commendavit, id verè erat spiritus humanus, à corpore ipsius egrediens: at interim Divina natura semper Humanæ, etiam in sepulcro jacenti, conjuncta remansit: i. adeò ut Deitas ipsa non minus in ipsò tunc fuerit, quam cum adhuc infans esset, etsi exiguum ad tempus sese non exereret. Quapropter confite-mur ipsum esse verum DEVM, & verum hominem: 2. Verum quidem DEVM, ut mortem suâ potentiâ vinceret; & verum hominem, ut in carnis suæ infirmitate pro nobis mortem obiret.
units.tr: We believe also that through this conception the Person of the Son was joined and united inseparably with the human nature, so that there are not two Sons of God, nor two Persons, but two Natures united in one and the same person, each of which retains its own properties. Thus, just as the divine nature has always remained uncreated, without beginning of days and without end of life, filling heaven and earth, so the human nature has not lost its properties but has remained a creature, having a beginning of days and an end of life, existing as a finite and circumscribed nature, and retaining all that belongs to a true body. And although he gave it immortality by his resurrection, he neither took away nor changed the truth of the human nature. For our salvation and resurrection depend on the truth of his own body. Moreover, these two natures are so united and joined together into one person that they could not be separated even by his death. What he commended to his Father in dying was truly a human spirit, departing from his body; yet in the meantime the divine nature always remained joined to the human, even while the body lay in the sepulchre; so that the Deity was no less in him then than when he was still an infant, although for a short time it did not show itself. Therefore we confess that he is true God and true man: true God, so that by his power he might conquer death; and true man, so that in the infirmity of his flesh he might die for us.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this article it seems to be taught.

units.la: I. Humana Christi natura cum divina natura unionem ejusmodi esse, qua non necessario requirat unitarum naturarum indistantiam, sed qua tantum consistat in influxu quodam divina virtutis in naturam Christi humanam. Ac proinde non esse personalem.
units.tr: I. That the union of the human nature of Christ with the divine nature is of such a kind that it does not necessarily require an indistance of the united natures, but consists only in a certain influx of divine power into the human nature of Christ. And therefore it is not personal.

units.la: A CONR. VORSTIO, Apol. Exeg. pag. 87. Non inepte re-sponderi posset unionem duarum in Christo naturarum non in essentiali duarum naturarum indistantia, sed in arcano quodam & ineffabili Deitatis τῷ λόγῳ in humanitatem influxu, hoc est, singulari quadam illius in hanc operatione, sive gratiosa hujus ad illam assumptione, aut peculiari appropriatione, revera consistere.
units.tr: From Conrad Vorstius, Apologia Exegetica, p. 87. It could fittingly be answered that the union of the two natures in Christ consists not in an essential indistance of the two natures, but in a secret and ineffable influx of the Deity of the Word [τῷ λόγῳ] into the humanity, that is, in a certain singular operation of it upon this humanity, or a gracious assumption of this by that, or a peculiar appropriation, truly consists.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 88. Non immerito aliquis collegerit etiam divinam τῷ λόγῳ hypostasin per arcanum aliquem influxum assumptæ humanitati communicari potuisse, & hanc perpetuo per illius intimam virtutem adhuc sustentari: etiamsi forte locali aliqua inter utramque substantiam conjunctio non intercedat.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 88. Someone may not unreasonably conclude that the divine hypostasis of the Word [τῷ λόγῳ] could also be communicated to the assumed humanity through a certain secret influx, and that this humanity is still perpetually sustained by its inmost power, even if perhaps no local conjunction intervenes between the two substances does not intervene.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 89. Sive igitur ad illum arcanum personalitatis τῷ λόγῳ influxum aut illapsum, sive ad aliam aliquam singularem Deitatis operationem, per quam humana Christi natura in hypostasi τῷ λόγῳ subsistat, hoc est, ad hypostasin τῷ λόγῳ quasi intime attracta sit, & perpetuo in ea conservetur ac sustentetur; sive ad extraordinariam quandam DEI dispensationem, quā DEVS olim singulariter in Christo homine habitaverit, animo respiciamus; semper æterna Christi divinitas abundè probari poterit.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 89. Whether then we look to that secret influx or inbreathing of the Word [τῷ λόγῳ] upon the personality, or to some other singular operation of the Deity by which the human nature of Christ subsists in the hypostasis of the Word, that is, is drawn intimately as it were into the hypostasis of the Word, and is perpetually preserved and sustained in it; or to some extraordinary dispensation of God by which God once dwelt singularly in Christ the man, let us consider; the eternal divinity of Christ can always be abundantly proved.

units.la: II. Personam Christi non constare ex duabus Naturis, Divina & Humana, sed tantum ex una, scilicet, humana.
units.tr: II. That the person of Christ does not consist of two natures, divine and human, but only of one, namely the human.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. Fol. D. 2. Ex quo etiam liquidò apparet, humanam naturam in Christo esse ipsius Filij DEI personam, cum necesse sit, si Filius DEI sit mortuus, ejus personam esse mortuam, & ita merum somnium id esse, quod à Papistis acceptum, Evangelici affirmant, Filij DEI personam esse revera divinam naturam in Christo, quâ humana sustentetur, quæ ipsa per se in Christo nequaquam sit persona.
units.tr: From Welsingius, De Officio hominis Christiani, fol. D. 2. From this also it clearly appears that the human nature in Christ is the very person of the Son of God, since, if the Son of God died, his person must have died; and so the Evangelicals affirm that what is received from the Papists is a mere dream: that the person of the Son of God is really the divine nature in Christ, by which the human is sustained, which itself in Christ is by no means a person.

units.la: ARTICULUS XX. De modo Redemptionis, per declarationem Iustitiæ & Misericordiæ DEI in CHRISTO.
units.tr: ARTICLE XX. On the manner of redemption, through the declaration of the justice and mercy of God in Christ.

units.la: CRedimus DEUM, qui summè & perfectissimè est tum misericors tum iustus, 1. Filium suum misisse, ut naturam illam assumeret, quæ per inobedientiam peccarat, ut in ea ipsa natura satisfaceret, atque ut Deus de peccato per acerbissimam mortem ac passionem Filij sui iustas pœnas sumeret. Deus igitur iustitiam suam in proprio Filio, in quem peccata nostra conjecerat, ostendit, & exeruit: Bonitatem verò & Misericordiam suam in nos nocentes & condemnatione dignos, benignè effudit & exeruit, dum Filium suum pro nobis, ex perfectissimo suo erga nos amore, morti tradidit, & eum rursus propter justificationem nostram e mortuis excitavit, ut immortalitatem & vitam æternam per illum consequeremur.
units.tr: We believe that God, who is supremely and most perfectly both merciful and just, sent his Son to assume that nature which had sinned through disobedience, so that he might make satisfaction in that very nature, and that God might exact just punishments for sin through the most bitter death and passion of his Son. God therefore showed and exercised his justice in his own Son, on whom he had laid our sins; but he generously poured out and exercised his goodness and mercy toward us who are guilty and worthy of condemnation, when he delivered his Son to death for us out of his most perfect love toward us, and raised him again from the dead for our justification, so that through him we might obtain immortality and eternal life.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this article it seems to be taught.

units.la: I. Justitiam DEI non necessario postulare punitionem peccatorum, sed DEUM posse, illæsa justitia sua, absque ulla satisfactione, peccata prorsus impunita dimittere: ac proinde non esse summè & perfectissimè justum.
units.tr: I. That the justice of God does not necessarily demand the punishment of sins, but that God can, with his justice unimpaired, forgive sins altogether unpunished without any satisfaction; and therefore he is not supremely and most perfectly just.

units.la: A CONR. VORSTIO, Disp. de Deo, pag.396. Non dicitur quòd justitia hæc DEI judicialis condignam pœnam ob quodvis etiam minimum delictum præcisè ac necessariò exigat.
units.tr: From Conrad Vorstius, Disputation on God, p. 396. It is not said that this judicial justice of God requires, precisely and necessarily, a condign punishment for any offence, even the smallest requires.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.397. Si absoluta potestate sua DEUS uti vellet, peccata, si non omnia, saltem plurima sine irrogatione condigna pœna peccantibus condonare posset.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 397. If God wished to use his absolute power, he could forgive sins, if not all, at least very many, to those who sin without the infliction of condign punishment.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.399. Falsum est quod nullum omninò peccatum per justitiam DEI possit impunitum dimitti.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 399. It is false that no sin at all can be forgiven unpunished through the justice of God sin at all can be forgiven unpunished through the justice of God.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.331. DEO non minus licitum est de jure suo remittere, quam jus suum retinere, aut persequi. Item. Justum omninò est apud DEUM tam non punire, quam punire, pro ut ipsi visum fuerit.
units.tr: Parasceue ad Piscatorem, p. 24. It is no less lawful for God to remit his right than to retain or pursue it. Likewise, it is altogether just with God not to punish as well as to punish, as it shall seem good to him.
