units.la: Parasc.ad Piscat.pag.24. Thesis hæc consistere non potest, quâ dicitur, non posse DEUM salva justitia sua ullum vel minimum peccatum impunitum dimittere.
units.tr: Parasceue ad Piscatorem, p. 24. This thesis cannot stand, in which it is said that God cannot, with his justice safe, forgive any sin, even the least, unpunished.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.25. Naturalis justitia in DEO revera non est: sive extra hypothesin decreti, nulla uspiam in DEO esse apparet.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 25. Natural justice in God does not truly exist: outside the hypothesis of the decree, no justice in God appears anywhere.

units.la: Tractat. de Satisfact. pag.36. Quæritur an in DEO sit essentialis aliqua justitia, quæ omnino peccata puniri dicet? ac proinde plenam pro ijs satisfactionem (si quidem ab ijs liberandi simus) exigat? Respondeo nullam esse in DEO ejusmodi justitiam.
units.tr: Tractatus de Satisfactione, p. 36. It is asked whether there is in God some essential justice which says that sins must absolutely be punished, and therefore demands full satisfaction for them (if indeed we are to be freed from them)? I answer that there is no such justice in God.

units.la: Epist. ad N. 10. Mart. 1595. Sic igitur credo: Dominum DEVM pro suprema suâ autoritate posse, si velit, omnia peccata hominibus condonare, nulla pro ijs accepta solutione: hoc est, statuo nullam esse justitiam DEI essentialem, quæ omnino & simpliciter exigat punitionem ob peccata, hoc est, plenam omnium pœnarum solutionem non esse absolute necessariam, quasi pendentem à necessitate divinæ naturæ.
units.tr: Letter to N., 10 March 1595. Thus I believe: that the Lord God, by his supreme authority, can, if he wills, forgive men all sins without any payment received for them; that is, I hold that there is no essential justice of God which absolutely and simply demands punishment for sins, that is, that the full payment of all penalties is not absolutely necessary, as if dependent on the necessity of the divine nature.

units.la: Epist.ad N.& N.15.Mart. 1598. DEVS potest peccata condonare, nulla solutione accepta.
units.tr: Letter to N. and N., 15 March 1598. God can forgive sins, no payment being received.

units.la: Quod DEVS ad omnia & singula peccata puniendum per justitiam suam adigatur, id verò nullo modo credere possumus.
units.tr: That God is bound by his justice to punish all and each sin, that we can by no means believe.

units.la: Parentes certè & reges minimè se obstrictos putant, ut pro omnibus delictis satisfactionem accipiant. Scio quanto perfectior sit DEI justitia, quam hominum: attamen mens humana impressas habet notitias, divinæ naturæ imagines.
units.tr: Parents certainly and kings do not think themselves at all bound to accept satisfaction for all offences. I know how much more perfect the justice of God is than that of men; yet the human mind has impressed notions, images of the divine nature.

units.la: Si punire, scilicet peccata, esset naturale, scilicet Deo (illâ nimirum actione, quæ secum fert necessitatem) non posset actio talis de personâ peccatoris in personam alteram transfire.
units.tr: If to punish sins were natural to God (that is, by that action which necessarily carries with it necessity), such an action could not pass from the person of the sinner into another person.

units.la: Nulla in DEO proprietas est, quæ istam satisfactionem necessariò postulat. Iustitia namque naturalis DEI proprietas non est, utinecque misericordia.
units.tr: There is no property in God which necessarily demands this satisfaction. For natural justice is not a property of God, any more than mercy is.

units.la: ARTICULUS XXI. De Satisfactione Christi pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXI. On the Satisfaction of Christ for our sins.

units.la: CRedimus IESUM CHRISTUM summum illum Sacerdotem esse, in æter-num cum jurejurando constitutum, secundum ordinem Melchisedeci, qui se nostro nomine coram Patre ad placandam ipsius iram cum plena satisfactione obtulit, 1. sistens seipsum super altare crucis, & sanguinem suum pretiosum ad purgationem pec-catorum nostrorum profudit, sicuti id Pro-phetæ futurum prædixerant. Scriptum enim est castigationem pacis nostræ super Filium D E I positam, & livore ejus nos sanatos esse. Item, ipsum tanquam ovem ad mactationem ductum, atq; inter peccatores & iniquos deputatum, condemna-tumq; à Pontio Pilato tanquam maleficum, etsi illum prius innocente pronuntiasset. Quæ igitur non rapuerat, persolvit, & justus pro injustis passus est, idque tum in animâ suâ, tum in corpore: adeo ut sentiens horribilem illam pœnam, quam nos peccatis nostris comme-riti riti eramus, 2. aquam & sanguinem sudave-rit:& tandem etiam exclamaverit, Devs meus, Deus meus,cur deseruisti me?Ea vero omnia pro remissione peccatorum nostrorum pertulit. Quamobrem merito cum divo Paulo dici-mus,nos nihil quidquam scire,nisi Iesvm Chri-stvm,eumque crucifixum: quinetiam omnia pro stercoribus ducimus propter excellentiam cognitio-nis Domini nostri Iesv Christi, ut qui in ejus vulneribus omnis generis consolationem capiamus. Itaq; nihil necesse est ut alias ullas rationes vel optemus, vel ipsi excogitemus, quibus Deo reconciliari possimus, præter hanc solam & semel peractam oblationem, quâ consecrati sunt & perfecti in perpetuum fideles omnes,qui sanctificantur. Atque hæc est causa cur ipse ab Angelo Iesvs vocatus sit, id est,Servator, quod servaturus esset populum suum à peccatis ipsius.
units.tr: We believe that Jesus Christ is that supreme Priest, appointed for ever with an oath, after the order of Melchizedek, who offered himself in our name before the Father, with full satisfaction, to appease his wrath: (1) by presenting himself upon the altar of the cross, and by pouring out his precious blood for the cleansing of our sins, as the Prophets had foretold would happen. For it is written that "the chastisement of our peace was laid upon the Son of God, and by his bruises we are healed," and again that he, "as a sheep led to the slaughter, was numbered among the sinners and the wicked," and was condemned by Pontius Pilate as a malefactor, although Pilate had first declared him innocent. "What he had not taken away, he paid back, and the just suffered for the unjust," and this both in his soul and in his body, so that, feeling that horrible punishment which we had deserved by our sins, (2) he sweated water and blood, and at last cried out, "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" He endured all these things for the remission of our sins. Wherefore we rightly say with the divine Paul that "we know nothing except Jesus Christ, and him crucified," and indeed that "we count all things as dung for the excellence of the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ," so that in his wounds we may receive every kind of consolation. Therefore there is no need that we either wish for, or devise for ourselves, any other means by which we may be reconciled to God, apart from this one and once-accomplished offering, by which all the faithful who are sanctified have been consecrated and made perfect for ever. And this is the reason why he was called Jesus by the Angel, that is, "Saviour, because he would save his people from their sins."

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: It seems to be taught against this article:

units.la: 1. Christum passione suâ pro peccatis nostris non satisfe-cisse justitiæ divinæ.
units.tr: 1. That Christ by his suffering did not satisfy the divine justice for our sins.

units.la: A Welsingio, De Offic. hom. Christ.pag. B. 7. Christi sanguine satisfactum justitiæ divinæ fuisse pro peccatis nostris, nec id usquam extat, & aperte pugnat cum liberali & justâ peccatorum remissione, quam Devs nobis per Iesvm Chri-stum obtulit.
units.tr: From Welsingius, On the Office of the Christian Man, p. B. 7: that the divine justice was satisfied for our sins by the blood of Christ. This is nowhere found, and it openly contradicts the free and just remission of sins which God offers us through Jesus Christ.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Epist.ad N.10.Mart.1595. Credo Dominum DEUM liberè decrevisse peccata non condonare, sed severiter ulcisci in omnibus peccatoribus: atque ita solutionem ab ipsismet exigere: contrà verò pœnitentibus & se ad ipsum convertentibus omnia peccata condonare, non acceptà pro ijs plenà solutione.
units.tr: From VORSTIUS, Letter to N., 10 March 1595. I believe that the Lord God freely decreed not to pardon sins, but to punish severely all sinners, and so to exact payment from them; but on the contrary, to pardon all sins to those who repent and turn to him, without receiving full payment for them.

units.la: Credo IESUM Christum idcirco potissimùm in mundum venìsse, ut nobis peccatoribus hanc liberalitatem non modò annunciaret, & multis modis confirmaret, sed etiam reipsa communicaret: videlicet, quatenus nos à peccatis averteret, & ad DEUM per seipsum converteret.
units.tr: I believe that Jesus Christ came into the world chiefly for this reason, that he might not only announce and confirm in many ways this liberality to us sinners, but also actually bestow it: namely, insofar as he would turn us away from sins and convert us to God through himself.

units.la: Credo IESUM Christum ut illius gratia nos participes efficere posset, oportuisse DEO usque ad mortem obedire, & multa acerba perpeti: quæ omnia rationem meriti habent, & ad nostram salutem sunt ordinata. Unde non immeritò Satisfactionis titulo insigniuntur: quia idipsum efficiunt, quod proprie dicta solutio efficere solet: videlicet liberationem nostri ab omni obligatione seu reatu pœnarum. Aliam Christi Satisfactionem ex sacris literis extrui posse non credo.
units.tr: I believe that Jesus Christ, so that he might make us partakers of his grace, had to obey God even unto death and suffer many bitter things; all of which have the character of merit and are ordained for our salvation. Hence they are not undeservedly honoured with the title of satisfaction, because they accomplish that very thing which a proper payment usually accomplishes: namely, our release from every obligation or guilt of punishment. I do not believe that any other satisfaction of Christ can be built from the sacred writings.

units.la: Tract. de Satisf. confess. pag.13. Si perfectà solutio fuisset absolutè necessaria, non posset DEUS jure à nobis exigere conditiones pœnitentiæ, fidei, &c. ad obtinendam peccatorum remissionem.
units.tr: From the Treatise on Satisfaction, Confession, p. 13: If a complete payment were absolutely necessary, God could not justly require from us the conditions of repentance, faith, etc., for obtaining the remission of sins.

units.la: Ibidem. Fieri non potest, ut ejusmodi absoluta totius debiti nostri solutio consistat cum liberali illà & munificà peccatorum condonatione, quam S. literæ passim DEO tribuunt, etiam cum de Christo ejusque λύτρῳ[?] pro nobis impenso agunt.
units.tr: Ibid.: It cannot be that such an absolute payment of our whole debt stands together with that free and bountiful forgiveness of sins which the holy writings everywhere attribute to God, even when they speak of Christ and of the ransom [λύτρῳ] given for us.

units.la: Catal.error.Sibr.err.66.p.38. Idipsum remitti verè non potest, quod plenâ solutione jam deletum est, & vice versâ, quod verè condonatum est, pro eo plena solutio justè exigi non potest.
units.tr: From the Catalogue of Errors of Sibrandus, error 66, p. 38: That very thing cannot truly be remitted which has already been cancelled by full payment; and conversely, for that which has truly been forgiven, a full payment cannot justly be demanded.

units.la: Ibidem. Plena solutio & vera remissio in eodem debito aut delicto perfectè concurrere non possunt.
units.tr: Ibid.: Full payment and true remission cannot perfectly coexist in the same debt or offence.

units.la: A SLATIO, Epist.ad N.Mart.9.& Iun.30.1608. Quæstio octava est: Num Christus propriè pro nobis satisfecerit? Resp. Id instituamur[?]. 1. Quia nulla in DEO proprietas est, quæ istam satisfactionem necessario postulat. Justitia namque naturalis DEI proprietas non est, uti neque misericordia. 2. Quia pugnant, peccatorum debita cuiquam remittere, & tamen plenariam satisfactionem eorum nomine accipere. 3. Quia foederi, quo DEVS gratiosam peccatorum remissionem promisit, nec non modo reconciliationis adversatur. Legitur namque DEVM in Christo mundum sibi reconciliasse. Qui? Plena satisfactione? minime: sed peccata ipsis non imputando. 4. Quia satisfactio ejusmodi in sacris literis non legitur. 5. Accedit quod Christus DEVM conciliasse non legitur, ut mundo iratum, sed quod mundum Deo reconciliaverit. 6. Adde quod neque conditionem fidei ab ullo postulare, neque ob peccata quemquam punire posset DEVS.
units.tr: From SLATIUS, Letter to N., 9 March and 30 June 1608. The eighth question is: Did Christ properly satisfy for us? Answer: We maintain this for the following reasons. (1) Because there is no property in God that necessarily requires this satisfaction. For natural justice is not a property of God, any more than mercy is. (2) Because it is contradictory to remit the debts of sins to anyone, and yet to receive a full satisfaction on their account. (3) Because it is opposed to the covenant by which God promised gracious remission of sins, and also to the mere fact of reconciliation. For it is read that God reconciled the world to himself in Christ. How? By full satisfaction? By no means, but by not imputing sins to them. (4) Because such a satisfaction is not read in the sacred writings. (5) Moreover, it is not read that Christ reconciled God, as if God were angry with the world, but that he reconciled the world to God. (6) Add that God could neither require faith as a condition of anyone, nor punish anyone for sins.

units.la: II. Christum non esse perpessum eandem illam pœnam, quam nos peccatis nostris eramus commeriti: ac proinde obedientia sua non plene satisfecisse justitiæ divinæ pro nobis secundum Legis rigorem, sed secundum peculiare aliquod pactum a Patre cum ipso initum: Patrem vero hanc Filii obedientiam loco perfectæ satisfactionis per acceptilationem gratiosè æstimare.
units.tr: II. That Christ did not suffer that very same punishment which we had deserved by our sins; and therefore that his obedience did not fully satisfy the divine justice on our behalf according to the strictness of the Law, but according to some peculiar covenant entered into with him by the Father; and that the Father graciously reckons this obedience of the Son, by acceptilation, in place of perfect satisfaction.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Epist. ad N. 10. Mart. 1595. conf. p. 6. Non possum, si maximè velim, mihi persuadere, IESVM Christum omnes pœnas nobis ob peccatum debitas (inter quas excellit mors æ-terna, quam ille minimè sensit) in sua persona verè sensisse, & hac ratione totum debitum nostrum dissol-visse.
units.tr: From VORSTIUS, Letter to N., 10 March 1595; cf. p. 6. I cannot, however much I might wish it, persuade myself that Jesus Christ truly felt in his own person all the punishments owed to us for sin (among which eternal death excels, which he by no means felt), and that in this way he discharged our whole debt.

units.la: Ibidem. DEVS non potest ullam a nobis conditionem, puta fidei, pœnitentiæ, charitatis erga fratres &c. exigere ad obtinendum remissionem peccatorum, si id totum a Christo recepit, quod nos ei debebamus.
units.tr: Ibid.: God cannot require from us any condition, such as faith, repentance, charity towards the brethren, etc., in order to obtain the remission of sins, if he has received from Christ everything that we owed him.

units.la: Tract. de Satisf. confess. pag. 14. Si DEVS id totum a Christo exegit ac recepit, quod nos ipsi debebamus, ita ut nihil amplius exigendum restet, certè nihil de jure suo remisit, nihil sibi debitum condonavit; quod tamen in omni verâ condonatione fieri necesse est.
units.tr: From the Treatise on Satisfaction, Confession, p. 14: If God has required and received from Christ everything that we ourselves owed, so that nothing further remains to be demanded, then certainly he has remitted nothing of his right, and has forgiven himself no debt; yet this must happen in every true remission.

units.la: Orat.Apol.pag.47. Devs etiam in ipsâ Iesv Christi satisfactione ἐπιείκεια [?] quandam, seu rigoris moderationem exercuit, hoc est, aliquid de stricto jure suo concessit, nec praecisè totum id, quod nos ob peccatum meriti eramus, à sponsore nostro Iesv Christo exegit.
units.tr: From the Apology, p. 47: God also, in the very satisfaction of Jesus Christ, exercised a certain clemency [ἐπιείκεια], or moderation of rigour; that is, he conceded something of his strict right, and did not demand from our surety, Jesus Christ, precisely all that we had deserved by sin.

units.la: Catal.err.Sibr.pag.61. Dico Christum satisfecisse per acceptilationem quandam, non per rigidam identitatem.
units.tr: From the Catalogue of Errors of Sibrandus, p. 61: I say that Christ satisfied by a certain acceptilation, not by a rigid identity.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.31. Acceptilatio autem illa quam ego hic agnosco, in eo posita est, quod Devs obedientiam Christi tanquam aequipollentem loco plenissimæ satisfactionis accepta-rit: nec interim praecisè id omne à Christo exegit, quod juxta rigorem iustitiæ à nobis peccatoribus exigere poterat.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 31: That acceptilation, however, which I acknowledge here, consists in this: that God accepted the obedience of Christ as equivalent in place of the most complete satisfaction, and yet did not demand from Christ precisely all that he could have required from us sinners according to the rigour of justice.

units.la: Parasc.ad Pisc.pag.25. Non nego peccata credentium, immò aliquatenus omnium hominum, in Christo sponsore verè punita fuisse: sed ita ut multiplex ἐπιείκεια [?], seu rigidi iuris remissio hic admixta fuerit.
units.tr: From the Parasceue ad Piscatorem, p. 25: I do not deny that the sins of believers, and indeed in some measure the sins of all men, were truly punished in Christ as surety; but in such a way that a manifold clemency [ἐπιείκεια], or remission of strict right, was mixed in here.

units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Artic.perpend.pag.33. Perpendendum est, An iustitiæ Dei non potuerit satisfieri, nisi Legi satisfieret. Item. An idem sit iustitia Dei in Christo satisfactum esse, & Legi per Christum esse satisfactum. Item. An actus obedientiæ à Christo præstitæ, quâ iustificamur, non fuerint ipsi im-positi [?] secundum peculiare mandatum Patris, & peculiare pactum à Patre cum ipso initum, quo illos actus obedientiæ præscripsit & stipulatus est, addita promissione, fore ut æternam redemptionem ijs acquireret, & [illegible, ~3 letters]men videret. quod ista obedientia per scientiam sui, id est, fidem in se iustificaret.
units.tr: From ARMINIUS, Articles Carefully Weighed, p. 33: It must be weighed whether the justice of God could not have been satisfied unless the Law were satisfied. Likewise, whether it is the same thing for the justice of God to be satisfied in Christ and for the Law to be satisfied through Christ. Likewise, whether the acts of obedience performed by Christ, by which we are justified, were not imposed upon him according to a peculiar command of the Father and a peculiar covenant entered into with him by the Father, by which he prescribed and stipulated those acts of obedience, with the added promise that he would acquire eternal redemption for them, and [illegible] see that this obedience, through knowledge of himself, that is, by faith, would justify them.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.34. Perpendendum est, an Electus in Christo poenam luerit, & obedientiam præstiterit reipsa, an vero æstimatione divinâ tantùm. Et, an æstimatio divina quâ luisse & præstitisse æstimatur, sit actus præcedens iustificationem.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 34. We must consider whether the Elect has actually borne the punishment in Christ and rendered obedience in fact, or only in the estimation of God. And whether the divine estimation by which he is reckoned to have suffered and obeyed is an act that precedes justification.

units.la: ARTICULUS XXII. De Fide Iustificante, & de Iustificatione Fidei.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXII. On Justifying Faith, and on the Justification of Faith.

units.la: CRedimus Spiritum Sanctum per veram magni hujus mysterij cognitionem in cordibus nostris veram Fidem accendere, quæ IESUM Christum cum omnibus suis meritis amplectitur 1. eumq; sibi proprium vindicat, 2. nihilque deinceps extra illum quærit. Necesse enim est, aut omnia quæ ad salutem nostram requiruntur in Christo non esse: aut si sint in eo omnia, eum qui fide IESUM Christum possidet, simul etiam perfectam habere salutem. Itaque horrenda est omninò in DEUM blasphemia, asserere Christum minimè sufficere, sed aliis quoque rebus opus esse. Inde enim sequeretur, Christum ex parte tantùm esse Servatorem. Meritò igitur jureque dicimus cum D. Paulo, Nos sola fide justificari, seu Fide, absque operibus Legis. Cæterùm nequaquam intelligimus esse fidem ipsam, proprie loquendo, 3. quae nos justificet, [seu propter fidem nos justificari,] nam illa tantum est velut instrumentum, 4. quo Christum justitiam nostram apprehendimus. Christus igitur ipse nobis imputans omnia sua merita, & tam multa sanctissima opera, quae pro nobis praestitit, est justitia nostra: 5. Fides vero est instrumentum, quo illi in communionem omnium bonorum ipsius copulamur, atque in eadem retinemur. Adeò ut illa omnia postquam nostra facta sunt, nobis plus quam sufficiant ad nostri a peccatis absolutionem.
units.tr: We believe that the Holy Spirit, through a true knowledge of this great mystery, kindles in our hearts a true faith, which embraces Jesus Christ with all his merits, 1. claims him as its own, 2. and thereafter seeks nothing outside him. For either all that is required for our salvation is not in Christ, or, if all is in him, then whoever possesses Jesus Christ by faith at the same time has perfect salvation. Therefore it is utterly horrible blasphemy against God to assert that Christ is not sufficient on his own, but that other things are also needed. For it would follow that Christ is a Saviour only in part. Rightly and justly, then, we say with St Paul that we are justified by faith alone, or by faith, apart from the works of the Law. Yet we by no means understand faith itself, properly speaking, to be what 3. justifies us [or that we are justified on account of faith]; for faith is only, as it were, the instrument 4. by which we lay hold of Christ as our righteousness. Christ himself, therefore, imputing to us all his merits and the many most holy works which he performed for us, is our righteousness; 5. but faith is the instrument by which we are joined to him in the fellowship of all his good things and kept in that fellowship. So that once all these things have become ours, they more than suffice for our absolution from sins.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: It seems to be taught against this article.

units.la: 1. Ad Fidem justificantem non necessario requiri cogni-tionem I E S V Christi: sed posse homines sine eius cogni-tione servari, seu justificari.
units.tr: 1. That knowledge of Jesus Christ is not necessarily required for justifying faith, but that men can be saved, or justified, without knowledge of him.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. F.3. Sextus error est, quo existimant Evangelici, eos qui sub V. T. coram Deo justi fuerint habiti, propterea tales habitos fuisse, & salutis aeternae nobiscum idcirco fore participes, quod sicut nos in Christum jam exhibitum, sic illi in eundem, quem exhibitum iri sperabant, omnino crediderint. Huic erro-ri universa Scriptura repugnat, quippe quae fidei in Christum nullam prorsus mentionem, nisi pro eo tempore, quo exhibitus fuit, usquam faciat,
units.tr: From Welsingius, On the Duties of a Christian Man, fol. F.3. The sixth error is that the Evangelicals think that those who were held righteous before God under the Old Testament were therefore held such and were made partakers of eternal salvation with us, because, just as we believed in Christ already revealed, so they fully believed in the same one, whom they hoped would be revealed. The whole of Scripture contradicts this error, since it nowhere makes any mention of faith in Christ except for the time when he was revealed.

units.la: Ibidem. Causa hujus erroris est quod creditum fuerit, nullam salutarem & justificantem fidem unquam fuisse, nisi fidem in Christum.
units.tr: Ibidem. The cause of this error is the belief that there has never been any saving and justifying faith except faith in Christ.

units.la: Ibidem. Vide autem de fide in Devm, quæ hominem illâ præditum ipsi Deo gratum facit, & ante Christi adventum, sine ullius in ipsum Christum fidei consideratione idipsum verè præstabat, caput xi. ad Hebræos.
units.tr: Ibidem. But see concerning faith in God, which makes the man endowed with it pleasing to God itself, and which before the coming of Christ, without any consideration of faith in Christ himself, truly accomplished this very thing, chapter 11 to the Hebrews.

units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Resp. ad 31. Art. pag. 87. Consideretur descriptio fidei Abrahami ab Apostolo, Rom. 4. prolixè fa-cta, & apparebit in illâ Iesv Christi mentionem non expressè fieri, sed illa implicatione, quam explicare non cuivis faci-le sit.
units.tr: From Arminius, Reply to the 31st Article, p. 87. Let the description of Abraham's faith given by the Apostle at length in Romans 4 be considered, and it will appear that mention of Jesus Christ is not made expressly in it, but only by that implication which is not easy for just anyone to explain.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 113. Conferatur quod dicitur Rom. 4. penè per totum caput de fide Abrahami, & ejus fidei objecto, & monstretur ex eo, quod Abraham in promissis istis, quæ fide apprehendit, Christum viderit.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 113. Let what is said in Romans 4, almost throughout the whole chapter, about the faith of Abraham and its object, be compared, and let it be shown from this that Abraham, in those promises which he grasped by faith, saw Christ.

units.la: A Petro Bertio, Discept. Epist. pag. 73. Apostolus ad Hebræos toto capite undecimo, hoc unum ex professo docet, Fide apprehendente res à sensibus humanis remotas Patres olim justitiæ testimonium reputasse, hoc est, justifi-catos esse. Et pag. 76. Nam de Christo quidem locis ex Epistolâ ad Hebræos allatis diserte nihil.
units.tr: From Peter Bertius, Disputed Epistle, p. 73. The Apostle to the Hebrews, throughout the whole eleventh chapter, teaches this one thing professedly: that the Fathers of old, by faith laying hold of things remote from human senses, were reckoned to bear witness of righteousness, that is, were justified. And p. 76. For concerning Christ, indeed, in the passages from the Epistle to the Hebrews cited there is expressly nothing.

units.la: A VENATORE, Declarat. pag. 183. Propter multas rationes salus alligari non potest historicæ de Iesv morte & passione fidei. Item. Nam si requiratur externa historiæ cognitio, & sine fide de Iesv passione & morte quis Deo gratus esse nequeat: quid fiet miseris Iudæis, quibus eâ de re in omnibus Mosis libris ne ullum quidem verbum diserte ma-nifestatum est?
units.tr: From Venator, Declaration, p. 183. For many reasons salvation cannot be bound to the historical knowledge of faith concerning Jesus' death and passion. Likewise: For if external knowledge of the history is required, and without faith concerning Jesus' passion and death no one can be pleasing to God, what will become of the unhappy Jews, to whom not even one word about this matter is expressly made known in all the books of Moses?

units.la: Ibidem.pag. 184. Nunquam legi pium illum Iobum, pæni-tentes Nineuitas, & pium illum centurionem Cornelium ullam litteralem cognitionem seu fidem historicam habuisse de passione Iesv, ejusque causa, & tamen Deo grati fuerunt.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 184. I have never read that the pious Job, the repentant Ninevites, and the pious centurion Cornelius had any literal knowledge or historical faith concerning the passion of Jesus and its cause, and yet they were pleasing to God.

units.la: Ibidem. Multi Erhnici[?] habuerunt etiam inter ipsos illu-stria testimonia interni, spiritualis, & veri cultus divini.
units.tr: Ibidem. Many Gentiles also had among themselves illustrious testimonies of internal, spiritual, and true divine worship.

units.la: Ibidem.pag. 185. Nemo potest pervenire ad possessionem dientibus dare ijs, in quibus per vim irrefistibilem omnia, quæ Lege præscribuntur, effecta sint, id verò Deus pro jure ac dominio suo facere non potest.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 185. No one can come into possession of ... to give to those who obey, in whom, by irresistible force, all the things prescribed by the Law have been brought about; yet God cannot do this by his own right and dominion.

units.la: Disput.privat. 46. Thes. 11. An circa ipsum effectum & voluntatem etiam versetur actio Spiritus sancti, immediatè ei aliquid imprimendo, non audemus, nec necesse habemus asserere, aut negare. Certum est mentem hac ratione illustratam facilè affectum jam obsequendi studio, imò obsequio aliquantum inclinatum, ulterius impellere, eique aspirare vim & ἐνέργειαν, quâ correptus affectus voluntatem deinde movet ad actiones affectui similes exercendas, ita tamen, ut pro libertate suâ in contrariam semper partem ferri possit.
units.tr: Private disputation 46, Thesis 11. Whether the action of the Holy Spirit is concerned with the effect and the will itself, by impressing something directly on it, we dare not, nor do we need to, assert or deny. It is certain that a mind thus illumined can easily push further an affection already inclined to eagerness to obey, indeed somewhat inclined to obedience, and breathe into it power and energy [ἐνέργειαν], by which the affection, once seized, then moves the will to carry out actions like the affection, yet in such a way that by its freedom it can always be borne to the contrary side.

units.la: Ibidem.corol.1. An ulla actio Spiritus Sancti immediata in voluntatem necessaria sit, ut quis credere possit verbo? Negativam tuebimur.
units.tr: Ibidem, corollary 1. Is any immediate action of the Holy Spirit upon the will necessary, so that someone could believe the word? We will defend the negative.

units.la: Disp.priv. 7.de Prædest. Thes.11. Iniquissimum est ab eo exigere abedientiam, in quo actus ipse obediendi per potentiam efficitur.
units.tr: Private disputation 7, on Predestination, Thesis 11. It is most unjust to demand obedience from one in whom the very act of obeying is effected by power.

units.la: Ibidem.thes.12. Quorsum enim postulatur serió id, quod potenter inseritur, atque inditur anima ejus, à quo postulatur.
units.tr: Ibidem, thesis 12. For why is that seriously demanded which is powerfully implanted and infused into the soul of him from whom it is demanded?

units.la: Ibidem.Disp.8.thes.7. Absurdum est statuere Deum aut efficere per potentiam, aut procurare per sapientiam, ut electi ea faciant, quæ ab ipsis, ut ipsi ea faciant, exigit & postulat.
units.tr: Ibidem, Disputation 8, thesis 7. It is absurd to hold that God either brings about through power, or procures through wisdom, that the elect do those things which he requires and demands from them, that they themselves should do them.

units.la: Ibidem.Disput.9.thes.3. Deus nemini mortalium sufficientem gratiam, cujus beneficio salutem consequi potest, negare absoluta voluntate constituit.
units.tr: Ibidem, Disputation 9, thesis 3. God has determined by absolute will to deny sufficient grace, by whose benefit one can attain salvation, to no mortal.

units.la: ARTICVLVS XV. De Peccato Originali.
units.tr: ARTICLE XV. Of Original Sin.

units.la: CRedimus Adami inobedientiâ 1. peccatum quod vocant Originis in totum genus humanum diffusum esse. 2. Est autem peccatum Originis corruptio totius naturæ, & vitium hæreditarium; 3. quo & ipsi infantes in matris utero polluti sunt: 4. quodque velut noxia quædam radix, genus omne peccatorum in homine producit: estque tam fœdum atque execrabile coram Deo, ut ad universi generis humani condemnationem sufficiat. 5. Neq; verò per Baptismum penitus aboletur aut radicitus evellitur; quandoquidem ex illo tanquam ex infaustâ ac corruptâ scaturigine perpetui rivuli assiduè exoriuntur atque effluunt: quamvis filijs Dei in condemnationem non cedat aut imputetur, sed ex purâ Dei gratiâ & misericordia illis remittatur: non ut huic remissioni confidentes obdormiant, sed ut sensus hujus corruptionis crebriores gemitus in fidelibus excitet, utque eo ardentius optent, ab hoc corpore mortis liberari. Hinc ergo Pelagianorum errorem damnamus, qui hoc peccatum originis nihil aliud esse asserunt, quam imitationem.6.
units.tr: We believe that through the disobedience of Adam the sin called original has spread over the whole human race. Original sin is the corruption of the whole nature and a hereditary vice, by which even infants are polluted in their mother's womb. It is like a harmful root that produces every kind of sin in a man, and it is so foul and detestable before God that it is sufficient for the condemnation of the entire human race. Nor is it wholly abolished or plucked up by the roots through Baptism, since from it, as from an unhappy and corrupt spring, perpetual streams continually well up and flow forth. Yet it is not reckoned or imputed to the children of God for condemnation, but is forgiven them by the pure grace and mercy of God; not so that they may fall asleep trusting in this forgiveness, but so that the awareness of this corruption may stir up more frequent groans in the faithful, and that they may long the more ardently to be freed from this body of death. Hence we condemn the error of the Pelagians, who assert that this original sin is nothing other than imitation.6.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Contrary to this article, the following is taught.

units.la: I. In Adamo posteros ejus non peccasse, neq; inobedientiam in Paradiso a primis parentibus commissam illis imputari.
units.tr: I. That his posterity did not sin in Adam, nor was the disobedience committed by the first parents in Paradise imputed to them.

units.la: Ab HENR. WELSINGIO, De Offic.hom. Christ.sol.E.4. Homines morti obnoxij sunt, non quidem quia inobedientia ista Adami illis imputetur: quid enim iniquius, nisi illi similiter inobedientes fuerint?
units.tr: From HENRICUS WELSINGIUS, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. E.4. Men are liable to death, not indeed because that disobedience of Adam is imputed to them: for what could be more unjust, unless they had been equally disobedient?

units.la: Ibidem. Reatum mortis per propagationem ipsam, sine ulla ipsius peccati imputatione, ab Adamo traximus, ut in conditionibus servilibus & vectigalibus evenire solet.
units.tr: Ibidem. We have drawn the guilt of death from Adam through propagation itself, without any imputation of that sin, as usually happens in servile and tributary conditions.

units.la: Ab ADOL. VENATORE, Declar. pag. 172. Non possum credere; DEVM voluisse Adamum & Evam collocare tanquam stirpem totius generis humani: neque posteros eorum omnes, etiam illos, qui post aliquot seculorum myriades ab ipsis essent nascituri, in aeternum reos esse mali illius, quod duo isti homines perpetrarunt, ac propter idipsum obnoxios esse igni infernali, ac si ipsi in Paradiso fuissent & peccatum hoc perpetrassent. Contr. Pastor. Dordr.pag.106. Nos in Adamo non peccasse, ex eo colligi potest; quod nemo in se deprehendat conscientiae suae accusationem, quod ante quinquies mille & quingentos annos in Paradiso hoc Adami peccatum perpetraverit. Ego saltem non deprehendi.
units.tr: From ADOLPHUS VENATOR, Declar. p. 172. I cannot believe that God intended to appoint Adam and Eve as the stock of the whole human race, nor that all their posterity, including those who would be born after many myriads of centuries, are guilty of that evil which those two men committed, and on account of that very thing are liable to hellfire, as if they themselves had been in Paradise and had committed this sin. Against the Pastors of Dordrecht, p. 106. We did not sin in Adam: this can be gathered from the fact that no one finds in himself any accusation of conscience for having committed this sin of Adam in Paradise five thousand five hundred years ago. At least I have not found it in myself.

units.la: II. Pronitatem ad peccandum, seu corruptionem humana natura non profluxisse ex Adami inobedientia, sed continuatis peccandi actibus attrahi.
units.tr: II. That the proneness to sin, or the corruption of human nature, did not flow from the disobedience of Adam, but is acquired by continued acts of sinning.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. E.3. Tertium errorem ejusdem generis statuimus, quod omninò Evangelici docent, hominis ad peccandum pronitatem ex illo primi hominis peccato profectam esse.
units.tr: From WELSINGIUS, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. E.3. We hold a third error of the same kind, which the Evangelicals altogether teach: that the proneness of man to sin arose from that first sin of the first man.

units.la: Ibidem. Pronitas ad peccandum, quæ in hominibus con-spicitur, non à primo illo peccato, sive ab uno illo primi hominis peccandi actu, statim exorta est, sed continuatis, post peccatum illud, alijs peccandi actibus peccandi habitum paulatim homines attraxerunt, seque ipsi corruperunt, & sic corru-ptionis istius semina per propagationem ad posteros trans-miserunt.
units.tr: Ibidem. The proneness to sin which is seen in men did not arise at once from that first sin, or from that single act of sinning by the first man, but by continued acts of sinning after that sin, men gradually acquired a habit of sinning, corrupted themselves, and so transmitted the seeds of this corruption to their posterity by propagation.

units.la: A VENATORE, Declar. pag. 172. Non possum credere propter hunc necessarium & à DEO decretum Adami lapsum, omnes homines ab ipsâ conceptione atq; ab utero matris esse maledictioni obnoxios, corpore & anima vitiatos, in intellectu plane occæcatos, & in voluntate necessariò ad malum proclives, adeò ut verum bonum non possint intelligere, & nihil aliud possint quam malum agere.
units.tr: From VENATOR, Declar. p. 172. I cannot believe that, because of this necessary fall decreed by God, all men from conception itself and from the mother's womb are liable to damnation, vitiated in body and soul, plainly blinded in understanding, and necessarily prone to evil in will, so that they cannot understand the true good and can do nothing but evil.

units.la: Item. Atq; hi, si Dijs placet, fructus sunt peccati Adami, & peccati originis, quod peccatum produxerit, scilicet, æter-nam impotentiam ad bonum, & inevitabilem mali ope-rationem.
units.tr: Likewise. And these, if it pleases God, are fruits of the sin of Adam, and of the original sin which that sin produced, namely an eternal inability for good and an inevitable working of evil.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.175. Non possum credere, hominem propterea non habere vires, quibus salvus fieri possit, quoniam Adamus se-mel de vetito fructu ante quinquies aut ferè sexies mille annos comederit.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 175. I cannot believe that man therefore lacks the powers by which he might be saved, since Adam once ate of the forbidden fruit some five or nearly six thousand years ago.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.179. Credo nullos parentes dona sufficientia ad salutem pro liberis aut posteris posse amittere.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 179. I believe that no parents can lose for their children or posterity the gifts sufficient for salvation.

units.la: III. Pronitatem hanc ad peccandum non esse vitium, seu peccatum proprie dictum, sed ita metonymice appellari, quia fit causa aut effectus peccati.
units.tr: III. That this proneness to sin is not a vice, or sin properly so called, but is so named metonymically, because it is the cause or effect of sin.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic.hom. Christ. sol. E.4. Errant Evangelici, cum statuunt concupiscentiam esse peccatum, quamvis ei nullo pacto assentiatur homo, sed statim & semper reprimat.
units.tr: From WELSINGIUS, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. E.4. The Evangelicals err when they hold that concupiscence is sin, although the man in no way assents to it, but immediately and always represses it.

units.la: A IAC. ARMINIO, Artic. perpend.pag.18. Perpenden-dum est, an peccatum originis sit tantum carentia justitia originalis, & sanctimoniæ primævæ, cum inclinatione ad peccandum, qua & antea in homine fuit.
units.tr: From JACOBUS ARMINIUS, Articles Weighed, p. 18. It must be weighed whether original sin is only the lack of original righteousness and primeval holiness, together with the inclination to sin which was in man before.

units.la: Contra Perkinf[?].pag.170. Nullum est peccatum quod simul sit malum culpæ, & malum pœnæ, seu pœna peccati, & causa alterius peccati, si rectè & rigidè ista considerentur.
units.tr: Against Perkins, p. 170. There is no sin which is at once an evil of guilt and an evil of punishment, or the punishment of sin and the cause of another sin, if these things are considered rightly and strictly.

units.la: A IOAN. ARNOLDO, Contra Gomarum,pag.4.5. Arminius sentiebat transgressionem legis & peccatum actuale proprie peccatum appellari, atque interim rotundè agnoscebat, peccatum, quod causa aliorum peccatorum est, etiam peccatum appellari, quia peccatum hoc in nos venit ut pœna peccati. Neque intelligere poterat quomodo illud, quod nobis ut pœna infligitur, proprie loquendo possit peccatum esse.
units.tr: From JOHANNES ARNOLDUS, Against Gomarus, p. 45. Arminius held that transgression of the law and actual sin are properly called sin, and yet he frankly acknowledged that the sin which is the cause of other sins is also called sin, because this sin comes upon us as the punishment of sin. Nor could he understand how that which is inflicted on us as a punishment could, properly speaking, be sin.

units.la: Contra Tilenum, pag.388. Planè verum est quod Arminius docet loco à te citato, perversè dici peccatum originale reum facere mortis, cum peccatum hoc pœna sit actualis peccati Adami: ex quibus verbis sequitur, quod dicis, scilicet Arminium docere, peccatum originis non esse proprie dictum peccatum.
units.tr: Against Tilenus, p. 388. It is quite true that Arminius teaches in the passage you cite that it is wrongly said that original sin makes a man liable to death, since this sin is the punishment of the actual sin of Adam. From these words it follows what you say, namely that Arminius teaches that original sin is not properly called sin.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.389. Arminius negat peccatum originis esse peccatum proprie dictum.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 389. Arminius denies that original sin is sin properly so called.

units.la: A VENATORE, Contra Past.[?]Dordr. pag.109. Peccatum originis proprie non est peccatum, nec condemnationem meretur.
units.tr: From VENATOR, Against the Pastors of Dordrecht, p. 109. Original sin is not properly sin, nor does it deserve condemnation.

units.la: IV. Infantes non nasci cum vitiositate hereditaria, per quam non sint idonei ad bonum, & proclives ad omne malum: sed nasci cum iisdem viribus ad bonum, cum quibus Adamus creatus fuit.
units.tr: IV. That infants are not born with a hereditary vitiation, by which they are unfit for good and prone to every evil; but are born with the same powers for good with which Adam was created.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. B.4. Nunquam verum esse ostendent Evangelici, ac ne in speciem quidem id uspiam in S. literis indicatum fuisse, docere poterunt, humanas vires in vitandis peccatis nullas esse, & propter primi hominis peccatum atque inobedientiam universum humanum genus ipsius voluntatis libertate in bene agendo, Deoque obediendo, privatum esse.
units.tr: From WELSINGIUS, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. B.4. The Evangelicals will never show this to be true, nor will they be able to teach that it was ever indicated in Scripture, even in appearance, that human powers for avoiding sin are nil, and that, because of the first man's sin and disobedience, the whole human race is deprived of the freedom of the will in doing good and in obeying God.

units.la: Ibidem.sol. E. 4. Evangelici addiderunt effectum primi peccati esse amissionem liberi arbitrij; qui ingens est error.
units.tr: Ibidem, sol. E.4. The Evangelicals have added that the effect of the first sin is the loss of free will, which is a great error.

units.la: Ibidem. Quidquid aliud Theologi vulgo de originali peccato disputant, praeter reatum necessariae perpetuaeque mortis, quem per propagationem ipsam sine ulla ipsius peccati imputatione, ab Adamo traximus, id omne, ut apud ipsosmet incertum omnino ac varium, sic humani ingenij figmentum prorsus censendum est.
units.tr: Ibidem. Whatever else the theologians commonly dispute about original sin, apart from the guilt of necessary and perpetual death, which we have drawn from Adam through propagation itself without any imputation of that sin, all of it, since it is altogether uncertain and varied even among themselves, must be judged to be a figment of the human mind.

units.la: A VENATORE, Theol. mera & vera pag. 2. Omnes infantes sunt simplices, & stantes in eodem statu, in quo Adam fuit ante lapsum, antequam Eva serpenti auscultasset, qui suadebat illis, ut comederent de veritâ arbore scientiae boni & mali.
units.tr: From VENATOR, Pure and True Theology, p. 2. All infants are simple, and stand in the same state in which Adam was before the fall, before Eve listened to the serpent who urged them to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

units.la: Contra Pastor. Dordr. pag. 172. Non possum credere propter hunc necessarium & a Deo decretum lapsum Adami omnes homines ab ipsâ conceptione atq; ab utero matris esse maledictioni obnoxios, corpore & animâ vitiatos, in intellectu plane occaecatos, in voluntate necessario ad malum proclives, adeo ut verum bonum non possint intelligere, & nihil aliud possint quam malum operari.
units.tr: Against the Pastors of Dordrecht, p. 172. I cannot believe that, because of this necessary fall decreed by God, all men from conception itself and from the mother's womb are liable to damnation, vitiated in body and soul, plainly blinded in understanding, and necessarily prone to evil in will, so that they cannot understand the true good and can do nothing but evil.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 175. Non possum credere hominem propterea non habere vires ad salutem sufficientes, quod Adamus semel de vetito fructu, ante quinquies aut penè sexies mille annos comederit; nec etiam hominem cum tali impotentiâ natum esse.
units.tr: Ibidem, p. 175. I cannot believe that man therefore lacks sufficient powers for salvation, because Adam ate once of the forbidden fruit some five or nearly six thousand years ago; nor that man is born with such impotence.

units.la: V. Peccatum originis non esse causam sufficientem ad universi generis humani condemnationem.
units.tr: V. That original sin is not a sufficient cause for the condemnation of the whole human race.

units.la: AIAC. ARMINIO, Respons. ad 9. quaest. pag. 174. Perverse dicitur peccatum originale reum mortis facere.
units.tr: Of Arminius, Response to the 9th question, p. 174: It is wrongly said that original sin makes a man guilty of death.

units.la: Artic. perpend. pag. 18. Perpendendum est an peccatum originis homines faciat reos irae DEI.
units.tr: Article examined, p. 18: It must be considered whether original sin makes men liable to the wrath of God.

units.la: Respons. ad 31. Artic. pag. 168. Subjeci & hoc disquiri posse, an Devs propter innatum nobis peccatum originale irasceretur.
units.tr: Response to the 31st article, p. 168: I add that it may also be asked whether God would be angry with us on account of the sin of origin that is innate in us.

units.la: Ab Adr. Borrio, Resp. Armin. ad 31. Artic. pag. 117. Necesse est omnes salvos fore, qui actualia peccata nulla ipsi perpetrarunt, quales sunt infantes omnes, sine discrimine. Quia Devs universum genus humanum in reconciliationis gratiam assumpsit, & cum Adamo, omnibusq; ejus posteris in eo foedus gratiae inivit: quumque infantes foedus illud transgressi non sint, non videntur condemnationi obnoxij. Et cum Devs ipsi Adamo, qui in propria persona peccavit, & voluntate sua libera, peccatum illud condonaverit, nulla est ratio cur Devs hoc peccatum infantibus imputare voluerit. Nam sic Devs videbitur cum infantibus rigidius agere quam cum ipsis Diabolis.
units.tr: From Adrian Borrius, Response to Arminius on the 31st article, p. 117: It is necessary that all who have committed no actual sins themselves, as all infants are, be saved without distinction. For God has taken the whole human race into the grace of reconciliation, and made a covenant of grace with Adam and all his posterity in him; and since infants have not broken that covenant, they do not seem liable to condemnation. And since God has pardoned that sin in Adam himself, who sinned in his own person and by his own free will, there is no reason why God should wish to impute this sin to infants. For in that case God would seem to deal more harshly with infants than with the devils themselves.

units.la: A Venatore, Contr. Past.[?] Dordr. pag. 98. Admodum absurdum mihi videtur statuere, quamvis peccatum Adami ante sex millia annorum perpetratum sit, tamen hoc non obstante, innocentes ipsos infantes nondum tres dies natos, imo in matris utero adhuc existentes, in aeternum gravissimae poena infernali obnoxios esse.
units.tr: From Venator, Against the Pastors of Dort, p. 98: It seems to me altogether absurd to hold that, although Adam's sin was committed six thousand years ago, nevertheless, notwithstanding this, innocent infants not yet three days old, indeed still existing in the mother's womb, are liable to the most severe punishment of hell for ever.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 101. Non video quomodo conveniat fini creationis, Dei bonitati, justitiae, & misericordiae, & veritati verbi ipsius, ut Devs creaturam propter parentum peccatum, & propter peccatum alienum, nasci vellet obnoxiam tantae miseriae, ut praestaret, imo longe praestaret nunquam fuisse, nunc non esse, nec unquam futurum, quam ita esse: adeo ut igne infernali propter Adami peccatum solum aeternum sit punienda.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 101: I do not see how it agrees with the purpose of creation, with God's goodness, justice, mercy, and with the truth of his own Word, that God should will to have a creature born, on account of the sin of its parents and another's sin, subject to such great misery that it would be better, indeed far better, never to have existed, than to exist as it does now and to be destined to exist for ever; so that, on account of Adam's sin alone, one would be punished with eternal infernal fire.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 112. Innatum peccatum punitur poena temporali, sed actuale insuper etiam aeterna. Item. Concessi homines propter peccatum Adami carere donis illis, quod non habeant arborem vitae, qui in Paradiso erat, & quod ipsis nunc sit moriendum.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 112: Innate sin is punished with temporal punishment, but actual sin additionally with eternal punishment. Likewise: I concede that men, on account of Adam's sin, lack those gifts which they would have had if they had the tree of life that was in Paradise, and that they must now die.

units.la: Declarat. pag. 172. Non possum credere omnes homines ab ipsa conceptione atque ab utero matris obnoxios esse maledictioni.
units.tr: Declaration, p. 172: I cannot believe that all men are liable to the curse from the very moment of conception and from the mother's womb.

units.la: A Ioan. WTENBOGARDO, Defens.decr.pag.192. Hanc consequentiam solidè vellem videre refutatam, infantes morientes sine peccatis actualibus (posito hoc, quod verum sit eos in Adamo peccasse) non rigidius à Deo tractari, quàm ipsos diabolos, si tantum propter peccatum originale in Adamo perpetratum condemnarentur. Diaboli enim condemnantur propter actualia sua peccata, isti verò minimè.
units.tr: From John Wtenbogaert, Defence of the Decree, p. 192: I would like to see this consequence solidly refuted: that infants who die without actual sins (granting that it is true that they sinned in Adam) are not treated more harshly by God than the devils themselves, if they were condemned only on account of the original sin committed in Adam. For the devils are condemned on account of their own actual sins, but these infants certainly are not.

units.la: A Ioan. ARNOLDO, contra Tilenum, pag.388. Planè verum est, quod Arminius docet loco à te citato, perversè dici peccatum originale reum facere mortis.
units.tr: From John Arnold, against Tilenus, p. 388: It is entirely true, as Arminius teaches in the passage you cite, that it is wrongly said that original sin makes men guilty of death.

units.la: VI. Adamum lapsu suo tantum speculum, exemplum, & antecessorem fuisse lapsuum reliquorum hominum.
units.tr: VI. That Adam by his fall was only a mirror, example, and forerunner of the falls of the rest of mankind.

units.la: A VENATORE, Declarat. pag.176. Cum Devs praevide-ret lapsum hominis, cujus Adamus speculum & quasi typus fuit, aliud fœdus erexit.
units.tr: Of Venator, Declaration, p. 176: When God foresaw the fall of man, of which Adam was a mirror and, as it were, a type, he set up another covenant.

units.la: Contr.Pasl.Dordrac.pag.100. Adamum fuisse speculum & primum peccatorem, atque inde malam consuetudinem & inclinationem ad peccandum fuisse attractam, concedere possem.
units.tr: Against the Pastors of Dort, p. 100: I could concede that Adam was a mirror and the first sinner, and that from this an evil custom and inclination to sin was drawn.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.110. Cæterum an Adamus ideo particeps factus est peccati Evæ, quia ab illa post peccatum natus fuerit? Minimè. Illa enim post ipsum creata fuit, imò ex ipsius costâ. Ergo erat exemplum. Eodem etiam modo Adam suis liberis, atque illi iterum suis posteris, exemplum & antecessor ad peccandum fuit. Et quoniam ipse primus fuit, hinc fit ut per ipsum natura sit corrupta. Ibidem. Quod omnes nos in peccatis concipiamur & nascamur, non est quod omnes cū peccato originali nascamur, sed quod illi à quibus nascimur, in plerisque ipsorum operibus, etiam in concipiendo, gignendo, & patiendo, non sint sine peccatis: ut jam non dicamus, nos postea in ipsorum operibus multa mala, & peccatis inquinata exempla videre, quæ sint humanæ fragilitatis atque infirmitatis testimonia. Item. Videmus enim quam efficacia sint exempla parentum in liberis, præceptorum in discipulis, & magistratuum in subditis. Et
units.tr: Ibid., p. 110: But was Adam made a partaker of Eve's sin because he was born of her after the sin? Not at all. For she was created after him, indeed from his rib. Therefore she was an example. In the same way Adam was an example and forerunner of sinning to his children, and they again to their posterity. And since he was the first, it follows that through him nature has been corrupted. Ibid.: That we are all conceived and born in sins does not mean that we are all born with original sin, but that those from whom we are born are not without sins in most of their works, including in conceiving, begetting, and bearing; not to mention that we afterwards see in their works many evil examples, stained with sins, which are testimonies of human frailty and weakness. Likewise: For we see how effective the examples of parents are upon their children, of teachers upon their pupils, and of magistrates upon their subjects. And

units.la: Quantum boni potest exemplum bonum, ad mandatorum DEI observationem, tantum mali contra potest exemplum malum ad abstrahendum ab observatione illâ.
units.tr: As much good as a good example can do towards the observance of God's commandments, so much harm can a bad example do, on the contrary, to draw people away from that observance.

units.la: ARTICULUS XVI. De Prædestinatione divinâ.
units.tr: ARTICLE XVI. Of Divine Predestination.

units.la: CRedimus DEUM, postquam tota A-dami soboles, sic in perditionem & exitium primi hominis culpâ praecipitata fuit, seipsum talem demonstrasse ac praestitisse, qualis est revera: nimirum misericordem & justum. Misericordem quidem eos damna-tione & interitu liberando & servando, quos in æterno & immutabili consilio suo, 1. pro merâ & gratuitâ suâ bonitate, per IESUM CHRISTUM Dominum nostrum elegit, 2. sine ullo [bonorum] operum ipsorum respectu. 3. Justum verò, alios in illo suo lapsu & perditione relinquendo, in quam sese ipsi præcipites dederunt. 4. [Hac ratione declarat se esse misericordem & clementem DEUM ijs quos salvos facit, quibus nihil debebat: uti quoque se declarat justum judicem ostensione justæ severitatis suæ erga reliquos. Atque interim illis nullam facit injuriam. Nam quod nonnullos salvos facit, non propterea fit, quod isti alijs sint meliores, cum omnes in exitium certum prolapsi sint, donec DEVS eos discernat, & liberet secundum æternum atque immutabile propositum suum, quod in IESV CHRISTO fundatum est, antequam mundus creatus fuit. Nemo itaque secundum hanc sententiam ad hanc gloriam pervenire per se ipsum potest, quoniam a nobis ipsis non sumus idonei ad cogitandum aliquid boni, nisi DEVS per gratiam ac meram bonitatem suam nos præveniat: adeo natura nostra est corrupta.]
units.tr: We believe that God, after the whole offspring of Adam had been so plunged into perdition and ruin by the fault of the first man, showed and presented himself as he truly is, namely merciful and just. Merciful, indeed, in freeing and saving from damnation and destruction those whom in his eternal and unchangeable counsel he chose, 1. out of his mere and free goodness, through Jesus Christ our Lord, 2. without any regard to their own works. 3. Just, however, in leaving the others in that fall and perdition into which they have thrown themselves headlong. 4. [By this means he declares himself a merciful and gracious God toward those whom he saves, to whom he owed nothing; just as he also declares himself a just judge by showing his righteous severity toward the rest. And meanwhile he does them no injustice. For the fact that he saves some is not because they are better than the others, since all have fallen into certain destruction, until God discerns them and frees them according to his eternal and unchangeable purpose, which is founded in Jesus Christ before the world was created. No one, therefore, according to this teaching can attain this glory through himself, since we of ourselves are not sufficient to think anything good, unless God forestall us by his grace and mere goodness: so corrupt is our nature.]

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this Article the following seems to be taught.

units.la: I. Consilium DEI de salvando hoc homine non esse certum nec immutabile.
units.tr: I. The counsel of God concerning the saving of this man is neither certain nor unchangeable.

units.la: Ab WELSINGIO, De Offic.hom.Christ.Fol.B.2. Lectorem monemus ex ipsis à nobis allatis testimonijs probari, DEVM velle & curare, ut vivant illi ipsi, qui pereunt, ac proinde posse perire eos, atque adeo evenire ut pereant, quos DEVS vult vivere.
units.tr: From Welsingius, On the Duties of the Christian Man, fol. B.2. We remind the reader that from the testimonies we ourselves have cited it is proved that God wills and takes care that they live who perish, and therefore that they can perish, and so it can come about that those whom God wills to live perish.

units.la: Ibidem. Ex quibus constat posse perire eos,quos DEVS salu-ti destinaverit.
units.tr: Ibid. From these it is clear that those whom God has destined for salvation can perish.

units.la: Ibidem.sol. B.3. Nihil mirum videri debet, ex electis aliquan-do reprobos, & vicissim ex reprobis electos effici.
units.tr: Ibid., fol. B.3. Nothing should seem surprising, that some of the elect are at times made reprobate, and conversely that the reprobate are made elect.

units.la: Deus vult seriò ut omnes homines salventur, at compulsus pertinaci & incorrigibili malitiâ nonnullorum, vult illos jacturam facere salutis, hoc est, condemnari.
units.tr: God seriously wills that all men be saved, but, compelled by the stubborn and incorrigible malice of some, he wills them to suffer the loss of salvation, that is, to be condemned.

units.la: A SIM. EPISCOPIO, Disp. de vol. DEI, thes. 21. Ineptum & ridiculum est dicere seriam & veram voluntatem DEI esse nequire, nisi effectum sortiatur.
units.tr: From Simon Episcopius, Disputation on the Will of God, thesis 21. It is foolish and ridiculous to say that the serious and true will of God cannot be unless it obtains its effect.

units.la: II. Per electionis decretum non intelligi propositum DEI, de certis aliquibus hominibus singulariter servan-dis, sed tantum de certo hominum genere servando, scili-cet, fidelium perseverantium.
units.tr: II. That by the decree of election is not meant God's purpose to save certain particular men individually, but only to save a certain kind of men, namely believers who persevere.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. B. 3. Decretum Electionis communiter loquendo non ad certos ac definitos homines, nominatim hos vel illos, sed ad certum potius hominum genus, sive ad homines generatim quidem acceptos, sed qualitate aliquâ, hoc est, obedientiâ vel inobedientiâ praeditos, omninò referri debet.
units.tr: From Welsingius, On the Duties of the Christian Man, fol. B.3. The decree of election, speaking in general, must be referred altogether not to certain and defined men, named this or that, but rather to a certain kind of men, or to men taken generally, yet endowed with some quality, that is, obedience or disobedience.

units.la: A IAC. ARMINIO, Artic.perpend.pag.21. Secundum decretum est, quo DEUS statuit respicientes & fideles in gratiam recipere, eosque perseverantes salvare in Christo, & per Christum. Illud secundum decretum est praedestinatio ad salutem.
units.tr: From Jacobus Arminius, Articles Carefully Weighed, p. 21. There is a second decree, by which God determined to receive those who repent and believe into grace, and to save those who persevere in Christ and through Christ. That second decree is predestination to salvation.

units.la: A REMONSTRANTIBVS, Col.Hag.pag.34. Nos aliam praedestinationem ad salutem in Evangelio revelatam non agnoscimus, quam quâ DEVS decrevit, credentes in Filium suum IESVM Christum, & in eâdem fide perseverantes, salvos facere.
units.tr: From the Remonstrants, Collatio Hagiensis, p. 34. We do not acknowledge any other predestination to salvation revealed in the Gospel than that by which God decreed to save those who believe in his Son Jesus Christ and persevere in the same faith.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 57. Perseverantes fideles velle salvos facere, totum est decretum Praedestinationis ad salutem.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 57. To will to save believers who persevere: this is the whole decree of predestination to salvation.

units.la: A IOAN. ARNOLDO, contra Tilen. pag. 53. Decretum Electionis nihil aliud est, quam decretum, quo DEVS statuit, fideles in Christo iustificare & salvare.
units.tr: From John Arnold, against Tilenus, p. 53. The decree of election is nothing other than the decree by which God determined to justify and save believers in Christ.

units.la: A NIC. GREVINCHOVIO, contra Amef.pag.111[?]. Unifor-mia & conformia mihi sunt Electionis & justificationis decreta.
units.tr: From Nicolaus Grevinchovius, against Amesius, p. 111[?]. The decrees of election and of justification are uniform and conformable to me.

units.la: III. Causam electionis singularis, seu quare DEVS hunc hominem præ illo ab æterno, saluti destinaverit, non esse merum Dei beneplacitum, seu meram ipsius & gratuitam bonitatem, sed fidem ac perseverantiam hominis, seu totam consummatam fidei obedientiam prævisam. Ac pro-inde Fidem ac perseverantiam hominis prævisam Electionem singularem præcedere, ut conditionem in eligendis requisitam, quæ DEVM ad eligendum moveat, non autem fructum esse, qui ex electione, tanquam prima ejusdem causâ, promanet.
units.tr: III. That the cause of a particular election, or why God from eternity destined this man rather than that one for salvation, is not God's mere good pleasure, or his own mere and free goodness, but the foreseen faith and perseverance of the man, that is, his whole completed obedience of faith. And therefore the foreseen faith and perseverance of man precede particular election, as a condition required in those to be elected, which moves God to elect, and not the fruit that flows from election as its first cause.

units.la: A Iac. Arminio, Declar.pag. 47. Decretum, quo DEVS decrevit, certas quasdam personas salvare, innititur præscientiæ DEI, quâ ab æterno scivit, quinam juxta ejusmodi administrationem mediorum ad conversionem & fidem idoneorum, ex præveniente ipsius gratiâ crediturî erant, & subsequente gratiâ perseveraturi.
units.tr: From Jacobus Arminius, Declaration, p. 47. The decree by which God determined to save certain persons rests upon the foreknowledge of God, by which he knew from eternity who, according to such an administration of means suited to conversion and faith, would believe from his prevenient grace, and who would persevere through subsequent grace.

units.la: A REMONSTRANTIBVS, Collat.Hag.pag.35. Nos rotundè confitemur fidem in consideratione divinâ, in eligendo ad salutem præcedere: & non ut fructum electionis sequi.
units.tr: From the Remonstrants, Collatio Hagiensis, p. 35. We frankly confess that faith, in the divine consideration, precedes in the choice to salvation, and does not follow as the fruit of election.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.82. Decretum ejusmodi absolutum, quo DEVS dicitur in eligendo non respexisse ad bonas cujusquam qualitates, quas antè prævidit, non potest vel cum naturâ Dei, vel cum Scripturis ipsius consistere.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 82. An absolute decree of this kind, by which God is said in electing not to have regarded any good qualities of anyone, which he foresaw beforehand, cannot stand either with the nature of God or with his Scriptures.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.86. Gratia illa, qua benignus DEVS hominem dignatur, cum verbum ipsi prædicari facit, & eum trahit per Spiritum suum ut credat, non manat ex decreto isto electionis ad salutem. Item, Mittit verbum suum, quo ipsi visum fuerit, non secundum absolutum aliquod decretum, sed propter alias causas in homine ipso latentes.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 86. That grace by which the kindly God deigns to a man, when he causes the word to be preached to him and draws him by his Spirit so that he believes, does not flow from that decree of election to salvation. Likewise: He sends his word as it seems good to him, not according to some absolute decree, but for other causes lying hidden in the man himself.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 89. Electio ad salutem, innititur præscientiæ huic, secundum quam DEVS novit, quinam in ipsum crediturî sint, quinam non.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 89. Election to salvation rests upon this foreknowledge, according to which God knows who will believe in him and who will not.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.93. Quæritur an Fides sit fructus ex Electione ad salutem emanans? Fratres affirmant, Nos negamus.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 93. It is asked whether faith is a fruit flowing from election to salvation? The brethren affirm; we deny.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.94. Non possumus simpliciter concedere S. Scripturam non ponere aliam causam Electionis, quam Dei propositum & bene placitum.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 94. We cannot simply concede that Holy Scripture does not posit another cause of election than the purpose and good pleasure of God.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 109. Absurdum est ponere absolutam Dei voluntatem in decreto Electionis pro causa prima, quæ reliquas causas, Christum puta, Fidem, aliasque omnes antecedat.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 109. It is absurd to place the absolute will of God in the decree of election as the first cause, which precedes all the other causes, Christ, faith, and all the rest.

units.la: A NICOL.GREVINCHOVIO, contra Amef.pag.24. Fides est conditio prærequisita in hoc vel illo eligendo. Item. Naturæ legum ac conditionum præscriptarum omnino conveniens est, ut voluntas iudicis à conditione postulata & præstita moveatur ad præmium.
units.tr: From Nicolaus Grevinchovius, against Amesius, p. 24. Faith is a prerequisite condition in this or that person to be elected. Likewise: It is entirely consonant with the nature of laws and of prescribed conditions that the will of the judge be moved to reward by the condition demanded and performed.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.104. Thesin istam ex mente nostra sic informo: Fidem esse necessarium prærequisitum à Deo prævisum in eo,[?] qui ad vitam æternam eligitur.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 104. I frame this thesis according to my mind thus: faith is a necessary prerequisite foreseen by God in him [?] who is elected to eternal life.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.111. Nego fidem esse medium electionis ad gloriam subordinatum. Ratio negationis in promptu est , quod scriptura fidem perpetuò describit ut conditionem requisitam à Deo, cujus præstationem Deus velit prius,quam gloriam aut salutem cuiquam præcisè velit aut destinet.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 111. I deny that faith is a means of election to glory subordinate to it. The reason for the denial is ready: Scripture always describes faith as a condition required by God, whose performance God wills before he precisely wills or destines glory or salvation for anyone.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 137. Electio peremptoria in objecto prærequirit totam consummatam fidei obedientiam.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 137. Peremptory election, with respect to its object, presupposes the whole completed obedience of faith.

units.la: IV. DEVM neminem relinquere in illà perditione, in quam sese ipsi præcipites dederunt, sed decrevisse omnes homines salvos facere, atque omnibus hominibus sufficientem gratiam ad salutem dare,
units.tr: IV. That God leaves no one in that perdition into which they have thrown themselves headlong, but has decreed to save all men, and gives sufficient grace to all men for salvation.

units.la: Ab ADOL. VENATORE, Declar.pag.175. Credo DEVM ab æterno decrevisse bonitatem suam declarare, atque eum in finem creaturas producere, ac imprimis hominem ad imaginem suam, ut eum beatitudinis suæ participem, atque omnes homines in æternum salvos faciat.
units.tr: From Adolphus Venator, Declaration, p. 175. I believe that God from eternity decreed to declare his goodness, and to this end produced creatures, and above all man in his own image, so that he might make him a partaker of his blessedness, and save all men for ever.

units.la: A SIM.EPISCOPIO, Disp.priv.9.de Repr.thes.3. DEUS nemini mortalium sufficientem gratiam, cujus beneficio salutem consequi potest, negare absoluta voluntate constituit.
units.tr: From Simon Episcopius, Private Disputation 9, on Reprobation, thesis 3. God has determined by an absolute will to deny to no mortal sufficient grace, by whose benefit he can attain salvation.

units.la: A IOAN. ARNOLDO, contra Tilen.pag.379. DEUS ex voluntate & affectu generali ex æquo omnium hominum salutem desiderat, omnibus Mediatorem dedit, & salutem indiscriminatim ex fide obtinendam ordinat, ideoque omnibus salutem offert, pœnitentiam ac fidem mandat, & ad utramque media administrat.
units.tr: From John Arnold, against Tilenus, p. 379. God, by a general will and affection, equally desires the salvation of all men, has given a Mediator to all, and ordains salvation to be obtained without distinction through faith; therefore he offers salvation to all, commands repentance and faith, and supplies means for both.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.121. Hæc est Arminij sententia, quæ huc redit, ut neget DEUM præcisa voluntate aliquos in Adæ lapsu voluisse relinquere, quia scilicet hoc ipsum Scripturis, & constant affectui, quo DEUS omnium salutem & conversionem se desiderare testatur, planissimè adversatur.
units.tr: Ibidem, pag. 121. This is Arminius's view, which comes down to this: he denies that God, by a bare act of will, decided to leave some in the fall of Adam, because this plainly contradicts Scripture and that constant affection by which God declares that he desires the salvation and conversion of all.

units.la: ARTICULUS XVII. De reparatione generis humani per Filium DEI.
units.tr: ARTICLE XVII. On the restoration of the human race through the Son of God.

units.la: Credimus etiam DEUM nostrum Opt. Maxim. quum cerneret hominem sese ita in mortis & corporeæ & spiritualis damnationem conjecisse, & prorsus miserum atque maledictum effectum esse, mirabili suâ tum sapientiâ, tum bonitate, adductum, ut illum abs se præ timore fugientem & quæreret, & benignè consolaretur: promisso illi Fi-liosuo, ex muliere nascituro, qui serpentis caput contereret, & illum beatum redde-ret.
units.tr: We also believe that our most good and great God, when he saw that man had thrown himself into death, both bodily and spiritual damnation, and had become utterly wretched and accursed, was moved by his wonderful wisdom and goodness both to seek him, as he fled from him in fear, and to comfort him kindly, by promising him his Son, who would be born of a woman, would crush the head of the serpent, and would make him blessed.

units.la: Sunt inter Remonstrantes, qui in controversiam aliquando vocarunt, an per semen mulieris, contriturum caput serpentis, promissum Gen. 3. 15. sit intelligendus DEI Filius ex muliere nasciturus.
units.tr: Some among the Remonstrants have at times raised the question whether the seed of the woman, promised in Gen. 3. 15 as the one who would crush the serpent's head, is to be understood as the Son of God to be born of a woman.

units.la: ARTICULUS XVIII. De Incarnatione Filij Dei.
units.tr: ARTICLE XVIII. On the Incarnation of the Son of God.

units.la: Confitemur itaque DEUM promissionem Patribus per os sanctorum Prophetarum factam implevisse, quum constituto ab se tempore Filium suum unicum & æternum in hunc mundum misit : qui formam servi assumpsit, similis hominibus factus, & veram naturam humanam cum omnibus ipsius infirmitatibus, excepto peccato, verè assumpsit, dum conceptus est in utero beatæ Virginis Mariæ, virtute Spiritus Sancti, absque ullâ maris operâ. Eam porrò naturam humanam non quoad corpus tantum induit, sed etiam quoad animam : fuit enim vera anima humanâ præditus, ut verus esset homo. Etenim cum anima non minus quam ipsum corpus damnationi esset obnoxia, ne-cesse fuit illum & hoc & illam assumere, ut utrumque simul servaret. Idcirco contra Anabaptistarum haeresin, qui negant Christum carnem humanam assumpsisse, confitemur Christum participem ejusdem carnis & sanguinis fuisse, sicut & pueri: ex lumbis Davidis secundum carnem: factum ex semine Davidis, secundum eandem carnem; fructumque ex utero virginis Mariæ, natum ex muliere: germen Davidis: surculum e radice Jesse: e tribu Juda, atque a Judæis ipsis ortum secundum carnem, & in summa, verum semen Abrahæ & Davidis, quandoquidem Abrahæ semen assumpsit, & fratribus suis per omnia similis factus est, excepto peccato [genitus ex Mariâ] adeo ut [hac ratione] factus sit revera noster Emmanuel, id est, Deus nobiscum.{2}
units.tr: We confess, therefore, that God has fulfilled the promise made to the Fathers through the mouth of his holy Prophets, when, at the time he had appointed, he sent into this world his only and eternal Son, who took the form of a servant, made like unto men, and truly assumed a true human nature with all its infirmities, apart from sin, since he was conceived in the womb of the blessed Virgin Mary, by the power of the Holy Spirit, without any work of a man. Moreover, he put on that human nature not only as to the body but also as to the soul: for he was endowed with a true human soul, so that he might be a true man. For since the soul was no less liable to damnation than the body itself, it was necessary for him to assume both this and that, so that he might save both together. Therefore, against the heresy of the Anabaptists, who deny that Christ assumed human flesh, we confess that Christ was a partaker of the same flesh and blood as the children: born of the loins of David according to the flesh: made of the seed of David according to the same flesh; and the fruit of the womb of the virgin Mary, born of a woman: the Branch of David: a shoot from the root of Jesse: of the tribe of Judah, and descended from the Jews themselves according to the flesh, and in sum, the true seed of Abraham and David, since he took on the seed of Abraham, and was made like his brethren in all things, apart from sin [born of Mary], so that [in this way] he was truly our Emmanuel, that is, God with us.{2}

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this Article the following seems to be taught:

units.la: 1. Non fuisse Filium aliquem DEI æternum, seu substantiam quandam divinam ex ipsâ substantiâ DEI genitam, quæ humanam naturam induerit.
units.tr: 1. That there was no eternal Son of God, or some divine substance begotten of the very substance of God, which put on human nature.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De offic. hom. Christ. sol. D.1. Ex quo sequitur, hominem illum IESVM Nazarenum sine ullâ divinâ cujusdam alterius essentia, quam ipse habeat, consideratione, esse unicum Dei Filium.
units.tr: From WELSINGIUS, On the office of the Christian man, solution of D.1. From this it follows that that man Jesus of Nazareth, without any consideration of some other divine essence which he himself might have, is the only Son of God.

units.la: Ibidem. sol. D. 2. Concludendum est igitur, Filium Dei unigenitum non esse subsistantiam quandam divinam, ex ipsâ substantiâ Dei genitam, quæ humanam naturam induerit.
units.tr: Ibidem, solution of D.2. It must therefore be concluded that the only-begotten Son of God is not some divine subsistence, begotten of the very substance of God, which put on human nature.

units.la: Inter Remonstrantes sunt qui contendant, nomen Emmanuel Christo attribui, non respectu Personæ, quia constet ex duabus naturis, Divinâ & Humanâ, sed tantum respectu officij, quia Deum nobis sit reconciliaturus.
units.tr: Among the Remonstrants there are some who maintain that the name Emmanuel is given to Christ not with respect to his Person, since it consists of two natures, divine and human, but only with respect to his office, because he is to reconcile us to God.

units.la: ARTICVLVS XIX.
units.tr: ARTICLE XIX.

units.la: De Vnione Hypostaticâ, seu Personali, duarum Naturarum in Christo.
units.tr: On the Hypostatic, or Personal, Union of the Two Natures in Christ.

units.la: Credimus etiam per hanc conceptionem, Personam Filij conjunctam atque unitam fuisse inseparabiliter cum humanâ naturâ, ita ut non sint duo Filij Dei, nec duæ Personæ, sed duæ Naturæ in unâ eâdemq; personâ unitæ, quarum utraq; proprietates suas retineat, adeo ut sicut Divina natura semper increata & absque initio dierum & sine fine vitæ remansit; cœlumq; & terram implens : sic natura Humana proprietaproprietates suas non amiserit, sed creatura remanserit, initium dierum & finem vitae habens, finitae ac circumscriptae naturae existens, atque omnia quae vero corpori competunt, retinens. Et quamvis illi immortalitatem resurrectione suâ dederit, veritatem tamen humanae naturae illi neque ademit, neque commutavit. Salus enim & resurrectio nostra à veritate corporis ipsius dependet.
