Caeterum duae istae naturae ita sunt simul unitae & conjunctae in unam personam, ut ne morte quidem ipsius separari potuerint. Quod igitur Patri suo moriendo commendavit, id verè erat spiritus humanus, à corpore ipsius egrediens: at interim Divina natura semper Humanae, etiam in sepulcro jacenti, conjuncta remansit: 1. adeo ut Deitas ipsa non minus in ipso tunc fuerit, quam cum adhuc infans esset, etsi exiguum ad tempus sese non exercret. Quapropter confitemur ipsum esse verum D E V M, & verum hominem: 2. Verum quidem DEVM, ut mortem suâ potentiâ vinceret; & verum hominem, ut in carnis suae infirmitate pro nobis mortem obiret.
units.tr: We believe also that, through this conception, the Person of the Son was joined and united inseparably with the human nature, so that there are not two Sons of God, nor two Persons, but two Natures united in one and the same person, each of which retains its own properties. Thus, just as the divine nature has always remained uncreated, without beginning of days or end of life, filling heaven and earth, so the human nature has not lost its own properties but has remained a creature, having a beginning of days and an end of life, existing as a finite and circumscribed nature, and retaining all that truly belongs to a body. And although he gave immortality to it by his resurrection, he neither took away nor changed the truth of the human nature. For our salvation and resurrection depend upon the truth of his very body. Moreover, these two natures are so united and joined together into one person that they could not be separated even by his death. That which he commended to his Father in dying was truly the human spirit, departing from his body; yet in the meantime the divine nature remained always joined to the human, even while the body lay in the sepulchre: (1) so that the Deity itself was no less in him then than when he was still an infant, although for a short time it did not put itself forth. Wherefore we confess him to be true GOD and true man: (2) true God, so that by his power he might overcome death; and true man, so that in the weakness of his flesh he might undergo death for us.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this Article, the following is taught.

units.la: I. Humana Christi natura cum divina natura unionem ejusmodi esse, qua non necessario requirat unitarum naturarum indistantiam, sed qua tantum consistat in influxu quodam divina virtutis in naturam Christi humanam. Ac proinde non esse personalem.
units.tr: I. The union of the human nature of Christ with the divine nature is of such a kind that it does not necessarily require the non-distance of the united natures, but consists only in a certain influx of divine power into the human nature of Christ. And therefore it is not personal.

units.la: A CONR. VORSTIO, Apol,Exeg.pag.87. Non inepte respondéri posset unionem duarum in Christo naturarum non in essentiali duarum naturarum indistantia, sed in arcano quodam & ineffabili Deitatis τῷ[?] λόγῳ in humanitatem influxu, hoc est, singulari quadam illius in hanc operatione, sive gratiosa hujus ad illam assumptione, aut peculiari appropriatione, revera consistere.
units.tr: From CONRAD VORSTIUS, Apology, Exegetical, p. 87. It could not unsuitably be answered that the union of the two natures in Christ does not consist in an essential non-distance of the two natures, but truly in a certain secret and ineffable influx of the Deity of the Word into the humanity, that is, in a certain singular operation of the one upon the other, or in a gracious assumption of the latter by the former, or a peculiar appropriation.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 88. Non immerito aliquis collegerit etiam divinam τῷ λόγῳ hypostasin per arcanum aliquem influxum assumptae humanitati communicari potuisse, & hanc perpetuo per illius intimam virtutem adhuc sustentari: etiam-si forte localis aliqua inter utramque substantiam conjunctio non intercedat.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 88. Someone might not unreasonably conclude that the divine hypostasis of the Word could have been communicated to the assumed humanity by some secret influx, and that it is still sustained continually by its inner power, even if perhaps no local conjunction lies between the two substances.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 89. Sive igitur ad illum arcanum personalita-tis τῷ λόγῳ influxum aut illapsum, sive ad aliam aliquam singularem Deitatis operationem, per quam humana Christi natura in hypostasi τῷ λόγῳ subsistat, hoc est, ad hypo-stasin τῷ λόγῳ quasi intime attracta sit, & perpetuo in ea conservetur ac sustentetur; sive ad extraordinariam quandam DEI dispensationem, qua DEUS olim singulariter in Christo homine habitaverit, animo respiciamus; semper aeterna Christi divinitas abunde probari poterit.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 89. Whether, therefore, we look to that secret influx or inflowing of the Person of the Word, or to some other singular operation of the Deity, by which the human nature of Christ subsists in the hypostasis of the Word, that is, is as it were inwardly drawn into the hypostasis of the Word and continually preserved and sustained in it; or whether we look to a certain extraordinary dispensation of God, by which God once dwelt singularly in Christ the man: in every case the eternal divinity of Christ can be abundantly proved.

units.la: II. Personam Christi non constare ex duabus Naturis, Divina & Humana, sed tantum ex una, scilicet, hu-mana.
units.tr: II. The Person of Christ does not consist of two natures, divine and human, but only of one, namely, the human.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. Fol. D. 2. Ex quo etiam liquidò apparet,humanam naturam in Christo esse ipsius Filij DEI personam,cum necesse sit, si Filius DEI sit mortuus, ejus personam esse mortuam, & ita merum somnium id esse, quod à Papistis acceptum, Evangelici affirmant, Filij DEI personam esse revera divinam naturam in Christo, quâ humana sustentetur, quæ ipsa per se in Christo nequaquam sit persona.
units.tr: From WELSINGIUS, On the Office of the Christian Man, fol. D. 2. From this it also clearly appears that the human nature in Christ is the very Person of the Son of God, since, if the Son of God has died, his person must have died; and so the Evangelicals affirm that what the Papists have received is mere dream: that the Person of the Son of God is in truth the divine nature in Christ, by which the human is sustained, which in itself is by no means a person in Christ.

units.la: ARTICULUS XX. De modo Redemptionis, per declarationem Iustitiæ & Misericordiæ DEI in CHRISTO.
units.tr: ARTICLE XX. On the manner of Redemption, through the declaration of the Justice and Mercy of God in CHRIST.

units.la: Credimus DEUM, qui summè & perse-ctissimè est tum misericors tum justus, 1. Filium suum misisse, ut naturam illam as-sumeret, quæ per inobedientiam peccarat, ut in ea ipsa natura satisfaceret, atque ut Deus de peccato per acerbissimam mortem ac passionem Filij sui justas pœnas sumeret. Deus igitur justitiam suam in proprio Filio, in quem peccata nostra conjecerat, ostendit, & exeruit: Bonitatem vero & Misericordiam suam in nos nocentes & condemnatione di-gnos, benignè effudit & exeruit, dum Filium suum pro nobis, ex perfectissimo suo erga nos amore, morti tradidit, & eum rursus propter justificationem nostram e mortuis excitavit, ut immortalitatem & vitam æternam per illum consequeremur.
units.tr: We believe that God, who is supremely and most perfectly both merciful and just, (1) sent his Son to assume that nature which had sinned through disobedience, so that he might make satisfaction in that very nature, and so that God might exact just penalties for sin through the most bitter death and passion of his Son. God therefore displayed and exhibited his justice in his own Son, upon whom he had laid our sins; and he generously poured out and exhibited his goodness and mercy toward us, who were guilty and worthy of condemnation, when out of his most perfect love toward us he delivered his Son to death for us, and raised him again from the dead for our justification, so that through him we might obtain immortality and eternal life.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this article the following seems to be taught.

units.la: 1. Justitiam DEI non necessario postulare punitionem peccatorum, sed DEVM posse, illæsa justitia sua, absque ulla satisfactione, peccata prorsus impunita dimittere: ac proinde non esse summe & perfectissime justum.
units.tr: 1. That the justice of God does not necessarily demand the punishment of sins, but that God can, with his justice unimpaired and without any satisfaction, forgive sins altogether unpunished; and therefore that he is not supremely and most perfectly just.

units.la: A CONR. VORSTIO, Disp. de Deo, pag.396. Non dicitur quòd justitia hæc DEI judicialis condignam pœnam ob quodvis etiam minimum delictum præcisè ac necessariò exigat.
units.tr: From CONRAD VORSTIUS, Disputation on God, p. 396. It is not said that this judicial justice of God requires a deserved punishment precisely and necessarily for any offence, even the smallest exigat.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.397.Si absoluta potestate sua DEVS uti vellet, peccata, si non omnia, saltem plurima sine irrogatione condigna pœna peccantibus condonare posset.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 397. If God wished to use his absolute power, he could pardon sins, if not all, at least very many, without inflicting a deserved punishment on sinners.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.399.Falsum est quod nullum omninò peccatum per justitiam DEI possit impunitum dimitti.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 399. It is false that no sin whatever can be forgiven unpunished by the justice of God.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.331. DEO non minus licitum est de jure suo remittere, quam jus suum retinere, aut persequi. Item. Justum omninò est apud DEVM tam non punire, quam punire, pro ut ipsi visum fuerit.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 331. It is no less lawful for God to remit his right than to retain or pursue it. Likewise. It is altogether just with God not to punish as much as to punish, as it shall seem good to him.

units.la: Parasc.ad Piscat.pag.24. Thesis hæc consistere non potest, quâ dicitur, non posse DEVM salvâ justitiâ suâ ullum vel minimum peccatum impunitum dimittere.
units.tr: Paraeus against Piscator, p. 24. This thesis cannot stand, which says that God cannot, with his justice intact, forgive any sin, even the smallest, unpunished.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.25. Naturalis justitia in DEO revera non est: sive extra hypothesin decreti, nulla uspiam in DEO esse apparet.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 25. Natural justice in God is in truth not there: outside the hypothesis of the decree, no justice in God appears anywhere.

units.la: Tractat.de Satisfact.pag.36. Quæritur an in DEO sit essentialis aliqua iustitia, quæ omnino peccata puniri dictet? ac proinde plenam pro iis satisfactionem (siquidem ab iis liberandi simus) exigat? Respondeo nullam esse in DEO eiusmodi iustitiam.
units.tr: Treatise on Satisfaction, p. 36. It is asked whether there is in God some essential justice which dictates that sins must wholly be punished, and so demands full satisfaction for them (since we are to be freed from them)? I answer that there is no such justice in God.

units.la: Epist. ad N. 10. Mart. 1595. Sic igitur credo: Dominum DEVM pro suprema sua autoritate posse, si velit, omnia peccata hominibus condonare, nulla pro iis accepta solutione: hoc est, statuo nullam esse iustitiam DEI essentialem, quæ omnino & simpliciter exigat punitionem ob peccata, hoc est, plenam omnium pœnarum solutionem non esse absolute necessariam, quasi pendentem a necessitate divinæ naturæ.
units.tr: Letter to N., 10 March 1595. Thus I believe: that the Lord God, by his supreme authority, can, if he wishes, forgive men all sins with no payment accepted for them: that is, I hold that there is no essential justice of God which altogether and simply demands punishment for sins, that is, that full payment of all penalties is not absolutely necessary, as though depending on the necessity of the divine nature.

units.la: Epist.ad N.&N.15.Mart. 1598. DEVS potest peccata condonare, nulla solutione accepta.
units.tr: Letter to N. and N., 15 March 1598. God can forgive sins with no payment accepted.

units.la: A SIM.EPISCOPO, Disput.de Dom. DEI, thes.13. Quod DEVS ad omnia & singula peccata puniendum per iustitiam suam adigatur, id vero nullo modo credere possumus.
units.tr: From SIMON EPISCOPIUS, Disputation on the Lord's Day of God, thesis 13. That God is compelled by his justice to punish all and each sin, this we can by no means believe.

units.la: A GER. VOSSIO, contra Ravensb.pag.86. Parentes certe & reges minime se obstrictos putant, ut pro omnibus delictis satisfactionem accipiant, Scio quanto perfectior sit DEI iustitia, quam hominum: attamen mens humana impressas habet notitias, divinæ naturæ imagines.
units.tr: From GERARD VOSSIUS, against Ravensberger, p. 86. Parents and kings certainly do not think themselves bound to accept satisfaction for all offences. I know how much more perfect God's justice is than that of men; yet the human mind has impressed notions, images of the divine nature.

units.la: Ibidem. Si punire, scilicet peccata, esset naturale, scilicet DEO (illa nimirum actione, quæ secum fert necessitatem) non possit actio talis de persona peccatoris in personam alteram transfire.
units.tr: Ibid. If to punish sins were natural, that is, to God (by that action which brings necessity with it), such an action could not pass from the person of the sinner into another person.

units.la: A SLATIO, Epist.ad N.1608. Mart.9. & Iun.30. Nulla in DEO proprietas est, quæ istam satisfactionem necessario postulat. Iustitia namque naturalis DEI proprietas non est, utinec-que misericordia.
units.tr: From SLATIUS, Letters of 9 March and 30 June 1608. There is no property in God which necessarily demands that satisfaction. For natural justice is not a property of God, nor is mercy.

units.la: ARTICVLVS XXI. De Satisfactione Christi pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXI. On Christ's Satisfaction for our sins.

units.la: CRedimus IESVM CHRISTVM summum illum Sacerdotem esse, in æternum cum jurejurando constitutum, secundum ordinem Melchisedeci, qui se nostro nomine coram Patre ad placandam ipsius iram cum plena satisfactione obtulit, 1. sistens seipsum super altare crucis, & sanguinem suum pretiosum ad purgationem peccatorum nostrorum profudit, sicuti id Prophetæ futurum prædixerant. Scriptum enim est castigationem pacis nostræ super Filium DEI positam, & livore ejus nos sanatos esse. Item, ipsum tanquam ovem ad mactationem ductum, atque inter peccatores & iniquos deputatum, condemnatumque a Pontio Pilato tanquam maleficum, etsi illum prius innocente pronuntiasset. Quæ igitur non rapuerat, persolvit, & justus pro injustis passus est, idque tum in anima sua, tum in corpore: adeo ut sentiens horribilem illam pœnam, quam nos peccatis nostris commeriti eramus, 2. aquam & sanguinem sudaverit:& tandem etiam exclamaverit, DEVS meus, DEVS meus,cur deseruisti me? Ea vero omnia pro remissione peccatorum nostrorum pertulit. Quamobrem merito cum divo Paulo dicimus,nos nihil quidquam scire,nisi IESVM CHRISTVM,eumque crucifixum: quinetiam omnia pro stercoribus ducimus propter excellentiam cognitionis Domini nostri IESV CHRISTI, ut qui in ejus vulneribus omnis generis consolationem capiamus. Itaq; nihil necesse est ut alias ullas rationes vel optemus, vel ipsi excogitemus, quibus DEO reconciliari possimus, præter hanc solam & semel peractam oblationem, quâ consecrati sunt & perfecti in perpetuum fideles omnes,qui sanctificantur. Atque hæc est causa cur ipse ab Angelo IESVS vocatus sit, id est,Servator, quod servaturus esset populum suum à peccatis ipsius.
units.tr: We believe that JESUS CHRIST is that supreme Priest, appointed for ever with an oath according to the order of Melchizedek, who offered himself in our name before the Father, with full satisfaction, to appease his wrath; (1) presenting himself upon the altar of the cross and shedding his precious blood for the cleansing of our sins, as the prophets had foretold would happen. For it is written: "the chastisement of our peace was laid upon the Son of God, and by his stripes we are healed." Also, that he, like a sheep led to the slaughter, was numbered among sinners and wicked men, and condemned by Pontius Pilate as an evildoer, although Pilate had earlier declared him innocent. "What he had not taken away, he paid, and the just suffered for the unjust"; and this both in his soul and in his body: so that, feeling that horrible punishment which we had deserved by our sins, (2) he sweated water and blood, and at last also cried out: "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" Yet he bore all these things for the remission of our sins. Wherefore we rightly say with the divine Paul: "we know nothing except Jesus Christ, and him crucified"; indeed "we count all things as dung because of the excellence of the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ," so that in his wounds we may take comfort of every kind. Therefore there is no need that we either wish for, or devise for ourselves, any other ways by which we might be reconciled to God, apart from this one and once-accomplished offering, by which all the faithful who are sanctified have been consecrated and made perfect for ever. And this is the reason why he was called Jesus by the Angel, that is, "Saviour, because he would save his people from their sins."

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur:
units.tr: Against this article the following seems to be taught:

units.la: 1. Christum passione sua pro peccatis nostris non satisfecisse justitiæ divinæ.
units.tr: 1. That Christ by his passion did not satisfy divine justice for our sins.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. pag. B. 7. Christi sanguine satisfactum justitiæ divinæ fuisse pro peccatis nostris, nec id usquam extat, & aperte pugnat cum liberali & justa peccatorum remissione, quam DEVS nobis per IESVM Christum obtulit.
units.tr: From WELSINGIUS, On the Duties of a Christian Man, p. B. 7. That divine justice was satisfied for our sins by the blood of Christ is nowhere found, and it openly conflicts with the free and just remission of sins which God offered us through Jesus Christ.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Epist.ad N.10.Mart.1595. Credo Dominum DEUM liberè decrevisse peccata non condonare, sed severiter ulcisci in omnibus peccatoribus: atque ita solutionem ab ipsismet exigere: contrà verò poenitentibus & se ad ipsum convertentibus omnia peccata condonare, non acceptâ pro ijs plenâ solutione. Credo JESUM Christum idcirco potissimum in mundum venisse, ut nobis peccatoribus hanc liberalitatem non modò annunciaret, & multis modis confirmaret, sed etiam reipsa communicaret: videlicet, quatenus nos à peccatis avertit, & ad DEUM per seipsum convertit. Credo JESUM Christum ut illius gratia nos participes efficere posset, oportuisse DEO usque ad mortem obedire, & multa acerba perpeti: quæ omnia rationem meriti habent, & ad nostram salutem sunt ordinata. Unde non immeritò Satisfactionis titulo insigniuntur: quia idipsum efficiunt, quod proprie dicta solutio efficere solet: videlicet liberationem nostri ab omni obligatione seu reatu poenarum. Aliam Christi Satisfactionem ex sacris literis extrui posse non credo.
units.tr: From VORSTIUS, Letter to N., 10 March 1595. I believe that the Lord God has freely decided not to forgive sins but to avenge them severely in all sinners, and so to demand payment from them themselves; but on the contrary, to forgive all sins to the penitent and to those who turn to him, without full payment being accepted for them. I believe that Jesus Christ came into the world chiefly for this reason: that he might not only announce this liberality to us sinners and confirm it in many ways, but also actually impart it: namely, insofar as he turns us away from sins and converts us to God through himself. I believe that Jesus Christ, so that he might make us partakers of his grace, had to obey God even to death, and to endure many bitter things: all of which have the nature of merit and are ordained for our salvation. Whence they are not undeservedly marked with the title of satisfaction: because they accomplish the very thing which a properly so-called payment is wont to accomplish: namely, our liberation from every obligation or guilt of penalties. I do not believe that any other satisfaction of Christ can be built from the sacred letters.

units.la: Tract. de Satisf. confess. pag.13. Si perfecta solutio fuisset absolutè necessaria,non posset Deus jure à nobis exigere conditiones poenitentiæ, fidei, &c. ad obtinendam peccatorum remissionem.
units.tr: Treatise on Satisfaction and Confession, p. 13. If a perfect payment were absolutely necessary, God could not justly demand from us the conditions of repentance, faith, etc., for obtaining the remission of sins.

units.la: Ibidem. Fieri non potest, ut ejusmodi absoluta totius debiti nostri solutio consistat cum liberali illà & munificà peccatorum condonatione, quam S. literæ passim DEO tribuunt, etiam cum de Christo ejusque λύτρῳ pro nobis impenso agunt.
units.tr: Ibid. It cannot be that such an absolute payment of our whole debt should stand together with that free and bountiful forgiveness of sins which the sacred letters everywhere attribute to God, even when they speak of Christ and his ransom [λύτρον] offered for us.

units.la: Catal.error.Sibr.err.66.p.38. Idipsum remitti vere non potest, quod plena solutione jam deletum est, & vice versà, quod verè condonatum est, pro eo plena solutio juste exigi non potest.
units.tr: Catalogue of Sibrand's errors, error 66, p. 38. That which has already been blotted out by full payment cannot truly be remitted, and conversely, what has truly been forgiven, full payment for it cannot justly be demanded.

units.la: Ibidem. Plena solutio & vera remissio in eodem debito aut delicto perfecte concurrere non possunt.
units.tr: Ibid. Full payment and true remission cannot perfectly concur in the same debt or offence.

units.la: A SLATIO, Epist.ad N.Mart.9.& Jun.30.1608. Quæstio octava est: Num Christus proprie pro nobis satisfecerit? Resp. Id infitiamur. 1. Quia nulla in DEO proprietas est, quæ istam satisfactionem necessario postulat. Justitia namque naturalis DEI proprietas non est, uti neque misericordia. 2. Quia pugnant, peccatorum debita cuiquam remittere, & tamen plenariam satisfactionem eorum nomine accipere. 3. Quia foederi, quo DEUS gratiosam peccatorum remissionem promisit, nec non modo reconciliationis adversatur. Legitur namque DEUM in Christo mundum sibi reconciliasse. Qui? Plena satisfactione? minime: sed peccata ipsis non imputando. 4. Quia satisfactio ejusmodi in sacris literis non legitur. 5. Accedit quod Christus DEUM conciliasse non legitur, ut mundo iratum, sed quod mundum DEO reconciliaverit. 6. Adde quod neque conditionem fidei ab ullo postulare, neque ob peccata quemquam punire posset DEUS.
units.tr: From SLATIUS, Letters of 9 March and 30 June 1608. The eighth question is: Did Christ properly satisfy for us? Answer: We deny it. (1) Because there is no property in God which necessarily demands that satisfaction. For natural justice is not a property of God, nor is mercy. (2) Because it is inconsistent to remit the debts of sins to anyone and yet to receive full satisfaction on their account. (3) Because it is contrary to the covenant by which God promised gracious remission of sins, and also to the manner of reconciliation. For it is read that God reconciled the world to himself in Christ. How? By full satisfaction? Not at all: but by not imputing sins to them. (4) Because such satisfaction is not read in the sacred letters. (5) Add that Christ is not read to have reconciled God, as if God were angry with the world, but that he reconciled the world to God. (6) Add that God could neither require faith as a condition from anyone, nor punish anyone for sins.

units.la: II. Christum non esse perpessum eandem illam poenam, quam nos peccatis nostris eramus commeriti: ac proinde obedientiâ suâ non plenè satisfecisse justitiæ divinæ pro nobis secundum Legis rigorem, sed secundum peculiare aliquod pactum à Patre cum ipso initum: Patrem verò hanc Filij obedientiam loco perfectæ satisfactionis per acceptilationem gratiosè æstimare.
units.tr: II. That Christ did not suffer the very punishment that we had deserved by our sins, and so by his obedience he did not fully satisfy divine justice on our behalf according to the strictness of the Law, but according to some special covenant made between the Father and himself; and that the Father graciously accounts this obedience of the Son as perfect satisfaction in place of the debt, by acceptilation.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Epist. ad N. 10. Mart. 1595. conf. p. 6. Non possum, si maximè velim, mihi persuadere, IESVM Christum omnes poenas nobis ob peccatum debitas (inter quas excellit mors aeterna, quam ille minimè sensit) in suâ personâ verè sensisse, & hac ratione totum debitum nostrum dissolvisse.
units.tr: A VORSTIUS, Letter to N., 10 March 1595, see p. 6. However much I might wish to, I cannot persuade myself that Jesus Christ truly felt in his own person all the punishments owed to us for sin (among which eternal death stands out, which he by no means felt), and that in this way he discharged our whole debt.

units.la: Ibidem. DEUS non potest ullam à nobis conditionem, puta fidei, poenitentiæ, charitatis erga fratres &c. exigere ad obtinendum remissionem peccatorum, si id totum à Christo recepit, quod nos ei debebamus.
units.tr: Ibid. God cannot require from us any condition, such as faith, repentance, love towards the brethren, etc., in order to obtain the remission of sins, if he has received from Christ all that we owed him.

units.la: Tract. de Satisf. confess. pag. 14. Si DEUS id totum à Christo exegit ac recepit, quod nos ipsi debebamus, ita ut nihil amplius exigendum restet, certè nihil de jure suo remisit, nihil sibi debitum condonavit; quod tamen in omni verâ condonatione fieri necesse est.
units.tr: Treatise on Satisfaction, Confession, p. 14. If God exacted and received from Christ all that we ourselves owed, so that nothing further remains to be demanded, then surely he has remitted nothing of his right, and has condoned nothing owed to himself; yet this must happen in every true condonation.

units.la: Orat.Apol.pag.47. Deus etiam in ipsâ Iesv Christi satisfactione ἐπιεικείαν[?] quandam, seu rigoris moderationem exercuit, hoc est, aliquid de stricto jure suo concessit, nec praecise totum id, quod nos ob peccatum meriti eramus, à sponsore nostro Iesv Christo exegit.
units.tr: Apology, p. 47. God also, even in the very satisfaction of Jesus Christ, exercised a certain leniency [ἐπιείκεια], or moderation of rigour; that is, he conceded something of his strict right, and did not precisely exact the whole of what we had deserved by sin from our surety, Jesus Christ.

units.la: Catal.err.Sibr.pag.61. Dico Christum satisfecisse per acceptilationem quandam, non per rigidam identitatem.
units.tr: Catalogue of the Errors of Sibrandus, p. 61. I say that Christ satisfied by a certain acceptilation, not by a rigid identity.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.31. Acceptilatio autem illa quam ego hic agnosco, in eo posita est, quod Deus obedientiam Christi tan-quam æquipollentem loco plenissimae satisfactionis accepterit: nec interim praecise id omne à Christo exegit, quod juxta rigorem justitiae a nobis peccatoribus exigere poterat.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 31. The acceptilation which I here acknowledge consists in this: that God accepted the obedience of Christ as equivalent in place of the fullest satisfaction, and yet did not precisely exact all that which, according to the rigour of justice, he could have demanded from us sinners.

units.la: Parasc.ad Pisc.pag.25. Non nego peccata credentium, immò aliquatenus omnium hominum, in Christo sponsore verè punita fuisse: sed ita ut multiplex ἐπιείκεια, seu rigidi iuris remissio hic admixta fuerit.
units.tr: Paraschema to Piscator, p. 25. I do not deny that the sins of believers, and indeed to some extent the sins of all men, were truly punished in Christ the surety; but with a manifold leniency [ἐπιείκεια], or remission of strict right, mixed in.

units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Artic.perpend.pag.33. Perpendendum est, An justitiae Dei non potuerit satisfieri, nisi Legi satisfieret. Item. An idem sit iustitia Dei in Christo satisfactum esse, & Legi per Christum esse satisfactum. Item. An actus obedientiae à Christo praestitae, quâ justificamur, non fuerint ipsi[?] im-positi secundum peculiare mandatum Patris, & peculiare pactum à Patre cum ipso initum, quo illos actus obedientiae praescripsit & stipulatus est, addità promissione, fore ut æternam redemptionem ijs acquirorent,[?] &[?] tamen videret, quod istâ obedientiâ per scientiam sui, id est, fidem in se justificaret.
units.tr: From ARMINIUS, Articles Considered, p. 33. It must be considered whether the justice of God could not have been satisfied unless the Law were satisfied. Likewise, whether it is the same thing for the justice of God to be satisfied in Christ and for the Law to be satisfied through Christ. Likewise, whether the acts of obedience performed by Christ, by which we are justified, were not laid upon him according to a special command of the Father and a special covenant made between the Father and himself, by which he prescribed and stipulated those acts of obedience, with the added promise that they would win eternal redemption for them; and yet he saw that by this obedience, through the knowledge of himself, that is, faith in him, he would justify them.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.34. Perpendendum est, an Electus in Christo pœnam luerit, & obedientiam praestiterit reipsa, an vero æstimatione divinâ tantùm. Et, an æstimatio divina quâ luisse & praestitisse æstimatur, sit actus praecedens justificatio-nem.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 34. It must be considered whether the Elect has paid the penalty in Christ and rendered obedience in reality, or only by divine estimation. And whether the divine estimation by which he is reckoned to have paid and rendered is an act preceding justification.

units.la: ARTICULUS XXII. De Fide Iustificante, & de Iustificatione Fidei.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXII. On Justifying Faith, and on the Justification of Faith.

units.la: CREDIMUS Spiritum Sanctum per veram magni hujus mysterij cognitionem in cordibus nostris veram Fidem accendere, quæ IESUM Christum cum omnibus suis me-ritis amplectitur 1. eumq; sibi proprium vin-dicat, 2. nihilque deinceps extra illum quæ-rit. Necesse enim est, aut omnia quæ ad sa-lutem nostram requiruntur in Christo non esse: aut si sint in eo omnia, eum qui fide IESUM Christum possidet, simul etiam perfectam habere salutem. Itaque horren-da est omnino in DEUM blasphemia, asserere Christum minime sufficere, sed aliis quoque rebus opus esse. Inde enim sequeretur, Chri-stum ex parte tantum esse Servatorem. Merito igitur jureque dicimus cum D. Paulo, Nos sola fide justificari, seu Fide, absque operi-bus Legis. Cæterum nequaquam intelligimus esse fidem ipsam, proprie loquendo, 3. quæ nos justificet, [seu propter fidem nos justificari,] nam illa tantum est velut instrumentum, 4. quo Christum justitiam nostram apprehendimus. Christus igitur ipse nobis imputans omnia sua merita, & tam multa sanctissima opera, quæ pro nobis præstitit, est justitia nostra: 5. Fides vero est instru-mentum, quo illi in communionem omnium bonorum ipsius copulamur, atque in eadem retinemur. Adeo ut illa omnia postquam nostra facta sunt, nobis plus quam sufficiant ad nostri à peccatis absolutio-nem.
units.tr: We believe that the Holy Spirit, through the true knowledge of this great mystery, kindles in our hearts a true faith, which embraces Jesus Christ with all his merits, 1. and claims him as its own, 2. and seeks nothing further outside him. For it is necessary either that all things required for our salvation are not in Christ, or, if all are in him, that whoever possesses Jesus Christ by faith also has perfect salvation. Therefore it is utterly horrible blasphemy against God to assert that Christ is not sufficient, but that other things are also needed. For from this it would follow that Christ is a Saviour only in part. Rightly and justly, then, we say with St Paul that we are justified by faith alone, or by faith without the works of the Law. Yet we by no means understand that faith itself, properly speaking, 3. is what justifies us [or that we are justified on account of faith]; for faith is only like an instrument, 4. by which we lay hold of Christ as our righteousness. Christ himself, therefore, imputing to us all his merits and so many most holy works which he performed for us, is our righteousness; 5. faith, however, is the instrument by which we are joined to him in the communion of all his goods and are kept in that communion. So that all those things, once they have become ours, are more than sufficient for us for the absolution of our sins.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this article the following is taught.

units.la: 1. Ad Fidem justificantem non necessario requiri cognitionem IESV Christi: sed posse homines sine eius cognitione servari, seu justificari.
units.tr: 1. That faith which justifies does not necessarily require knowledge of Jesus Christ, but people can be saved, or justified, without knowing him.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. F.3. Sextus error est, quo existimant Evangelici, eos qui sub V. T. coram DEO justi sunt habiti, propterea tales habitos fuisse, & salutis æternæ nobiscum idcirco fore participes, quod sicut nos in Christum jam exhibitum, sic illi in eundem, quem exhibitum iri sperabant, omnino crediderint. Huic erro-ri universa Scriptura repugnat, quippe quæ fidei in Christum nullam prorsus mentionem, nisi pro eo tempore, quo exhibitus fuit, usquam faciat.
units.tr: From Welsingius, De Officio hominis christiani, sol. F.3. The sixth error is that the Evangelicals think those who were held righteous before God under the Old Testament were therefore held to be such and would share with us in eternal salvation, because they believed entirely in the same one who they hoped would be revealed, just as we believe in the one already revealed. The whole of Scripture contradicts this error, since it nowhere makes any mention at all of faith in Christ except for the time when he was revealed.

units.la: Ibidem. Caussa hujus erroris est quod creditum fuerit, nullam salutarem & justificantem fidem unquam fuisse, nisi fidem in Christum.
units.tr: Ibid. The cause of this error is the belief that there has never been any saving and justifying faith except faith in Christ.

units.la: Ibidem. Vide autem de fide in DEUM, quæ hominem illâ præditum ipsi Deo gratum facit, & ante Christi adventum, sine ullius in ipsum Christum fidei consideratione idipsum verè præstabat, caput xi. ad Hebræos.
units.tr: Ibid. But see, in Hebrews chapter 11, concerning faith in God, which makes the man endowed with it pleasing to God himself, and which before Christ's coming truly accomplished this without any consideration of faith in Christ himself.

units.la: AB ARMINIO, Resp. ad 31. Art. pag. 87. Consideretur de-scriptio fidei Abrahami ab Apostolo, Rom. 4. prolixè fa-cta, & apparebit in illa Iesu Christi mentionem non expresse fieri, sed illa implicatione, quam explicare non cuivis faci-le sit.
units.tr: From Arminius, Response to the 31 Articles, p. 87. Consider the description of Abraham's faith given by the Apostle at length in Romans 4, and it will appear that the name of Jesus Christ is not expressly mentioned in it, but only by an implication that is not easy for just anyone to explain.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 113. Conferatur quod dicitur Rom. 4. pene per totum caput de fide Abrahami, & ejus fidei objecto, & monstretur ex eo, quod Abraham in promissis istis, quæ fide apprehendit, Christum viderit.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 113. Compare what is said in Romans 4, almost throughout the whole chapter, about Abraham's faith and its object, and it will be shown from this that Abraham, in those promises which he grasped by faith, saw Christ.

units.la: A PETRO BERTIO, Discept. Epist. pag. 73. Apostolus ad Hebræos toto capite undecimo, hoc unum ex professo do-cet, Fide apprehendente res à sensibus humanis remotas Patres olim justi-tiæ testimonium reputasse, hoc est, justifi-catos esse. Et pag. 76. Nam de Christo quidem locis ex Epi-stola ad Hebræos allatis diserte nihil.
units.tr: From Peter Bertius, Disceptatio Epistolaris, p. 73. The Apostle to the Hebrews, throughout the whole eleventh chapter, teaches this one thing expressly: that the Fathers of old, by faith grasping things removed from human senses, were counted as witnesses of righteousness, that is, were justified. And p. 76: for concerning Christ, indeed, there is expressly nothing in the passages from the Epistle to the Hebrews cited.

units.la: A VENATORE, Declarat. pag. 183. Propter multas rationes salus alligari non potest historicæ de Iesu morte & passione fidei. Item. Nam si requiratur externa historiæ cognitio, & sine fide de Iesu passione & morte quis Deo gratus esse nequeat: quid fiet miseris Iudæis, quibus ea de re in omnibus Mosis libris ne ullum quidem verbum diserte ma-nifestatum est?
units.tr: From Venator, Declaratio, p. 183. For many reasons salvation cannot be bound to a historical faith in Jesus' death and passion. Likewise: for if an external knowledge of the history is required, and no one can be pleasing to God without faith in Jesus' passion and death, what will become of the unhappy Jews, to whom no word at all about this matter is expressly made known in all the books of Moses?

units.la: Ibidem.pag.184. Nunquam legi pium illum Iobum, pæni-tentes Ninevitas, & pium illum centurionem Cornelium ullam litteralem cognitionem seu fidem historicam habuisse de passione Iesu, ejusque causa, & tamen Deo grati fuerunt.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 184. I have never read that the pious Job, the penitent Ninevites, and the pious centurion Cornelius had any literal knowledge or historical faith about Jesus' passion and its cause, and yet they were pleasing to God.

units.la: Ibidem. Multi Ethnici[?] habuerunt etiam inter ipsos illu-stria testimonia interni, spiritualis, & veri cultus divini.
units.tr: Ibid. Many Gentiles among themselves also had illustrious testimonies of inner, spiritual and true divine worship.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.185. Nemo potest pervenire ad possessionem gloriæ æternæ sine misericordia, de quâ miseri Ethnici aliquam habuerunt coruscationem, atque in necessitatibus suis, vel in extremo vitæ agone, ad gratiam Dei se converte-runt, exclamantes: O Ens entium miserere mei.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 185. No one can attain possession of eternal glory without mercy, of which some flicker was present among the wretched Gentiles, and in their needs, or in the last agony of life, they turned to the grace of God, crying out: O Being of beings, have mercy on me.

units.la: Contra Pasl.Dordr.pag.131. Nego unicam viam ad salutem esse intelligere vitam, passionem, mortem, resurrectionem, ascensionem in cœlos & reliqua omnia, quæ de IESV in novo Testamento descripta invenimus.
units.tr: Against the Synod of Dort, p. 131. I deny that the only way to salvation is to understand the life, passion, death, resurrection, ascension into heaven, and all the other things about Jesus that we find described in the New Testament.

units.la: Ab Episcopio, Disput.de Discr.V.& N.T.thes.21. Patres crediderunt firmiter promissis divinis, quæ typos & umbras rerum cælestium continebant, quæque Christum, ejusque beneficia, iuxta intentionem divinam repræsentabant & præfigurabant: quâ ratione in Christum IESVM respexisse fidem illorum statuimus. An verò fides hæc in omnibus & singulis (Prophetas enim & alios nonnullos excipi volumus) conjunctam sibi habuerit notitiam & scientiam claram atque apertam typorum atque umbrarum, quod videlicet typi atque umbræ essent rerum earum, quæ nobis nunc apparent, & in Christo postmodum evenerunt, disquiri permittimus.
units.tr: From Episcopius, Disputatio de discrimine Veteris et Novi Testamenti, thesis 21. The Fathers firmly believed the divine promises, which contained the types and shadows of heavenly things, and which represented and foreshadowed Christ and his benefits according to the divine intention; for this reason we hold that their faith looked to Christ Jesus. But whether this faith, in all and each (for we wish the Prophets and some others to be excepted), had joined with it a clear and open knowledge and understanding of the types and shadows, namely that the types and shadows were of those things which now appear to us and afterwards came to pass in Christ, we allow to be investigated.

units.la: II. Ad Fidem justificantem non requiri certam fiduciam, quâ fidelis sibi applicat merita Christi, ac certò persuadet peccata sibi propter merita ac satisfactionem Christi esse remissa.
units.tr: II. That for justifying faith there is not required a certain confidence by which the believer applies to himself the merits of Christ, and firmly persuades himself that his sins have been forgiven him on account of the merits and satisfaction of Christ.

units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Artic.perpend.pag. 27. Fides justificans non est quâ quis credit sibi propter Christum esse remissa peccata.
units.tr: From Arminius, Articuli perpenduntur, p. 27. Justifying faith is not that by which someone believes that his sins have been forgiven him on account of Christ.

units.la: A VORSTIO, De Satisf.in Confess.pag.14. Sequitur eos fallere & falli, qui solam illam specialem, ut vocant, persuasionem de Satisfactione Christi pro se nominatim præstita Fidem justificantem esse putant.
units.tr: From Vorstius, De Satisfactione, in the Confession, p. 14. It follows that those deceive and are deceived who think that only that special, as they call it, persuasion concerning the satisfaction of Christ rendered for himself by name is justifying faith.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.32, Hæc definitio fidei, quæ statuit eam nihil aliud esse, quam credere peccata nostra esse deleta per ea quæ Christus est passus, est falsa, cum talis fides in Scriptura fit inaudita. Item. Certum est Christum id nunquam docuisse, nec quidquam ijs, qui hanc fidem haberent, promisisse.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 32. This definition of faith, which holds that it is nothing other than to believe that our sins have been blotted out through what Christ suffered, is false, since such faith is unheard of in Scripture. Likewise: it is certain that Christ never taught this, nor promised anything to those who had this faith.

units.la: Catal.error.Sibr.pag.62. Sacræ literæ docent Fidem idem esse, quod Observatio Christianismi. Item. Credere idem esse, quod observare Christi præcepta.
units.tr: Catalogus errorum Sibrandi, p. 62. The sacred letters teach that faith is the same as the observance of Christianity. Likewise: to believe is the same as to observe the precepts of Christ.

units.la: AB EPISCOPIO, Disp.priv.15.thes.5. Fiducia specialis misericordiæ, quâ credo mihi remissa esse peccata gratis, non est essentiale fidei constituens, sed consequens tantum.
units.tr: From Episcopius, Disputatio privata, thesis 15, thesis 5. The special confidence in mercy by which I believe that my sins have been freely forgiven me is not the essential constituent of faith, but only a consequence of it.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. B. 6. 7. Explicandus autem apertius hic est ingens Evangelicorum error in definiendo, quænam sit Fides in Christum, qua justificamur. Statuerunt merito contra Pontificiorum sententiam, Fidem istam esse fiduciam, atqui interim quæ & qualis sit ista fiducia non animadverterunt. Statuerunt enim hanc fiduciam esse sibi firmiter hoc ipsum persuadere & sic confidere, quod per Christi mortem deleta fuerint peccata nostra, quodque DEUS propter ipsum Christum nos acceptos & gratos habeat.
units.tr: From Welsingius, De Officio hominis christiani, sol. B.6, 7. The great error of the Evangelicals in defining what faith in Christ is, by which we are justified, must be explained more plainly here. They rightly held, against the opinion of the Papists, that this faith is confidence; yet meanwhile they did not notice what and of what kind this confidence is. For they held that this confidence is to persuade oneself firmly of this very thing, and so to trust, that our sins have been blotted out by the death of Christ, and that God on account of Christ himself holds us as accepted and pleasing.

units.la: Ibidem. Non igitur hæc est illa fides in Christum, seu per Christum in DEUM, qua justificamur; sed ea quæ verè ac proprie est fiducia, nempe Christo, seu Deo per Christum, plane confidere, hoc est, sub spe ea consequendi, quæ à Deo per Christum ijs sunt promissa, qui ipsius Christi præcepta ita servaverint, ut merito obedientes dici possint, ipsi Deo & Christo obedire, & sic, ut uno verbo dicam, non secundum carnem, sed secundum spiritum ambulare.
units.tr: Ibid. This, then, is not that faith in Christ, or through Christ in God, by which we are justified; but that which truly and properly is confidence, namely to trust fully in Christ, or in God through Christ, that is, under the hope of obtaining those things which are promised by God through Christ to those who have so kept the precepts of Christ himself that they can rightly be called obedient, obeying God himself and Christ; and so, to say it in one word, to walk not according to the flesh but according to the spirit.

units.la: A REMONSTRANTIBUS, Resp. ad Epist. VVal. pag. 88. Fides justificans non est , qua quis credit sibi remissa esse peccata.
units.tr: From the Remonstrants, Response to the Epistle of Walaeus, p. 88. Justifying faith is not that by which someone believes that his sins have been forgiven him.

units.la: III. Fidem proprie loquendo , seu in Credere , nos justificare: seu esse justitiam nostram, quâ coram DEO consi-[?]stimus & justificamur.
units.tr: III. That faith, properly speaking, or the act of believing, justifies us, or is our righteousness, by which we stand before God and are justified.

units.la: AB ARMINIO, Epist.ad Hipp.pag.(*.)2. Dico ipsum fidei actum, id est, τò Credere, imputari in justitiam: idque proprie sensu, non metonymicè.
units.tr: From Arminius, *Epistola ad Hipparchum*, p. (*) 2. I say that the act of faith itself, that is, the act of believing [τὸ πιστεύειν], is imputed for righteousness, and that in the proper sense, not metonymically.

units.la: Ibidem. Fides gratiosè pro justitiâ habetur, per gratiosam dignationem DEI.
units.tr: Ibid. Faith is held as righteousness graciously, through the gracious favour of God.

units.la: Ibidem. Fides est objectum imputationis divinæ.
units.tr: Ibid. Faith is the object of divine imputation.

units.la: Declar.pag.65. Quaestio movetur de verbis Apostoli Pauli ad Romanos cap.4. hisce videlicet, Fides imputatur ad justitiam, utrum nempe ea debeant proprie intelligi, sicut ipsa fides, tanquam actus juxta mandatum Evangelij præstitus, imputetur coram Deo in, sive ad justitiam, idque ex gratiâ, cum non sit ipsamet justitia Legis: an verò sic intelligi debeant, ut justitia Christi per fidem apprehensa nobis in justitiam imputetur, id est, figuratè atq; improprie. Ego prio-rem sententiam secutus sum in thesibus de Justificatione sub me disputatis.
units.tr: Declaratio, p. 65. The question is raised about the words of the Apostle Paul in Romans chapter 4, namely: faith is imputed for righteousness; whether these things ought to be understood properly, just as faith itself, as an act performed according to the command of the Gospel, is imputed before God in or for righteousness, and that by grace, since it is not itself the righteousness of the Law; or whether they ought to be understood so that the righteousness of Christ, grasped through faith, is imputed to us for righteousness, that is, figuratively and improperly. I have followed the former opinion in the theses on Justification disputed under me.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 66. Statuo bene & proprie dici fidem homini credenti in justitiam ex gratiâ imputari.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 66. I affirm that it is well and properly said that faith is imputed to the believing man for righteousness by grace.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Catal.error.Sibr.pag.41. Fides nobis ad justitiam imputatur formaliter.
units.tr: From Vorstius, Catalogus errorum Sibrandi, p. 41. Faith is imputed to us for righteousness formally.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 46. Nos asserimus fidem imputative pro justitiâ haberi, seu justitiæ loco nobis duci. Item. Loco perfecta justitia fides nostra nobis imputatur, & à DEO ducitur.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 46. We assert that faith is held as righteousness by imputation, or is reckoned to us in place of righteousness. Likewise: In place of perfect righteousness our faith is imputed to us and is accounted by God.

units.la: Confess.pag.35. Cum fides nobis dicitur imputari ad justitiam, nihil aliud significatur, quam quod fides loco nostra justitia ducitur nobis.
units.tr: Confess. pag. 35. When faith is said to be imputed to us for righteousness, nothing else is meant than that faith is reckoned to us in place of our righteousness.

units.la: A BERTIO, Epist.ad Sibr.pag.81. Cum Scriptum fidei tribuat, ut reputetur ad justitiam, ut salvet, ut ex eâ vivamus, sequitur fidem proprie accipiendam esse, pro habitu, sive obedientia illa, quæ præstatur Evangelio, eaque nos proprie, sed tamen gratis justificari à DEO, & servari.
units.tr: From BERTIUS, Epist. ad Sibr. pag. 81. Since Scripture ascribes faith to us so that it is reckoned for righteousness, so that it saves us, and so that we live by it, it follows that faith must be understood properly as a habit, or that obedience which is rendered to the Gospel; and by this we are properly, yet freely, justified and saved by God.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.85. Justificare est universalis affectio fidei.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 85. To justify is a universal affection of faith.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 48. Fides subflituta est in locum plenæ observationis Legis, ideoque eam per gratuitam ratishabitionem DEI, nullo nostro merito, censeri pro universâ justitiâ Legis.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 48. Faith has been substituted in the place of full observance of the Law, and therefore, through God's gracious acceptance, without any merit of ours, it is reckoned for the whole righteousness of the Law.

units.la: A IOAN. ARNOLDO. Contra Gomar. pag.35. Fides in Justificatione consideratur tanquam Lex, postulatum, & conditio, quam debemus præstare, ut propositum præmium justitiæ consequamur.
units.tr: From JOHANN ARNOLD, Against Gomarus, pag. 35. In justification faith is considered as a law, a demand, and a condition, which we must fulfil so that we may obtain the promised reward of righteousness.

units.la: Ibidem. Arminius dicit DEVM in nostri Justificatione ita spectare fidem, ut æstimet eam pro obedientia & pro opere secundum Evangelicam postulationem & Legem præstito.
units.tr: Ibidem. Arminius says that God, in our justification, so regards faith that he esteems it as obedience and as a work rendered according to the evangelical demand and law.

units.la: Item. Arminius intelligit DEVM fidem nobis imputare pro obedientia.
units.tr: Likewise. Arminius understands that God imputes faith to us as obedience.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 41. Arminius dicit fidem justificare ut actum, qui opus illud DEI est, Ioan. 6. atque ipsum τὸ[?] credere in Christum nobis in justitiam imputari.
units.tr: Ibidem. pag. 41. Arminius says that faith justifies as an act, which is that work of God (John 6), and that the very believing [τὸ πιστεύειν] in Christ is imputed to us for righteousness.

units.la: A REMONSTRANTIBVS, Respons. ad Epist. VVal. pag. 86.
units.tr: From the REMONSTRANTS, Response to the Letter of Walaeus, pag. 86.

units.la: Deus qui in fœdere Legali exactam mandatorum suorum obedientiam exigebat, nunc in fœdere Evangelico fidem exigit, & illam gratiosa æstimatione propter meritum & omnibus numeris exquisitissimam Christi obedientiam habere loco legalis obedientia.
units.tr: God, who in the legal covenant demanded exact obedience to his commandments, now in the evangelical covenant demands faith, and, by gracious estimation on account of the merit and the most exquisite obedience of Christ in every respect, holds it in place of legal obedience.

units.la: IV. Fidem in negotio justificationis non debere considerari ut instrumentum apprehendens Christi justitiam.
units.tr: IV. In the matter of justification, faith ought not to be considered as the instrument that lays hold of Christ's righteousness.

units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Resp. ad 31. Art. pag. 159. Fides non qua instrumentum, sed qua actio imputatur in justitiam.
units.tr: By ARMINIUS, Response to the 31st Article, pag. 159. Faith is imputed for righteousness not as an instrument, but as an act.

units.la: A IOAN. ARNOLDO, Contra Gomar. pag. 41. Arminius dicit ipsum credere in Christum nobis in justitiam imputari, non ut instrumentum. Item. Arminio displicuit, quod fides dicatur esse instrumentalis causa nostræ justificationis.
units.tr: From JOHANN ARNOLD, Against Gomarus, pag. 41. Arminius says that the very believing in Christ is imputed to us for righteousness, and not as an instrument. Likewise: It displeased Arminius that faith should be called the instrumental cause of our justification.

units.la: A SIM. EPISCOPIO, Disput. priv. de justif. thes. §.6. Fides itaque in negotio justificationis consideranda est, non tanquam instrumentum apprehendens justitiam hanc quæ imputatur, sed tanquam apprehendens Christum IESVM, per quem justitia illa impetrata est, Instrumentum tamen proprie dici non potest, sed conditio fœdere Evangelico præscripta & requisita.
units.tr: From SIMON EPISCOPIUS, Private Disputation on Justification, thesis 6. Faith, therefore, in the matter of justification, is to be considered not as an instrument laying hold of that righteousness which is imputed, but as laying hold of Jesus Christ, through whom that righteousness has been obtained. Yet it cannot properly be called an instrument, but is a condition prescribed and required in the evangelical covenant.

units.la: V. Iustitiam Domini nostri IESV CHRISTI non esse iustitiam illam, quæ in nostri iustificatione nobis à DEO imputetur in iustitiam nostram, quâ coram DEO consistimus, seu iustificamur: sed esse tantum causam meritoriam, quâ impetratum sit ut iustitia aliqua nobis ipsis inhærens in iustitiam nostram à DEO per gratiosam æstimationem imputetur.
units.tr: V. The righteousness of our Lord Jesus Christ is not that righteousness which is imputed to us by God in our justification as our righteousness, by which we stand or are justified before God; but it is only the meritorious cause by which it has been obtained that some righteousness inhering in ourselves be imputed by God to us as our righteousness, through gracious estimation.

units.la: Sententia Evangelicorum de Iustificatione ejusmodi est, ut mirum videri possit, si quis eam amplexus, vitam tamen homine Christiano dignam interea ducat. Nam invaluit apud eos opinio imputata credentibus iustitia Christi, quâ scilicet fiat, ut etiamsi Christi fideles, & sic iustificati coram DEO homines, propriâ sanctitate vitæ non sint prædíti, non tamen ista carere dici possint, quippe quibus DEVS Christi sanctitatem & innocentiam imputet.
units.tr: The Evangelicals' view of justification is of such a kind that it may seem strange if anyone who embraces it nevertheless lives a life worthy of a Christian man. For among them the opinion has prevailed that the righteousness of Christ is imputed to believers, namely, that even if they are Christ's faithful ones, and so men justified before God, they are not endowed with holiness of life of their own, yet they cannot be said to lack it, since God imputes to them the holiness and innocence of Christ.

units.la: Ibidem. Apostolus Rom. 4. affirmat quidem nobis imputari iustitiam, seu credentes in DEVM pro iustis haberi: sed quod Christi iustitia nobis imputetur, hoc est, ejus sanctitas & innocentia nostra esse censeatur, de eo nihil prorsus loquitur, vel loqui cuiquam merito videri potest.
units.tr: Ibidem. The Apostle, in Romans 4, indeed affirms that righteousness is imputed to us, or that believers in God are held as righteous; but concerning the imputation of Christ's righteousness to us, that is, that his holiness and innocence are counted as ours, he says absolutely nothing, nor can anyone rightly think he does.

units.la: Christus & obedientia ejus causa justificationis impetratoria seu meritoria est, at non objectum justificationis seu imputationis divina, quasi DEVS Christum ejusque iustitiam nobis imputet in iustitiam, quod fieri nequit.
units.tr: Christ and his obedience are the impetratory or meritorious cause of justification, but not the object of justification or of divine imputation, as though God imputed Christ and his righteousness to us for righteousness, which cannot happen.

units.la: Dico me credere peccatores solâ Christi obedientiâ iustos constitui: & quod iustitia Christi sola meritoria causa sit, propter quam DEVS credentibus peccatum condonet: & statuo bene & proprie dici fidem homini credenti in iustitiam ex gratia imputari. Hanc sententiam Arminij BERTIVS testatur, Epist. ad Sibr. pag. 119. meritum Christi excludere.
units.tr: I say that I believe sinners are made righteous by Christ's obedience alone, and that the righteousness of Christ is the sole meritorious cause on account of which God pardons sin to believers; and I maintain that it is well and properly said that faith is imputed by grace to the believing man for righteousness. BERTIUS bears witness that this opinion of Arminius excludes the merit of Christ, Epist. ad Sibr. pag. 119.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Catal.err.Sibr.pag.41. Nusquam diserte scriptum est, obedientiam Christi nobis ad justitiam, imputari, aut saltem esse justitiam illam,per quam nos justificamur,puta formaliter,& non effective.
units.tr: From VORSTIUS, Catalogue of the Errors of Sibrandus, pag. 41. Nowhere is it plainly written that the obedience of Christ is imputed to us for righteousness, or at least that it is that righteousness by which we are justified, namely formally and not effectively.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.46. Obedientia & satisfactio Christi non proprie & formaliter,sed effective seu metonymice justitia imputata dicitur..
units.tr: Ibidem, pag. 46. The obedience and satisfaction of Christ are called imputed righteousness not properly and formally, but effectively or metonymically.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.50. Christi obedientia consideratur in justificatione nostri ut causa efficiens & meritoria, & obedientia nostra ut conditio sine qua non. Item. Apostolus per justitiam suam non simpliciter eam intelligit, quam revera in seipso haberet, licet a Deo gratis in Christo donatam: sed quam ipse per opera legis sibi ex seipso comparasset.
units.tr: Ibidem, pag. 50. The obedience of Christ is considered in our justification as the efficient and meritorious cause, and our obedience as the condition without which not. Likewise: The Apostle, by his righteousness, does not understand simply that which he would really have in himself, although granted to him freely by God in Christ; but that which he himself would have acquired from himself through the works of the law.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.54. Obedientia Christi non imputatur nobis pro justitia formali, sive ad hoc ut per eam formaliter justi simus. Effective tamen imputari nobis & potest & solet.
units.tr: Ibidem, pag. 54. The obedience of Christ is not imputed to us as formal righteousness, that is, so that we are formally made just by it. Effectively, however, it both can and commonly is imputed to us.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.61. Vera assertio est Fidem justificantem esse illam inhaerentem justitiam, quam Papistae urgent, si de fide formata sermo sit. Talis enim fides iuxta stylum Scripturæ non male inhaerens justitia vocari potest: quippe habitus spiritualis ex fide, spe, charitate compositus, quem justitia titulo fraudare velle, desipere est.
units.tr: Ibidem, pag. 61. It is a true assertion that justifying faith is that inherent righteousness which the Papists press, if the discussion concerns formed faith. For such faith, according to the manner of speaking of Scripture, can not unfittingly be called inherent righteousness, since it is a spiritual habit composed of faith, hope, and charity; and to wish to deprive it of the title of righteousness is folly.

units.la: Ibidem. Christi satisfactio nobis non formaliter, sed effective imputatur.
units.tr: Ibidem. The satisfaction of Christ is imputed to us not formally, but effectively.

units.la: A BERTIO, Epist.ad Sibr.pag.69.70. Dices ineptum videri nos habitu, sive qualitate nobis inhaerente justificari & servari. Quid? ineptumne etiam videbitur, si id dicat DEUS?
units.tr: From BERTIUS, Epist. ad Sibr. pag. 69, 70. You will say that it seems absurd for us to be justified and preserved by a habit, or a quality inhering in us. What? Will it also seem absurd if God himself says this?

units.la: Ibidem.pag.74. Si ergo fides est qualitas nobis inhaerens: hi vero omnes quos commemorat Apostolus, fide justifi-cati sunt, consequens est eosdem qualitate sibi inhaerente ju-stificatos esse.
units.tr: Ibidem, pag. 74. If, therefore, faith is a quality inhering in us, and all those whom the Apostle mentions were justified by faith, it follows that they were justified by a quality inhering in themselves.

units.la: Item.pag.75. Neque enim quemquam ita infantem esse puto, ut post tot, tamque validas ἀποδείξεις [?] dicturus sit, fidem hic correlative (ut loquuntur) significare Christum ipsum & justitiam Christi.
units.tr: Likewise, pag. 75. For I do not think anyone is so much a child that, after so many and such strong demonstrations [ἀποδείξεις], he would say that faith here signifies, correlatively (as they say), Christ himself and the righteousness of Christ.

units.la: A SIM.EPISCOPIO,Disput.privat.de iustific.thes.4. Non itaque iustitia proprie Christi,nedum actava aut passiva, est iustitia illa quae imputari dicitur, sed id quod Christus utraque promeruit, & nos per solum Christum IESUM consequimur: non enim iustitia Christi proprie id est quod imputatur, sed id propterquod imputatur nobis credentibus in ipsum iustitia.
units.tr: From SIMON EPISCOPIUS, Private Disputation on Justification, thesis 4. Therefore the righteousness of Christ, not to mention active or passive, properly speaking is not that righteousness which is said to be imputed; rather it is that on account of which righteousness is imputed to us who believe in him, which we obtain through Jesus Christ alone. For the righteousness of Christ is not properly that which is imputed, but that on account of which righteousness is imputed to us who believe in him.

units.la: ARTICVLVS XXIII. De Iustitia nostra qua coram DEO consistimus.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXIII. On the Righteousness by Which We Stand before God.

units.la: CRedimus beatitudinem nostram sitam esse in peccatorum nostrorum remissione, quae fit propter IESUM Christum: atque in ea contineri iustitiam nostram coram DEO: uti nos D. Paulus docet ex Davide, quum pronuntiat Beatum eum hominem, cui DEUS imputat iustitiam absque operibus. idem Apostolus ait, Nos gratis iustificari per redemptionem factam in Christo IESU. Ac propterea hoc fundamentum [in æternum] firmum retinemus, & DEO gloriam omnem tribuimus, de nobis ipsis quam humiliter sentientes, ut qui probè noverimus qui, qua-lesque lesque [?] simus revera. Ideoque de nobis ullif-ve nostris meritis nihil quidquam præsumi-mus, sed foli IESV Christi crucifixi obe-dientiæ innixi, ineâ prorsus acquiescimus, quæ nostra fit quando in eum credimus 1. Hæc porrò una abūdè sufficit, tum ad omnes nostras iniquitates obtegendas, tum etiam ad nos tutos securosque reddendos adversus o-mnes tentationes. Illa enim procul à conscientiâ abigit omnem metum, omnem horro-rem, omnem denique formidinem, quò pro-pius ad DEVM accedamus, nec primi illius nostri parentis exemplum imitemur, qui præ metu fugiens, ficulneis sese foliis obtegere & occultare conatus est. Et sanè si nobis ipsis, aut ulli alteri creaturæ vel tantillum nitentes coram DEO nos sistere oporteret, certum est nos statim absorptum iri. Idcircò cum Davi-de nobis singulis potius est exclamandum, Domine ne intres in judicium cum servo tuo, quia non justificabitur in conspectu tuo ullus vivens.
units.tr: We believe that our blessedness consists in the forgiveness of our sins, which takes place on account of Jesus Christ, and that our righteousness before God is contained in this forgiveness, as the Apostle Paul teaches us from David, when he pronounces blessed is the man to whom God imputes righteousness without works. The same Apostle says, We are justified freely through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. Therefore we firmly hold to this foundation for ever, and we ascribe all glory to God, thinking humbly of ourselves, since we know well who and what sort of people we truly are. Accordingly we presume nothing on account of ourselves or any of our merits, but, resting solely on the obedience of Jesus Christ crucified, we rest wholly in it, which becomes ours when we believe in him. 1. This alone is abundantly sufficient, both to cover all our iniquities and to make us safe and secure against all temptations. For it drives far from the conscience all fear, all horror, and finally all dread, so that we may draw nearer to God, and not imitate the example of our first parent, who, fleeing in fear, tried to hide and conceal himself under fig leaves. And indeed, if we had to present ourselves before God relying even slightly on ourselves or on any other creature, it is certain that we would be swallowed up at once. Therefore, with David, each of us should rather cry out: Lord, do not enter into judgment with your servant, for no living man will be justified in your sight.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: It seems that the following is taught against this Article.

units.la: I. Iustitiam nostram, quâ coram DEO consistimus, non esse iustitiam Christi, quæ extra nos est, sed esse iustitiam nobis ipsis inhærentem.
units.tr: I. That our righteousness, by which we stand before God, is not the righteousness of Christ, which is outside us, but a righteousness inhering in ourselves.

units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Epist. ad Hipp. (·.·)2. Fieri non potest, ut DEVS Christum ejusque iustitiam nobis imputet in iustitiam.
units.tr: From ARMINIUS, Letter to Hippolytus (2). It cannot happen that God imputes Christ and his righteousness to us as righteousness.

units.la: Ibidem. Christus cum obedientiâ suâ non est obiectum im-putationis divinæ.
units.tr: Ibid. Christ, with his obedience, is not the object of divine imputation.

units.la: Ab EPISCOPIO, Disput.privat.de Iustif.thes.4. Iustitia Christi non est proprie id quod imputatur, sed id propter quod imputatur nobis credentibus in ipsum Justitia.
units.tr: From EPISCOPIUS, Private Disputation on Justification, thesis 4. The righteousness of Christ is not properly that which is imputed, but that on account of which righteousness is imputed to us who believe in him.

units.la: A BERTIO, Epist.ad Sibr.pag.69.70. Non est ineptum dicere, cum DEVS ipse id dicat, nos habitu seu qualitate nobis inhæ-rente justificari.
units.tr: From BERTIUS, Letter to Sibrandus, pp. 69–70. It is not absurd to say, since God himself says so, that we are justified by a habit or quality inhering in us.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.74. Si fides est qualitas nobis inhærens: hi vero omnes, quos commemorat Apostolus, fide justificati sunt, consequens est eosdem qualitate sibi inhærente justifica-tos esse.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 74. If faith is a quality inhering in us, and all those whom the Apostle mentions were justified by faith, it follows that they were justified by a quality inhering in themselves.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Catal.err.Sibr.pag.50. Apostolus Phil.3.9.per justitiam suam non simpliciter intelligit eam, quam revera in seipso haberet, licet à DEO gratis in Christo donatam: sed quam ipse per opera Legis sibi ex seipso comparasset.
units.tr: From VORSTIUS, Catalogue of the Errors of Sibrandus, p. 50. By his own righteousness the Apostle (Phil. 3.9) does not simply mean that which he actually had in himself, although freely given to him by God in Christ, but that which he had acquired for himself from himself through the works of the Law.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.61. Fides quæ per charitatem operatur, non male inhærens justitia vocari potest; quippe habitus spiritualis ex fide, spe, charitate compositus, quem justitiæ titulo frau-dare velle, desipere est.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 61. Faith which works through love can not badly be called an inhering righteousness; for it is a spiritual habit composed of faith, hope and love, and to want to deprive it of the title of righteousness is folly.

units.la: In Anti-Bell.pag.613. Cavendum ne quemquam statua-mus justificari absque vera & viva fide, quæ fides rectè in-tellecta est justitia illa inhærens, quam Adversarij semper hic urgent.
units.tr: In Anti-Bellarminus, p. 613. We must take care that we do not hold that anyone is justified without true and living faith, which, rightly understood, is that inhering righteousness which our opponents always press here.

units.la: ARTICVLVS XXIV. De Sanctificatione, & de bonis operibus.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXIV. On Sanctification and on Good Works.

units.la: CRedimus veram hanc fidem per auditum verbi DEI & Spiritus Sancti operationem in nobis productam, nos regenerare ac veluti novos homines efficere, ut quos ad novam vitam vivendam excitet, & à peccati servitute liberos reddat. Tantum abest igitur ut fides hæc justificans à rectâ sanctáque vivendi ratione avocet aut tepidiores efficiat 1. ut contrà absque illâ nemo unquam quidquam boni ex amore DEI agere atque operari possit, sed tantùm ex amore suiipsius & ex metu condemnationis. Fieri itaque non potest, ut hæc fides sancta in homine sit otiosa. Neque enim loquimur de fide inani, sed de eâ tantum, quæ in Scripturâ dicitur per charitatem operari, quæque impellit hominem, ut in illis sese operibus exerceat, quæ DEVS ipse in verbo suo præcepit. Hæc verò opera à sincerâ fidei hujus radice emanantia, ideò demum bona & DEO grata sunt, quia per illius gratiam sanctificantur: ad nos autem justificandos nullius prorsus sunt momenti 2. Fide enim in IESVM Christum justificamur, & quidem priusquàm bona ulla opera ediderimus 3. Neque enim magis ante fidem opera nostra bona esse possunt, quam fructus arboris esse possunt boni, priusquam arbor ipsa bona fuerit. Facimus igitur bona quidem opera, sed non ut aliquid ijs promereamur. Quid enim promereri nos possimus? Quinimò DEO magis magisque ad bona opera, si quæ facimus, sumus obstricti, non DEVS nobis. DEVS enim is est, qui efficit in nobis, ut & velimus, & ut efficiamus, pro gratuita sua benevolentia. Unde ad illud nobis semper est respiciendum quod scriptum est: Quum feceritis omnia, quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite, servi inutiles sumus, nam quod debuimus facere, hoc fecimus. Interea non negamus DEVM bona opera in suis remunerari: sed id merâ suâ gratiâ fieri dicimus, ut qui dona sua in nobis coronet, 4. Cæterum quamvis bona opera faciamus, nequaquam tamen ullam salutis nostræ spem in illis collocamus. Nulla enim opera edere possumus, quæ non sint carnis nostræ vitio polluta, ac proinde supplicio pœnisque digna. 5, Quod si etiam aliquod ejusmodi opus proferre quiremus, sola tamen peccati recordatio sufficeret, ad illud è conspectu DEI removendum. Itaque semper in dubio essemus, hinc inde fluctuantes, absq; ulla certitudine, & miserae nostrae conscientiae semper vexarentur, nisi unico merito mortis & passionis Servatoris nostri niterentur, & in illo acquiescerent.
units.tr: We believe that this true faith, produced in us through the hearing of the Word of God and the operation of the Holy Spirit, regenerates us and makes us as it were new men, since it stirs us up to live a new life and renders us free from the bondage of sin. So far is this justifying faith from calling us away from a right and holy manner of life, or from making us more lukewarm, that, on the contrary, without it no one can ever do or perform anything good from love of God, but only from love of himself and from fear of condemnation. Therefore it cannot happen that this holy faith is idle in a man. For we do not speak of an empty faith, but only of that which Scripture calls working through love, and which impels a man to exercise himself in those works which God himself has commanded in his word. Moreover, these works, springing from the true root of this faith, are therefore good and pleasing to God, because they are sanctified by his grace; but for our justification they are of no importance at all. 2. For we are justified by faith in Jesus Christ, and indeed before we have produced any good works. 3. For our works cannot be good before faith any more than the fruits of a tree can be good before the tree itself is good. We therefore do good works, but not so that we may merit anything by them. For what can we merit? Rather, we are bound more and more to God by good works, if we do any, and not God to us. For God is he who works in us both to will and to work, according to his gracious goodwill. Hence we must always look to what is written: When you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, we are unprofitable servants, for we have only done what we ought to have done. Meanwhile we do not deny that God rewards good works in his own people, but we say that this is done by his mere grace, so that he crowns his own gifts in us. 4. Moreover, although we do good works, we nevertheless place no hope of our salvation in them. For we can produce no works which are not polluted by the vice of our flesh, and therefore worthy of punishment and penalties. 5. Even if we could bring forward some such work, the mere remembrance of sin would suffice to remove it from the sight of God. Thus we would always be in doubt, wavering this way and that, without any certainty, and our wretched consciences would always be troubled, unless they rested on the sole merit of the death and passion of our Saviour and acquiesced in him.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: It seems to be taught against this article.

units.la: I. Doctrinam, quâ docetur, homines justificari solâ fide, seu solâ justitiâ Christi fide apprehensâ, nobisque gratis imputatâ, reddere homines tepidos ac securos, & à sanctitatis studio avocare.
units.tr: I. The doctrine that men are justified by faith alone, that is, by the righteousness of Christ alone, apprehended by faith and freely imputed to us, makes men lukewarm and careless and draws them away from the pursuit of holiness.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic.hom. Christ.sol.B. 4. Sententia Evangelicorum ejusmodi est, ut mirum videri possit, si quis eam amplexus vitam tamen homine Christiano dignam interea ducat.
units.tr: From Welsingius, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. B. 4. The opinion of the Evangelicals is of such a kind that it may seem remarkable if anyone who embraces it nevertheless regards a life worthy of a Christian man as something to be lived in the meantime.

units.la: Ibidem sol.B.7. Cum docetur bona opera ad nos justificandos nihil pertinere, sed tantum esse fructus fidei, quâ homo coram DEO justificatur; quid inveniri potuit aptius ad hominem in uno pluribusve peccatis manentem, in eo statu perpetuò confervandum, eumq; plane deterrendum à stu-dio sese à peccatorum laqueis extricandi.
units.tr: Ibid. sol. B. 7. When it is taught that good works contribute nothing to our justification, but are only the fruits of the faith by which a man is justified before God, what could be found more fitting for keeping a man who remains in one or more sins in that state forever, and for utterly deterring him from the effort to free himself from the snares of sin?

units.la: Ibidem sol.8. Deo & Christo obedire, & non secundum carnem, sed secundum spiritum vivere, ista Evangelicorum fides certè nec in seipsâ, ut deberet, continet, nec etiam vel efficit, vel efficere potest.
units.tr: Ibid. sol. 8. This faith of the Evangelicals certainly neither contains in itself, as it ought, the obedience owed to God and Christ, and the living not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit, nor does it even bring this about or can it bring it about.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Catal. err. Sibr. pag. 33. Si certi sumus postquam justificatio semel est impetrata, qualitatem poenitentiae certò secuturam, persuasio haec nil nisi profanam carnis securitatem parere potest.
units.tr: From Vorstius, Catal. err. Sibr. p. 33. If we are certain that, once justification has been obtained, the quality of repentance will surely follow, this persuasion can produce nothing but a profane security of the flesh.

units.la: A BERTIO, Epist. ad Sibr. pag. 99. Cum extra hominem omnia ponimus in Christo, periculum imminet Ecclesijs nostris à profanitate & securitate.
units.tr: From Bertius, Epist. ad Sibr. p. 99. When we place everything outside man in Christ, danger threatens our churches from profanity and security.

units.la: II. Opera à sincera fidei radice emanantia non excludi à justificatione, sed tantum opera Legis, quae ex viribus no-stris proficiscuntur, & quibus perfecta & continua totius Legis observatio praestatur. Ac proinde nos justificari coram DEO operibus nostris, quae secundum Evangelium ex fide praestamus.
units.tr: II. Works springing from the sincere root of faith are not excluded from justification, but only the works of the Law, which proceed from our own powers, and by which a perfect and continual observance of the whole Law is rendered. And therefore we are justified before God by our works, which we perform from faith according to the Gospel.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Catal. err. Sibr. pag. 49. Scopus Apostoli, omniaque ipsius argumenta, quae pro gratuita hominis credentis justificatione illic (Rom. 4.) adducit, satis ostendunt, eum semper hic loqui de operibus Legis, nec istorum nomine quidquam aliud intelligere, quam perfectam & continuam totius Legis observationem.
units.tr: From Vorstius, Catal. err. Sibr. p. 49. The aim of the Apostle, and all the arguments he adduces there (Rom. 4) for the free justification of the believing man, sufficiently show that he is always speaking here of the works of the Law, and that by those works he understands nothing other than the perfect and continual observance of the whole Law.

units.la: Ibidem. Opposita illa gratia & operum, quae Rom. 4. & 11. Ephes. 2. Tit. 3. & alibi extat, non simpliciter & universaliter, nec de quibusvis operibus, etiam fidei & fidelium pro-priis, sed limitate de operibus Legis, quaeque meritoria esse pu-tantur, accipienda sunt.
units.tr: Ibid. That opposition of grace and works, which occurs in Rom. 4 and 11, Eph. 2, Tit. 3 and elsewhere, is not to be taken simply and universally, nor of any works whatever, even those of faith and the faithful's own works, but in a limited sense, of the works of the Law, which are thought to be meritorious.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 50. Apostolus Phil. 3. 9. per justitiam suam non simpliciter eam intelligit, quam revera in seipso haberet, licet à Deo gratis in Christo donatam: sed quam ipse per opera Legis sibi ex seipso comparasset: prout vel ex solâ antithesi Legis & fidei satis ibidem apparet. Lex enim urget obedientiam ex viribus nostris praestandam; at fides gratiam Christi hic praedicat.
