units.tr: Ibid. p. 50. The Apostle in Phil. 3:9 does not understand by "his righteousness" simply that which he would actually have in himself, though freely given him by God in Christ, but that which he would have acquired for himself from himself by the works of the Law; as is sufficiently clear there from the antithesis of Law and faith alone. For the Law urges obedience to be rendered from our own powers, whereas faith here proclaims the grace of Christ.

units.la: Schol.pag.233. Nos nostra obedientia, proprie sumpta, coram Deo justificamur, ut conditione prius à nobis implenda, quam ipsam justitiam, hoc est, veniam peccatorum reipsa obtinere atque impetrare possimus.
units.tr: Schol. p. 233. We are justified before God by our obedience, properly taken, as a condition to be fulfilled by us beforehand, so that we may actually obtain and procure that righteousness itself, that is, the forgiveness of sins.

units.la: Catal.err.Sibr.pag.31. Fateor obedientiam nostram, quae ex Lege est, à causis justificationis excludendam esse, neque nos ullo modo justitiam & salutem obedientiâ nostrâ promereri; sed hoc nihil ad obedientiam fidei pertinere dico, & Apostoli verba Phil. 3. 9. huc quidquam facere nego.
units.tr: Catal. err. Sibr. p. 31. I admit that our obedience, which is from the Law, is to be excluded from the causes of justification, and that we in no way merit righteousness and salvation by our obedience; but I say this has nothing to do with the obedience of faith, and I deny that the words of the Apostle in Phil. 3:9 bear anything on this.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 61. Homo justificatur per praecedentem pœniten-tiam, sive per opera à Christo mandata, si sub pœnitentiæ nomine conditio tantum praecedanea: item si per opera metonymicè fides operans accipiatur.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 61. A man is justified through preceding repentance, or through works commanded by Christ, if under the name of repentance only a preceding condition is meant; likewise if by works faith that works is metonymically understood.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.54. Operibus justificari, & fide per charita-tem operante justificari, opposita interdum sunt, cum videlicet opera Legis, seu meritoria coram Deo, hic intelliguntur, Alioquin falsa est assertio.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 54. To be justified by works and to be justified by faith working through love are sometimes opposed, namely when the works of the Law, or works meritorious before God, are here understood; otherwise the assertion is false.

units.la: Ibidem. Deus ipse non modo possibile, sed & necessarium esse dixit, ut impius per poenitentiam justificetur.
units.tr: Ibid. God himself has said that it is not only possible but also necessary that the wicked be justified through repentance.

units.la: Confess.pag.30. Via perveniendi ad vitam æternam est ob-servatio mandatorum Dei,si non quatenus per Mosem, sal-tem quatenus per Christum explicata sunt.
units.tr: Confess. p. 30. The way of attaining eternal life is the observance of God's commandments, if not insofar as they are explained through Moses, at least insofar as they are explained through Christ.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.33. Justificamur per Christum, quatenus Deus nobis per illum dat resipiscentiam, vel quod idem est, per eum nos avertit à peccatis nostris. Atque huc pertinent omnia Scriptura loca, quae docent sanguine Christi nostra peccata expiari, vel Christum esse pro nostris peccatis expiationem.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 33. We are justified through Christ, insofar as God gives us repentance through him, or, what is the same, through him turns us away from our sins. And to this pertain all the passages of Scripture which teach that our sins are expiated by the blood of Christ, or that Christ is the expiation for our sins.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.14. Nos dicimur expiare peccata nostra, cum ab iis aversi veniam eorum ex Dei liberalitate obtinemus.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 14. We are said to expiate our sins when, turned away from them, we obtain their forgiveness from God's generosity.

units.la: Catal. err. Sibr. pag.92. Fides (qua justificamur) idem est quod observatio Christianismi.
units.tr: Catal. err. Sibr. p. 92. Faith (by which we are justified) is the same thing as the observance of Christianity.

units.la: Plen.resp.sol. B.1. Hominem fide justificari, esse idem quod obserobservatione Christianismi justificare, si tantum Synecdoche hic notetur.
units.tr: Plen. resp. sol. B. 1. For a man to be justified by faith is the same as to be justified by the observance of Christianity, if only synecdoche is noted here.

units.la: A P.Bertio, Epist.ad Sibr.pag.49.& 51. Opus,si accurato examine rem pensites,duplex est,Legis & Evangelij: Opere Legis nemo salvatur, ut ante positum est, quia nemo Legem praestat. Opere vero Evangelico, quod dicitur obedientia fidei, obedientia Evangelij, quemquam salvari quis negabit, nisi qui statuit neminem credere?
units.tr: From P. Bertius, Epist. ad Sibr. p. 49 and 51. The work, if you weigh the matter with careful examination, is twofold, of the Law and of the Gospel. By works of the Law no one is saved, as was said before, because no one fulfils the Law. But by the Evangelical work, which is called "the obedience of faith" or "the obedience of the Gospel," who will deny that anyone is saved, unless he holds that no one believes?

units.la: Ibidem.pag.52. Certè si fides credentis reputatur ei in justitiam: fides autem est opus credentis, necesse est opus credentis reputari: quidquid contra afferri possit.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 52. Certainly if the faith of the believer is reckoned to him for righteousness, and faith is a work of the believer, it is necessary that the work of the believer be reckoned; whatever may be objected to this.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.54. Eadem est ratio hujus conclusiunculæ:Fi-des servat. Fides est opus. Ergo opus servat. Sed quod opus? opus Evangelij, & ut Christus loquitur, opus Dei. Item. Itaque beatus Paulus quotiescunque de operibus in causa justificationis agit, non excludit opus fidei (est enim in eo ut illud astruat) sed duntaxat opus Legis.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 54. The reasoning of this little conclusion is the same: Faith saves. Faith is a work. Therefore the work saves. But what work? The work of the Gospel, and, as Christ speaks, the work of God. Likewise: so the blessed Paul, whenever he treats of works in the cause of justification, does not exclude the work of faith (for he is in fact establishing it), but only the work of the Law.

units.la: A REMONSTR. praefat. Armin. in cap. 7. ad Rom. Tenendum hic ex Scripturis veram conversionem praestationemq; bono-rum operum esse conditionem praerequisitam ante justificationem.
units.tr: From the Remonstrants, preface to Arminius on chap. 7 to the Romans. We must hold here, from the Scriptures, that true conversion and the performance of good works is a condition required before justification.

units.la: III. Bona opera nostra praecedere nostri justificationem, non autem eam sequi.
units.tr: III. Our good works precede our justification, and do not follow it.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Catal.error.Sibr.pag.53. Pœnitentia requiritur à justificandis, tanquam conditio prævia.
units.tr: From Vorstius, Catal. error. Sibr. p. 53. Repentance is required of those to be justified as a condition that comes first.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.54. Regula illa, quam Augustinus forte primus tradidit, qua dicitur, Bona opera non praecedunt justificandum, sed sequuntur justificatum, humanitus tradita est, nusquam autem in S.literis expressa, neque admittenda est, nisi cum nomine justificationis intelligitur conversio à peccatis ad justitiam.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 54. That rule which Augustine perhaps first handed down, by which it is said that good works do not precede the one to be justified but follow the one justified, has been handed down by human authority, and is nowhere expressed in the Holy Scriptures; nor is it to be admitted, unless by the name of justification is understood conversion from sins to righteousness.

units.la: A REMONSTR.praefat.Armin.in 7. cap.ad Rom. Præstatio bo-norum operum est conditio praerequisita ante justificatio-nem.
units.tr: From the Remonstrants, preface to Arminius on chap. 7 to the Romans. The performance of good works is a condition required before justification.

units.la: IV. Vitam æternam à Deo nobis dari tantùm ut mercedem operibus nostris debitam.
units.tr: IV. Eternal life is given us by God only as a reward due to our works.

units.la: Sacra Scriptura proponit nobis vitam aeternam tantùm ut mercedem nostrae obedientiae, ut praemium certantium, & coronam justitiae.
units.tr: Holy Scripture sets before us eternal life only as the reward of our obedience, as the prize of those who strive and the crown of righteousness.

units.la: Qui negat fidelibus licere facere bona opera ex intuitu mercedis operibus nostris debita; ille naturam fidei, omnis Religionis, legislationis divinae, vitae, & mortis aeternae, pervertit & negat, Sanctorum imò & Domini nostri Iesu Christi obedientiam proscindit, & hominibus persuadet, non esse licitum ut permoveantur ad obedientiam rationibus atque argumentis ijsdem, quibus Deus in verbo suo utitur, atque etiam ipsissimum ponit fundamentum Davidianorum & Libertinorum, qui vitam aeternam negant.
units.tr: He who denies that believers may lawfully do good works with a view to the reward due to our works, perverts and denies the nature of faith, of all religion, of divine law, of life and of eternal death; he tears apart the obedience of the saints and indeed of our Lord Jesus Christ, and persuades men that it is not lawful for them to be moved to obedience by the same reasons and arguments which God uses in his Word. He even lays down the very foundation of the Davidians and Libertines, who deny eternal life.

units.la: V. Regenitos posse praestare bona opera, quae ita sint perfecta, ut nullo carnis nostrae vitio sint inquinata, neque ullis poenis digna.
units.tr: V. The regenerate can perform good works which are so perfect that they are undefiled by any fault of our flesh and worthy of no punishment.

units.la: Perpendendum est an de bonis operibus fidelium vere dicatur immunda esse instar panni menstruati, eisque competat dictum illud Esai. 64.
units.tr: It must be weighed whether the good works of the faithful are truly said to be unclean, like a menstrual rag, and whether that saying of Isaiah 64 applies to them.

units.la: Omnes justitia nostra &c.
units.tr: "All our righteousnesses," etc.

units.la: Locus Esaiae, quo fatetur inter caetera justitias suas ut pannum menstruatae esse, pernitiosa torsione corrumpitur: allegatur enim perpetuò, ac si sensus illius inferret excellentissima quaeque praestantissimorum Christianorum opera esse, ut pannum menstruatae, hoc est foeda coram facie Dei.
units.tr: The passage of Isaiah in which he confesses, among other things, that "our righteousnesses are like a menstruous rag," is corrupted by a pernicious twisting. For it is constantly cited as if its sense implied that the most excellent works of the most outstanding Christians are like a menstruous rag, that is, foul before the face of God.

units.la: Optima etiam Ethnicorum opera non possunt aliter quam dilectioni Dei & proximi conformia censeri.
units.tr: The best works of the heathen also cannot be regarded as anything other than in accordance with the love of God and of neighbour.

units.la: ARTICVLVS XXV. De abrogatione Legis Ceremonialis: & de Convenientiâ V. & N. Testamenti.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXV. On the abrogation of the Ceremonial Law, and on the agreement of the Old and New Testaments.

units.la: CRedimus omnes Ceremonias & figuras Legis, omnes denique umbras cessasse, adventu Christi, adeò ut earum quoque usus inter Christianos jam tolli atque aboleri debeat. Interim tamen manet nobis illarum veritas & substantia in Christo, in quo omnes impletæ fuerunt. Legis verò & Prophetarum testimonijs adhuc utimur, ut nos ipsos in Evangelij doctrinâ confirmemus:{1} & omnem vitam nostram honestè ad DEI gloriam juxta ipsius voluntatem, componamus{2}
units.tr: We believe that all the ceremonies and figures of the Law, and finally all the shadows, ceased with the coming of Christ, so that their use too ought now to be removed and abolished among Christians. Yet their truth and substance remain for us in Christ, in whom they were all fulfilled. We still use the testimonies of the Law and the Prophets so that we may confirm ourselves in the doctrine of the Gospel,{1} and so that we may order our whole life honourably, to the glory of God, according to his will.{2}

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this article the following is held to be taught.

units.la: 1. In V.T. nullas extare Evangelicas promissiones de vitâ æternâ: ac proinde doctrinam Evangelij non posse confirmari testimonijs Prophetarum.
units.tr: 1. In the Old Testament there are no evangelical promises of eternal life; and therefore the doctrine of the Gospel cannot be confirmed by the testimonies of the Prophets.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic.hom. Christ.[?] sol.E.6. Septimus error Evangelicorum est, quod credant vitam æternam non demùm ac primùm in N.T. sed antea quoque in V. fuisse promissam, & ex ipso DEI promissò à fidelibus ejus temporis expectatam. Quo vix quidquam potest inveniri divinis te-stimoniis, & oraculis magis contrarium. In illis siquidem, quemadmodum vitæ æternæ, à DEO hominibus ipsíque populo suo promissæ, pro eo tempore quod Christi adventum præcessit, nulla prorsus fit aperta mentio, sic apertissimè commemoratur atque inculcatur, vitam æternam demùm per IESVM Christù promissam fuisse, & per ejus Evangelium hominibus patefactam, cum ea prius apud DEVM lateret: ac denique novum fœdus in melioribus promissionibus quam vetus fuisse sancitum.
units.tr: From Welsingius, De Offic. hom. Christ. [?] sol. E.6. The seventh error of the Evangelicals is that they believe eternal life was not first and only in the New Testament, but that it was promised earlier also in the Old, and was expected from God's own promise by the faithful of that time. Yet scarcely anything can be found more contrary to the divine testimonies and oracles. For just as no open mention is made in them of eternal life as promised by God to men and to his own people for the time that preceded the coming of Christ, so it is most openly recorded and insisted upon that eternal life was at last promised through Jesus Christ, and was made known to men through his Gospel, since it had previously lain hidden with God; and finally that the new covenant was ratified with better promises than the old.

units.la: A VORSTIO, De autor. S. Script. pag. 58. Promisit Moses omnibus, Legem divinam quam ipse dedit, confervantibus, multa fœlicia in hac vita esse eventura. Ibidem. pag. 59. Nullo modo hac in parte Moses cum IESV Christo conferendus est.
units.tr: From Vorstius, De autor. S. Script. p. 58. Moses promised to all who kept the divine Law which he himself gave that many happy things would come about in this life. Ibid. p. 59. In this respect Moses is in no way to be compared with Jesus Christ.

units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Disput. de Leg. & Evang. comp. thes. 6. Discrimen inter Legem quatenus per Mosem data est, & Vetus Testamentum appellatur, & Evangelium, quà Novi Testamenti nomine venit, tertium est in materia mandatorum & pro-missionum. Promissiones enim in V. T. plærœque corporales fuerunt & terrenam hæreditatem veteri homini convenientem, spondentes: Evangelium verò continet promissionem hæreditatis cœlestis, novo homini congruentis.
units.tr: From Arminius, Disput. de Leg. & Evang. comp. thes. 6. The difference between the Law, insofar as it was given through Moses and is called the Old Testament, and the Gospel, insofar as it comes under the name of the New Testament, is a third one in the matter of commandments and promises. For the promises in the Old Testament were for the most part bodily, and promised an earthly inheritance suited to the old man; but the Gospel contains the promise of a heavenly inheritance, suited to the new man.

units.la: Ab EPISCOPIO, Disput. de Conven. & Discr. V. & N. Test. thes. 5. Secunda differentia V. & N. Test. in speciali materia promis-sionum consistit. Legis enim promissiones beatitudinem cœlestem præfigurantes, temporales & de terrena fœlicitate fuerunt. Evangelium vero, melioris spei introductio vocatur. Hebr.7.19.&8.6. promissa continere dicitur maxima & pre-tiosa 2.Pet.1.4. plenariam nimirum peccatorum remissionem, Spiritus S. copiosam donationem, vitamq; æternam aliquando in cœlo degendam.
units.tr: From Episcopius, Disput. de Conven. & Discr. V. & N. Test. thes. 5. The second difference between the Old and New Testaments consists in the special matter of the promises. For the promises of the Law, which foreshadowed heavenly blessedness, were temporal and concerned earthly happiness. The Gospel, however, is called the introduction of a better hope (Heb. 7.19; 8.6). It is said to contain the greatest and most precious promises (2 Pet. 1.4): namely, the full forgiveness of sins, the abundant gift of the Holy Spirit, and eternal life to be lived at some time in heaven.

units.la: Ibidem. thes. 20. Pactum Vetus & Novum differunt secundò, in speciali promissorum & præceptorum materia. Promisiones enim pacti cum Abrahamo initi cœlestem hære-ditatem adumbrabant, quemadmodum cap. 17. Gen. & Epist.ad Gal.cap.3.verf.17.percurrenti perspicuum esse po-test.Ibi enim promissiones Abrahamo facta tribus hisce capi-tibus comprehendi posse videntur: ut primum sit depofsi-denda terra felicissima Canaan, verf.8. Secundum de consequendo semine prater & supra natura ordinem & censum. Verf. 16.17.&c. Tertium de feminis benedictione in numero & felicitate. verf.7.& Gen.22.17.
units.tr: Ibid. thes. 20. The Old and New Covenants differ, secondly, in the special matter of promises and precepts. For the promises of the covenant made with Abraham foreshadowed the heavenly inheritance, as can be seen clearly by one who runs through Genesis 17 and Galatians 3:17. For the promises made to Abraham there seem to be comprehended under three heads: the first is the possession of the most fortunate land of Canaan (v. 8); the second is the obtaining of a seed beyond and above the order and reckoning of nature (vv. 16, 17, etc.); the third is the blessing of his descendants in number and prosperity (v. 7; and Gen. 22.17).

units.la: Ibidem. thef.21. Fideles V.T. crediderunt bona animalis hujus vita ex promisso ad se pertinere.
units.tr: Ibid. thes. 21. The faithful of the Old Testament believed that the goods of this animal life belonged to them by promise.

units.la: Disput.privat.19.de fœd.cum populo V.T. inito.thef.12. Promissiones a. pleræque V.T.carnales & terrena fuerunt. Ibidem. Disp.45.De promisis N.fœderis.thef.2. Promissa novi fœderis duum generum sunt: alia pertinent ad vitam supernaturalem tantum, alia ad naturalem hanc sive animalem etiam. Primi generis duo sunt, justitia, sive justificationis à peccatis, cui conjuncta necessario est præmij remuneratio, sive vita æterna donatio. Alterum Spiritus Sancti.
units.tr: Disput. privat. 19 de fœd. cum populo V.T. inito, thes. 12. Most of the promises of the Old Testament were carnal and earthly. Ibid. Disp. 45, De promissis N. fœderis, thes. 2. The promises of the new covenant are of two kinds: some pertain to supernatural life only, others to this natural, or even animal, life. Of the first kind there are two: righteousness, or justification from sins, which is necessarily joined with the reward of recompense, or the gift of eternal life; and the other is the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Disput.privat.13.de fœd.vet.thef. 5. Promissa vero omnia V.T. sunt carnalia & temporalia ad præsentem hanc vitam solummodo pertinentia.
units.tr: Disput. privat. 13 de fœd. vet., thes. 5. But all the promises of the Old Testament are carnal and temporal, pertaining only to this present life.

units.la: Ibidem.Disput.14. de novo fœd.thef.8. Promissa novi fœderis duo sunt, Vita æterna, quæ remissionem peccatorum & resuscitationem ex mortuis sibi præcedanea habet, & Spiritus Sancti.
units.tr: Ibid. Disput. 14 de novo fœd., thes. 8. The promises of the new covenant are two: eternal life, which has as its antecedents the forgiveness of sins and resurrection from the dead, and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: II. In novo Testamento à Christo alia perfectiora, ac præstantiora præcepta moralia esse præscripta, quam quæ tradita sunt in Lege morali à Mose & à Prophetis, ac proinde nos hodie in N.Test. non posse vitam nostram instituere secundum voluntatem DEI, si eam instituamus secundum testimonia seu præcepta moralia Legis & Prophetarum.
units.tr: II. In the New Testament Christ prescribed moral precepts that are other, more perfect and more excellent than those delivered in the moral Law by Moses and the Prophets; and therefore we today, in the New Testament, cannot order our life according to the will of God if we order it according to the testimonies or moral precepts of the Law and the Prophets.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. D.4. Alius Evangelicorum error est, quod non differant præcepta moralia N.T. à præceptis T.V. similiter moralibus, hoc est, ad mores pertinentibus. Ibidem. Ex hoc ipso errore est natus alius error quo credunt in V.T. vel jussa vel vetita fuisse, quæ tamen non fuerunt. Idcirco ita credunt, quia utrumque Testamentum eadem plane, quod ad mores attinet, præcipere ac prohibere statuunt. Et Propterea verba illa Christi, Matth.5. toties repetita, Audivistis quod dictum est antiquis, &c. Ego autem dico vobis, &c. ita interpretantur, ac si Christus Scribarum ac Pharisæorum perversas Legis Mosaicæ interpretationes reprehenderet, atque corrigeret; non autem Legi Mosaicæ quidquam adderet, eamque ad præstantiorem exactioremque formam adduceret.
units.tr: From Welsingius, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. D.4. Another error of the Evangelicals is that the moral precepts of the New Testament do not differ from the similarly moral precepts of the Old Testament, that is, those pertaining to conduct. Ibid. From this very error there arose another, by which they believe that in the Old Testament things were either commanded or forbidden which were not. They therefore believe this because they hold that both Testaments plainly enjoin and forbid the same things as far as conduct is concerned. And for this reason they interpret those words of Christ in Matthew 5, repeated so often, You have heard that it was said to the ancients, etc. But I say to you, etc., as if Christ were rebuking and correcting the perverse interpretations of the Law of Moses by the scribes and Pharisees, and were not adding anything to the Law of Moses or bringing it to a more excellent and exact form.

units.la: Ibidem. Per antiquos, non recte seniores illi intelliguntur, quorum traditiones alibi à Domino rejiciuntur, sed illi potius intelligendi sunt, quibus initio Lex Mosis in deserto tradita fuit: ac proinde non dictum est ab antiquis, sed (ut Græca dictio simpliciter sonat) dictum est antiquis, videlicet in ipsâ Lege Mosis, omninò interpretandum est.
units.tr: Ibid. By the ancients are rightly understood not those elders whose traditions are rejected by the Lord elsewhere, but rather those to whom the Law of Moses was first delivered in the wilderness. Therefore the phrase must be interpreted entirely as: not "it was said by the ancients", but (as the Greek expression plainly sounds) "it was said to the ancients", namely in the very Law of Moses.

units.la: A VORSTIO, Confess.pag.29. Quæritur, quid significet illud ἐῤῥέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις[?]? Resp. Dictum est antiquis videlicet in Lege Mosis, non dictum est ab antiquis videlicet Rabbinis: Nam Christus hoc loco sua præcepta etiam ipsi Legi, non autem Pharisæorum tantùm commentis opponit.
units.tr: From Vorstius, Confess. p. 29. It is asked what the words ἐῤῥέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις [errhethē tois archaiois] mean. Answer: "it was said to the ancients", namely in the Law of Moses; it is not "it was said by the ancients", namely by the Rabbis. For Christ in this place sets his precepts against the Law itself as well, and not merely against the inventions of the Pharisees.

units.la: Ibidem. In V.T. licita erant divortia, etiam extra casum adulterij: In N.T. autem prohibita sunt, quippe in quo major sanctimonia ac charitatis perfectio requiritur.
units.tr: Ibid. In the Old Testament divorces were lawful, even apart from the case of adultery; but in the New Testament they are forbidden, since a greater holiness and perfection of charity is required in it.

units.la: Ibidem. In V. Testam. licitum erat facile jurare in votis & promissionibus, vindictam adversus proximum expetere, extraneos & hostes populi odisse, &c. in Novo Test. ista non licent.
units.tr: Ibid. In the Old Testament it was lawful to swear easily in vows and promises, to seek vengeance against a neighbour, to hate foreigners and the enemies of the people, and so on; in the New Testament these things are not lawful.

units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Disput. de Legis & Evang. comp. thes. 6. Tertia differentia Legis & Evangelij consistit in materiâ mandatorum. Mandata enim Legis pleraque carnalia fuerunt. Evangelium vero est spirituale, mandata continens spiritualia.
units.tr: From Arminius, Disput. de Legis & Evang. comp. thes. 6. The third difference between Law and Gospel consists in the matter of the commandments. For the commandments of the Law were for the most part carnal; but the Gospel is spiritual, containing spiritual commandments.

units.la: A Sim.Episcopio, Disp.de conven. & discr.V. & N.T. thes. 28.Secunda pacti veteris & novi differentia consistit in speciali praeceptorum materia.
units.tr: Likewise from Episcopius, Disp. de conven. & discr. V. & N.T. thes. 28. The second difference between the old and new covenant consists in the special matter of the precepts.

units.la: ARTICVLVS XXVI. De intercessione CHRISTI.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXVI. On the intercession of CHRIST.

units.la: Credimus nos nullum ad Deum accessum habere, nisi tantum per unicum Mediatorem atque advocatum Iesum Christum justum, qui hanc ob causam homo factus est, & cum divina natura personaliter unitus, ut nos homines per ipsum ad divinam Majestatem accessum haberemus: alioquin nobis hic aditus erat praeclusus, [haud secus uti spinae ad ignem accedere non possunt. Nos sola ipsius voce absorpti fuissemus, sicuti in Adamo apparet, qui tremebundus a Domino profugiebat: atque in Israelitis ad montem Sinai, qui mediatorem postulabant, ex metu ne propter vocem Domini morerentur.] Hic Mediator, quem Pater inter ipsum & nos ordinavit, non debet nos propter majestatem suam deterrere, ut alium mediatorem, prout nobis visum fue-rit, rit, quæramus: nemo enim est ex omnibus creaturis in cœlo aut in terris, quæ nos impensius amet, quam Iesus Christus, qui tam-etsi esset in forma Dei, seipsum tamen exinanivit, forma servi accepta, similis factus hominibus, ac fratribus suis per omnia. [Ipse qui dives erat, nostra causa pauper factus est.] At vero si alius nobis Mediator esset quærendus, qui bene erga nos esset affectus, quem invenire possemus, qui nos magis diligat, quam qui vitam suam pro nobis posuit, etiam tunc quum essemus ipsius inimici? Sin autem nobis quærendus aliquis est, qui potentia atque autoritate valeat, quis est qui tanta polleat, quanta is qui ad dextram Dei Patris sui consedit, atque omnem autoritatem habet in cœlo & in terra? Quis est qui facilius exaudietur, quam proprius & unice dilectus filius? Sola itaque diffidentia hanc consuetudinem invexit, quod Sancti ignominia afficiantur, dum illos honorare volunt, ejusmodi illis exhibentes honorem, quem illi ipsi nunquam desiderarunt, sed semper constantissimè, prout officium etiam eorum exigebat, respuerunt, uti ex scriptis eorum patet. Neque hic prose-renrendum illud est, quod nos non simus digni: hic enim non quæritur de precibus nostris propter dignitatem nostram DEO offerendis, sed tantum propter excellentiam & dignitatem IEsv Christi, cuius justitia est nostra per fidem. Quapropter Apostolus hunc stultum metum, seu potius diffidentiam nobis eximere volens, merito nobis dicit, IE-SVM Christum fratribus suis per omnia similem esse factum, ut misericors esset & fidelis Pontifex in iis quæ apud DEVM agenda forent, ad expiandum peccata populi. Nam ex eo quod perpessus fuit, cum tentatus est, potest & iis, qui tentantur, succurrere. Et paulo post, ut in nobis tanto maiorem [ad ipsum accedendi] fiduciam accendat, addit: Habentes igitur Pontificem magnum, qui penetravit cælos, IESVM Filium DEI, teneamus hanc professionem: non enim habemus Pontificem, qui non possit affici sensu infirmitatum nostrarum, sed tentatum in omnibus similiter absque peccato.
units.tr: We believe that we have no access to God except only through the one Mediator and Advocate, Jesus Christ the righteous, who for this reason was made man and personally united with the divine nature, so that we men might have access through him to the divine Majesty. Otherwise this approach would have been closed to us [just as thorns cannot approach a fire. We would have been overwhelmed by his voice alone, as appears in Adam, who fled from the Lord in trembling, and in the Israelites at Mount Sinai, who asked for a mediator for fear that they would die because of the voice of the Lord]. This Mediator, whom the Father appointed between himself and us, should not frighten us away by his majesty, so that we seek another mediator as it may seem good to us. For there is no one among all creatures in heaven or on earth who loves us more tenderly than Jesus Christ, who, although he was in the form of God, nevertheless emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made like to men and in all things like his brethren. [Though he was rich, for our sake he became poor.] But if we had to seek another Mediator who was well disposed toward us, whom could we find who loves us more than he who laid down his life for us, even when we were his enemies? If, on the other hand, we must seek someone who has power and authority, who is as mighty as he who sat down at the right hand of God his Father and has all authority in heaven and on earth? Who is more readily heard than his own dear and only Son? Distrust alone has introduced this custom, that the saints are dishonoured while men wish to honour them, offering them a kind of honour which they themselves never desired, but always most steadfastly rejected, as their office also required, as their writings make plain. Nor must we pursue here the objection that we are not worthy. For the question here is not about offering our prayers to God on account of our own worthiness, but only on account of the excellence and worthiness of Jesus Christ, whose righteousness is ours through faith. Wherefore the Apostle, wishing to remove this foolish fear, or rather distrust, from us, rightly tells us that Jesus Christ was made like his brethren in all things, so that he might be a merciful and faithful High Priest in those things which pertain to God, to make atonement for the sins of the people. For in that he himself has suffered when tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted. And a little later, to kindle in us so much greater confidence [in approaching him], he adds: Since then we have a great High Priest who has passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our confession. For we have not a High Priest who cannot sympathize with our infirmities, but one who was tempted in all things likewise, without sin.

units.la: Accedamus igitur cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ, ut consequamur misericordiam, & gratiam inveniamus ad opportunum auxilium.
units.tr: Let us therefore draw near with confidence to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and find grace for timely help.

units.la: [Commutat hic tremendum gloriæ thro-num in thronum gratiæ, ut nos faciat ad ipsum accedere.] Idem Apostolus docet, nos habere libertatem ingrediendi sacrarium per san-guinem Iesv. Accedamus itaque, ait, cum certa per-suasione fidei, &c. Item, Christus habet perpetuum sacerdotium: Unde & servare prorsus potest eos qui per ipsum accedunt ad DEVM, semper vivens ut interpellet pro iis. Quid amplius desiderari po-terit, cum Christus ipse palam testetur, Ego sum via, veritas, & vita: Nemo potest ad Patrem venire, nisi per me? Quem in finem quaeremus alium advocatum, [cum per ipsum solum accessum habeamus ad Patrem?] Cumq; DEO placuerit nobis Filium suum dare, ut esset advocatus noster, ne illum relinquamus, ut nobis alium sumamus, vel potius ut alium quae-ramus, & nūquam inveniamus. Quum enim DEVS eum nobis donaret, probe sciebat nos esse peccatores. Quare praeceptum Christi sequentes, Patrem coelestem invoca-mus per Christum unicum Mediatorem no-strum, quemadmodum ipse nos docuit in O-ratione Dominica, certo persuasi, quidquid Patrem petierimus in ipsius nomine, nos esse idipsum impetraturos.
units.tr: [He here exchanges the dreadful throne of glory for the throne of grace, so as to make us draw near to him.] The same Apostle teaches that we have freedom to enter the sanctuary through the blood of Jesus. Let us therefore draw near, he says, with a sure assurance of faith, etc. Likewise: Christ has a perpetual priesthood. Whence also he is altogether able to save those who come to God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them. What more could be desired, since Christ himself plainly testifies, I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me? To what end, then, should we seek another advocate [since we have access to the Father through him alone]? Since it has pleased God to give us his Son to be our advocate, let us not abandon him in order to take another for ourselves, or rather to seek another and never find one. For when God gave him to us, he knew well that we were sinners. Therefore, following the command of Christ, we call upon our heavenly Father through Christ, our only Mediator, just as he himself taught us in the Lord's Prayer, being certain that whatever we ask the Father in his name, we shall obtain it.

units.la: ARTICVLVS XXVII.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXVII.

units.la: De Ecclesia Catholica.
units.tr: On the Catholic Church.

units.la: CRedimus & confitemur unicam Eccle-siam Catholicam, seu Vniversale, quæ est sancta congregatio seu cœtus omnium fidelium Christianorum, qui totam suam salutem ab uno IESV CHRISTO expectant, abluti ipsius sanguine, & per Spiritum ejus sanctificati atque obsignati. 1. Hæc porrò Ecclesia ab initio mundi fuit, & usque ad fi-nem ejus est perduratura: quemadmodū hoc vel ex eo apparet, quod Christus Rex æter-nus est, qui nunquam sine subditis esse po-test. 2. Cæterùm hanc Sanctam Ecclesiam Deus contra omnem mundi furorem & im-petum tuetur: quamvis ad aliquod tempus parva admodum, & quasi extincta in con-spectu hominum appareat: quemadmodum tempore illo periculosissimo Achabi, Deus sibi septem millia virorum reservasse dicitur, qui non flexerant genua coram Baal. Deni-que hæc Ecclesia sancta nullo est aut certo loco sita & circumscripta, aut ullis certis per-sonis sonis astricta aut alligata: sed per omnem orbem terrarum sparsa atque diffusa est, quamvis animo ac voluntate in uno eodemque spiritu, virtute fidei, tota sit simul conjuncta atque unita.
units.tr: We believe and confess one holy Catholic, or universal, Church, which is the holy congregation or assembly of all the faithful Christians, who look for their whole salvation from the one Jesus Christ, washed in his blood and sanctified and sealed by his Spirit. (1) This Church has existed from the beginning of the world and will endure until its end, as is evident from the fact that Christ is an eternal King, who can never be without subjects. (2) Moreover, God preserves this holy Church against all the rage and assault of the world, although for a time it appears very small and as if extinguished in the sight of men, just as in that most perilous time of Ahab God is said to have reserved for himself seven thousand men who had not bowed their knees before Baal. Finally, this holy Church is not situated or confined to any particular place, nor bound or tied to any particular persons, but is spread and diffused throughout the whole world, though in mind and will, in one and the same Spirit, by the power of faith, it is wholly joined and united together.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: It seems to be taught against this article.

units.la: I. Ad Ecclesiam Catholicam etiam pertinere multos, qui nullam cognitionem de Christo habent, & qui proinde salutem suam ab uno IESV Christo non expectant.
units.tr: I. Many who have no knowledge of Christ also belong to the Catholic Church, and so do not expect their salvation from Jesus Christ alone.

units.la: A VENATORE, Declar.pag.168. Credo Ecclesiam esse coetum evocatum ad audiendum ea quae divina & spiritualia sunt, & quae ad salutem pertinent: seu esse societatem, & multitudinem, evocatam & congregatam ad intelligendam & exercendam unam aliquam religionem.
units.tr: From VENATOR, Declar. p. 168. I believe the Church is an assembly called together to hear the things that are divine and spiritual and pertain to salvation; or it is a society and multitude called together and gathered to understand and practise one religion.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.183. Salus non alligatur cognitioni historiae de Christi passione & morte.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 183. Salvation is not bound to knowledge of the history of Christ's passion and death.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.184. Multi probi Ethnici illustria habuerunt testimonia internae & spiritualis veri cultus divini.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 184. Many upright heathens have had illustrious testimonies of the inward and spiritual true worship of God.

units.la: Contra Pasl.[?] Dord.pag.130. Nego absolute & sine exceptione esse necessarium, ut omnes illi qui salutis per Christum participes futuri sunt, intelligere debeant, quaecunque de ipso Evangelistae & Apostoli praedicarunt & scripserunt.
units.tr: Against Pasl.[?] Dord. p. 130. I deny absolutely and without exception that all those who are to partake of salvation through Christ must understand whatever the Evangelists and Apostles preached and wrote about him.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.134. Cur igitur me oporteret tam esse severum, ut miseros Ethnicos, quibus hae manifestationes & tam claras doctrinas, quas Apostoli habuerunt, ne in minimo quidem factae sunt, & quibus ne verbum quidem de Christo manifestatum est, & tamen vitam piam duxerunt, (hoc enim est quod simul intelligi semper volo) condemnarem, & crederem DEVM cum ipsdem secundum rigorem acturum, atq; ipsis ita immisericordem futurum. Cur sentire debeQ​m, DEUM esse ab aliquo plus postulaturum, quam quod ipsi dedit? Cui parum datum est, an ab ipso plus quam illud parum exigetur? Nequeo concipere quænam ibi foret justitiæ proportio.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 134. Why then should I be so severe as to condemn the wretched heathens, to whom these manifestations and such clear doctrines as the Apostles had were not made known even in the smallest degree, and to whom not even a word about Christ was revealed, yet who led a pious life (for this is what I always want to be understood along with it), and to believe that God will deal with them according to strict justice and be so unmerciful to them? Why should I think that God will require more from anyone than he has given him? If little has been given to someone, will more than that little be exacted from him? I cannot conceive what proportion of justice there would be in that.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.135. Posse homines sine plena fide historiæ de Christo servari, etiam postquam fides Christiana ei revelata est, intelligi facile potest, si examen instituamus quantam cognitionem adulti singuli inter Christianos habeant.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 135. That men can be saved without a full faith in the history of Christ, even after the Christian faith has been revealed to them, can easily be understood if we examine how much knowledge individual adults among Christians actually have.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 137. Dico Ethnicos talem habuisse fidem, qualis postulatur, scilicet, DEUM esse, & præmia largiri ijs qui ipsum diligunt. Imo purum & sincerum divinum cultum animarum docuerunt. Quinimo excepto eo quod historiam de Christo ignorarunt, DEUS illustria testimonia veritatis, accepti cultus divini, atque etiam veræ dilectionis DEI & proximi, inter ipsos, saltem inter multos, distribuit.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 137. I say that the heathens had such faith as is required, namely, that God exists and bestows rewards on those who love him. Indeed, they taught pure and sincere divine worship of the soul. Moreover, apart from their ignorance of the history of Christ, God has distributed among them, at least among many, illustrious testimonies of truth, accepted divine worship, and also of true love of God and of neighbour.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.138. Nego hanc propositionem, Nemo potest, salvus fieri, qui Christo per veram fidem non est insitus.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 138. I deny this proposition: No one can be saved who has not been grafted into Christ by true faith.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.141. Credo multos fide de historia Christi præditos Christum nunquam induisse, & contra multos Christum induisse, atque in se habuisse, qui ejusmodi plenam de historia Christi cognitionem non habuerunt.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 141. I believe that many endowed with faith in the history of Christ have never put on Christ, and on the contrary that many have put on Christ and had him within themselves who did not have such full knowledge of the history of Christ.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 145. DEUS Ethnicis poterit respondere, etsi per-mitto ut ad lucem Lunæ, aut stellarum ambuldetis, tantum tamen lucis habetis, ut viam vestram ambulare possitis.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 145. God may answer the heathens: although I allow you to walk by the light of the moon or the stars, you still have enough light to walk your way.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.147. Quamvis simplex carentia historiæ de Christo non necessario condemnet, tamen Religio Christiana admodum utilis est, & quando DEUS eam manifestari & credi vult, plane necessaria.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 147. Although a mere lack of the history of Christ does not necessarily condemn, nevertheless the Christian religion is very useful, and when God wishes it to be made known and believed, it is plainly necessary.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.148. Quamvis Ethnici infernali igne non punirentur, tamen Christiani majorem gloriam in regno cælorum possent habere, quam ipsi, cum Theologi fere omnes docent ibi diversos fore gloriæ gradus.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 148. Although the heathens would not be punished with infernal fire, Christians could nevertheless have greater glory in the kingdom of heaven than they, since almost all theologians teach that there will be different degrees of glory there.

units.la: II. Totam atque universam Ecclesiam in terris deficere posse: neque necesse esse ut Christus Rex & caput Ecclesiæ semper Ecclesiam aliquam veram in terris habeat.
units.tr: II. That the whole and entire Church can fail on earth, and that it is not necessary for Christ, the King and head of the Church, always to have some true Church on earth.

units.la: Ab EPISCOPIO, Disput.priv.de Eccl.thes,10. Addimus, quod tamen ex eo [scilicet Ecclesiam quamlibet deficere posse] necessario sequitur, totam & universam Ecclesiam in terris deficere posse.
units.tr: From EPISCOPIUS, Private disputation on the Church, thesis 10. We add that, however, from this [namely, that any Church may fail] it necessarily follows that the whole and entire Church can fail on earth.

units.la: Ibidem.thes.11. Neque vero necesse esse credimus adhoc, ut Christus Rex & caput maneat, in terris Ecclesiam aliquam veram semper esse.
units.tr: Ibid. thesis 11. Nor do we believe it necessary, in order for Christ to remain King and head, that there always be some true Church on earth.

units.la: ARTICULUS XXVIII. De communione Sanctorum cum verâ Ecclesiâ.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXVIII. On the communion of the saints with the true Church.

units.la: CRedimus quòd cum sanctus hic coetus & congregatio sit eorum qui servari debent: & salus nulla sit extra eam; neminem cujuscunque dignitatis aut nominis is fuerit, sese ab eâ subducere aut segregare debere, ut sua tantum consuetudine contentus, solus ac separatim vivat. Sed omnes ac singulos teneri huic coetui se adjungere atque uniri, Ecclesiæ unitatem sollicitè conservare, sesèq; illius tum doctrinæ, tum disciplinæ subjicere, collum denique Christi jugo sponte subjicere, ac tanquam communia ejusdem corporis membra ædifiædificationi fratrum inservire, prout DEUS unicuiq; sua dona fuerit largitus. Porrò ut hæc melius observentur, omnium fidelium partes sunt, sese juxta DEI verbum ab ijs o-mnibus disiungere, qui sunt extra Ecclesiam constituti, huicque fidelium cœtui ac congregationi se adjungere, ubicunque illam DEUS constituerit: etsi id contraria Principum vel Magistratuum edicta prohibeant, indicta etiam in eos capitis & mortis corporeæ poena, qui id fecerint. Quicunque igitur à vera illa Ecclesia recedunt, aut se illi aggregare recusant, aperte DEI mandato repugnant.
units.tr: We believe that since this holy assembly and congregation consists of those who are to be saved, and there is no salvation outside it, no one, of whatever dignity or name, ought to withdraw or separate himself from it, so as to live alone and apart, content with his own company only. Rather, all and each are bound to join and unite themselves to this assembly, carefully to preserve the unity of the Church, to submit themselves both to its doctrine and its discipline, finally to place their neck willingly under the yoke of Christ, and, as common members of the same body, to serve the edification of the brothers, as God has bestowed his gifts on each. Furthermore, so that these things may be better observed, it is the duty of all the faithful, according to the word of God, to separate themselves from all those who are placed outside the Church, and to join this assembly and congregation of the faithful wherever God has established it, even though the edicts of princes or magistrates forbid this, with the penalty of bodily death declared against those who do so. Whoever therefore withdraws from that true Church, or refuses to join it, openly opposes the command of God.

units.la: ARTICULUS XXIX. De Notis veræ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXIX. On the Marks of the True Church.

units.la: CRedimus summa tum diligentia, tum prudentia, ex verbo DEI esse inquirendum ac discernendum, quænam sit illa vera Ecclesia: quandoquidem omnes sectæ, quotquot hodie in mundo vigent, Ecclesiæ titulum nomenque usurpant atque præte-xunt. xunt. Nequaquam verò de hypocritarum coetu nunc loquimur, qui bonis in Ecclesiâ sunt permisti, [& simul hoc Ecclesiæ titulo sunt tecti, ] sed ad Ecclesiam proprie non pertineant, licet in eâ corpore præsentes sint: sed de distinguendâ veræ Ecclesiæ congregatione ab omnibus aliis sectis, quæ se Ecclesiæ memb a esse falsò gloriantur. Notæ quibus vera Ecclesia à falsâ discernitur, hæ sunt: 1. Si Ecclesia utatur purâ Evangelij prædicatione, & sincerâ Sacramentorum administratione, secundum Christi institutionem: si Disciplina Ecclesiastica rectè utatur ad corrigenda vitia: 2. si denique (ut uno verbo cuncta complectamur) ad normam verbi DEI omnia exigat, & quæcunq; huic adversantur, repudiet: Christumq; unicum caput agnoscat. Hisce notis certum est veram Ecclesiam dignosci posse, à qua fas non sit quemquam disiungi. Quæ autem sint veræ hujus Ecclesiæ vera membra ex communibus Christianorum omnium notis poterit judicari, qualis est Fides; atque hinc cognoscuntur, quod Christum unicum Servatorem fide apprehendant, peccatum fugiant iustitiam consectentur: verum etiam DEUM & proximum diligant, neque ad dextram neque ad sinistram deflectentes, carnemque suam cū ipsius operibus crucifigentes:quod quidem ita minime est intelligendum, quasi nulla amplius in illis sit infirmitas, sed quod adversus eam per omne vitæ tempus virtute Spiritus pugnent, confugientes semper ad sanguinem, mortem, passionem,& obedientiam Domini nostri IESU Christi,in quo solo remissionem peccatorum suorum habent, per fidem in ipsum. Quod ad falsam vero attinet Ecclesiam, illa sibi suisque institutis & traditionibus plus semper autoritatis attribuit, quam verbo DEI: illa Christi jugo se subjici recusat; illa Sacramenta non administrat prout Christus in verbo suo præscripsit: sed illis pro arbitrio modo addit aliquid, modo detrahit. Præterea hominibus illa semper plus quam Christo nititur, eósque qui sancte ex præscripto verbi DEI vitam suam componere student, quíque vitia illius, atque imprimis avaritiam & idolomanias taxant, ac reprehendunt, hostiliter persequuntur. Ex his igitur facile est utramque Ecclesiam agnoscere atque à se invicem discernere.
units.tr: We believe, with the greatest care and prudence, that it must be sought out and distinguished from the Word of God which church is the true one, since all the sects that flourish in the world today usurp and pretend to the title and name of Church. We are not speaking here of the assembly of hypocrites, who are mingled with the good in the Church and are covered by its title, but who do not truly belong to the Church even though they are present in it bodily. Our concern is to distinguish the true congregation of the Church from all the other sects, which falsely boast that they are members of the Church. The marks by which the true Church is distinguished from the false are these: (1) if the Church uses the pure preaching of the Gospel and the sincere administration of the sacraments according to Christ's institution, and if it rightly uses church discipline to correct vices; (2) and finally, to sum up everything in one word, if it directs all things by the rule of the Word of God and rejects whatever opposes it, and acknowledges Christ as its only head. By these marks it is certain that the true Church can be recognised, and no one may lawfully separate from it. The true members of this Church may be judged from the common marks of all Christians, such as faith; and they are known by this, that they lay hold of Christ alone as Saviour by faith, flee from sin, pursue righteousness, and love God and their neighbour, not turning aside to the right or to the left, and crucifying their flesh with its works. This is not to be understood as if there were no weakness left in them, but that they fight against it by the power of the Spirit throughout the whole of life, always taking refuge in the blood, death, passion and obedience of our Lord Jesus Christ, in whom alone they have the forgiveness of their sins through faith in him. As for the false Church, it always attributes more authority to itself and its own institutions and traditions than to the Word of God; it refuses to submit to the yoke of Christ; it does not administer the sacraments as Christ prescribed in his Word, but at its own pleasure now adds something to them, now takes something away. Moreover, it always leans on men more than on Christ, and it persecutes with hostility those who study to order their lives holily according to the prescription of the Word of God, and who censure and rebuke its vices, above all its covetousness and idolatries. From these things it is therefore easy to recognise each Church and to distinguish one from the other.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this article the following is taught.

units.la: I. Nullas notas dari posse, aut ut dentur opus esse, per quas in cognitionem verae Ecclesiae perveniatur.
units.tr: I. That no marks can be given by which one may come to the knowledge of the true Church, or that, if they are given, there is no need of them.

units.la: AB EPISCOPIO, Disput. priv. de Notis Eccl. Thes. 2. Cum nota omnis semper notior esse debeat ea re, cujus nota est, & ad quam tanquam obscuram & ignotam notificandam adhibetur: ei vero, qui, quae doctrina salutaris sit, recte intelligit, nihil omnino deest, quo Ecclesia cognosci queat. relinquitur etiam nullas notas dari posse, aut ut dantur opus esse, per quas in cognitionem Ecclesiae veniatur.
units.tr: FROM EPISCOPIUS, private disputation on the marks of the Church, Thes. 2. Since every mark ought always to be better known than the thing of which it is the mark, and is used to make known what is obscure and unknown, and since nothing at all is lacking to the person who rightly understands what saving doctrine is, by which the Church may be recognised, it follows that no marks can be given by which one may come to the knowledge of the Church, or, if they are given, there is no need of them.

units.la: Ibidem. Thes. 5. Ullas esse circumstantias per quas tanquam notas in verae Ecclesiae certam & infallibilem cognitionem deveniatur, impossibile esse statuimus.
units.tr: Ibidem. Thes. 5. We hold it to be impossible that there are any circumstances as marks by which one may arrive at a certain and infallible knowledge of the true Church.

units.la: Ibidem. Thes. 6. Imò quod magis est hanc ipsam de certis & infallibilibus Notis, extra hanc Doctrinae salutaris professionem, assignandis quaestionem, praecipuum gradum fuisse credimus, per quem & verae Ecclesiae, sive salutaris doctrinae solida cognitio deturbata, & Antichristi solium evectum atque exaltatum, quinimò pura veritatis ignorantia introducta est, adferere[?] non dubitamus.
units.tr: Ibidem. Thes. 6. Indeed, what is worse, we believe that this very question of assigning certain and infallible marks apart from the profession of this saving doctrine was the chief step by which the solid knowledge of the true Church, or of saving doctrine, was overthrown, the throne of Antichrist was raised up and exalted, and even a complete ignorance of the truth was introduced; and we do not hesitate to assert this.

units.la: II. Notas verae Ecclesiae non esse puram praedicationem Verbi divini, sinceram Sacramentorum administrationem, & Disciplinae Ecclesiasticae legitimum usum, sed si nota aliqua est statuenda, eam esse unam, scilicet salutaris doctrinae professionem, ad quam pura verbi divini praedi-catio non pertineat.
units.tr: II. That the marks of the true Church are not the pure preaching of the divine Word, the sincere administration of the sacraments, and the lawful use of church discipline; but if some mark is to be set down, it is one only, namely the profession of saving doctrine, to which the pure preaching of the divine Word does not belong.

units.la: AB EPISCOPIO, Disput. priv. de Not. Eccl. Thes. 8. Quod si quae tamen Ecclesiae nota statuenda est, ea alia esse non potest, quam una salutaris doctrinae professio.
units.tr: FROM EPISCOPIUS, private disputation on the marks of the Church, Thes. 8. But if any mark of the Church is to be set down, it cannot be any other than the one profession of saving doctrine.

units.la: Ibidem.Thes.11.Ad hanc salutaris doctrinæ professionem] non pertinet prædicatio verbi divini,quippe quæ Pastoris actio potius quam Ecclesiæ est, & non tam necessaria, quam utilis est ad ædificationem illius, postquam Scriptura omnibus & singulis legenda data est, ut ex suopte marte discat quisque quantum satis est.
units.tr: Ibidem. Thes. 11. The preaching of the divine Word does not belong to this profession of saving doctrine, since it is rather the action of the minister than of the Church, and is not so much necessary as useful for its edification, once Scripture has been given to all and each to be read, so that each may learn for himself as much as is enough.

units.la: A VENATORE,Declar.pag.170.Qui DEVM & Christum confitetur, & ejus vocem audit, & de fidei dogmatibus paratus est confiteri & sentire quæ de iis rotunde Scriptura loquitur,etsi necpossit nec velit recipere, quod ab his aut illis Conciliis, Synodis, Patribus, & Ecclesiis forte fit decretum, ut utatur his aut illis verbis aut phrasibus,in quocunque etiam fuerit fidei dogmate, quæ plerumque per curiositatem hominum sunt inventæ, & causæ acerborum schismatum, & horribilium persecutionum ac cædium inter Christianos fuerunt, sed qui dicit: Verba, quibus ipse Christus usus est, mihi sufficiunt, ego ea emendare non possum, atque etiam credo te non esse Præceptore tuo sapientiorem ad describendas res spirituales: quis talem virum non agnosceret pro membro Ecclesiæ? & talem cœtum pro Ecclesiâ?
units.tr: FROM VENATOR, Declaration, p. 170. One who confesses God and Christ, and hears his voice, and is ready to confess and to hold what Scripture speaks of plainly concerning the doctrines of faith, but who cannot and will not accept whatever has perhaps been decreed by this or that council, synod, father or church, that one should use this or that word or phrase, in whatever doctrine of faith it may be, which for the most part have been invented through men's curiosity and have been the causes of bitter schisms and dreadful persecutions and slaughters among Christians; but who says: "The words which Christ himself used are enough for me; I cannot improve them, and I also believe that you are no wiser than your Teacher in describing spiritual things": who would not acknowledge such a man as a member of the Church? And such an assembly as a Church?

units.la: Ibidem.Nullum est convenientius medium ad diminuendas sectas, atque ut omnes Christiani in unam Ecclesiam, in fraterna unitate, colligi possint: quam ut singuli phrases in dogmatibus fidei vel à se inventas, aut ab aliis confictas, à se autem receptas, omittant, & ut unusquisque in sensu suo abundet, explicationes, descriptiones & sensus [verborum Scripturæ]sibi servando.
units.tr: Ibidem. There is no more suitable means of diminishing sects, and of allowing all Christians to be gathered into one Church in fraternal unity, than that each should omit the phrases in matters of faith which he has either invented himself or has borrowed from others and accepted, and that each should abound in his own sense, reserving to himself explanations, descriptions and meanings [of the words of Scripture].

units.la: ARTICULUS XXX. De Regimine Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXX. On the Government of the Church.

units.la: Credimus veram hanc Ecclesiam debere regi ac gubernari spirituali illa politia, 1. quam nos Deus ipso verbo suo edocuit: nimirum ut sint in ea Pastores ac Ministri, qui purè & concionentur & Sacramenta administrent 2. Sint quoque Seniores & Diaconi, qui Presbyterium, seu Ecclesiæ Senatum constituant 3. ut his veluti medijs vera Religio conservari, veraque doctrina passim propagari & retineri possit: hominesque vitijs dediti spiritualiter corripi & emendari, ac veluti fræno quodam Disciplinæ cohiberi: pauperes item & afflicti auxilio & consolatione pro cujusque necessitate sublevari possint. Tunc enim omnia rite & ordine fient in Ecclesiâ, cum viri fideles ac pij ad ejus gubernationem deligentur, juxta D. Pauli præscriptum, quod habetur.1.Tim.3·& Tit.1.
units.tr: We believe that this true Church ought to be ruled and governed by that spiritual polity (1) which God himself has taught us in his Word: namely, that there should be in it pastors and ministers who preach purely and administer the sacraments; (2) there should also be elders and deacons, who constitute the presbytery, or senate of the Church; (3) so that by these, as it were, middle agents, true religion may be preserved, sound doctrine spread and retained everywhere, and men given over to vices may be spiritually rebuked and corrected and restrained as with a kind of bridle of discipline. Likewise the poor and afflicted may be relieved with help and comfort according to each one's need. For then all things will be done properly and in order in the Church, when faithful and godly men are chosen for its government, according to the prescription of St. Paul, which is found in 1 Tim. 3 and Titus 1.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this Article the following seems to be taught.

units.la: I. Regimen Ecclesiæ non pertinere ad Pastores, Seniores, & Diaconos, sed ad Magistratum, si Christianus est.
units.tr: I. The government of the Church does not belong to the pastors, elders, and deacons, but to the magistrate, if he is a Christian.

units.la: A Ioan. Wtenbogardo, De Offic. Christ. Magistr. in Eccl. pag.84. Oportet itaque Christianum Magistratum necessario agnoscere pro Magistratu sub Christo, etiam in Ecclesia, & in rebus ad Ecclesiam spectantibus, ad eam regendam ac gubernandam secundum verbum ejus.
units.tr: From Johannes Wtenbogaert, On the Office of the Christian Magistrate in the Church, p. 84. Therefore the Christian magistrate must necessarily acknowledge that he is a magistrate under Christ, also in the Church and in matters pertaining to the Church, to rule and govern it according to his Word.

units.la: A Casp. Barlæo, Dissert.pag.14. Tantum abest ut Principibus summa in Ecclesiæ negotijs iuris dicundi potestas denegari merito debeat, ut plerique veterum, tum in Dei populo ante Mosis & Aaronis tempora, tum etiam apud gentiles duo hæc munera conjuncta habuerint, Sacerdotium inquam & Regnum. In Melchisedeco res plana est, & quæ regni cuiusdam habebant speciem, in Patriarcharum familijs. Inter Ethnicos Diotogenes Pythagoricus tria in legitimo Rege requirit, ut belli dux sit, ut judex, ut sacerdos. Augustus pontificatum maximum imperio adjunxit, eumque secuti Principes idem fecere.
units.tr: From Caspar Barlaeus, Dissertation, p. 14. So far is it from being rightly denied to princes that they should have supreme judicial power in church affairs, that most of the ancients, both among God's people before the times of Moses and Aaron and also among the Gentiles, held these two offices joined together, I mean the priesthood and the kingship. In Melchizedek the matter is plain, and those in the families of the patriarchs had the appearance of a kind of kingship. Among the heathen, Diotogenes the Pythagorean requires three things in a lawful king: that he be a leader in war, a judge, and a priest. Augustus joined the highest pontificate to the empire, and the princes who followed him did the same.

units.la: A Sim. Episcopio, Disput.de jure Magistr.Thes.11. Magistratus non simpliciter opus habet consilio ipsorum, quibus sacrorum administratio demandata est, in conficiendis decretis suis, aut in ijs roborandis & stabiliendis autoritate, cum sufficienter à Scriptura consilijs instructus, & plenaria potestate, quâ omnia solus, quando vult, exequi potest, desuper à Deo donatus sit.
units.tr: From Simon Episcopius, Disputation on the Right of the Magistrate, Thesis 11. The magistrate does not simply need the counsel of those to whom the administration of sacred things has been entrusted, in drawing up his decrees, or in confirming and establishing them by authority, since he has been sufficiently instructed by Scripture and endowed by God from above with full power, by which he alone can carry out all things whenever he wishes.

units.la: II. Administrationem Sacramentorum non pertinere ad solos Pastores, sed licere etiam cuilibet privato ea administrare.
units.tr: II. The administration of the sacraments does not belong to the pastors alone, but any private person may also be permitted to administer them.

units.la: Ab Episcop. in Disput.publ.14.Iul.1618. Hæc est mea sententia, licere etiam cuilibet privato Christiano administrare Cœnam Dominicam.
units.tr: From Episcopius, in a public disputation, 14 July 1618. This is my opinion: that any private Christian may also be permitted to administer the Lord's Supper.

units.la: III. Ecclesiam non debere regi per tales Presbyteros, seu Seniores, quales hodie sunt in Reformatis Ecclesijs Belgicis, qui in verbo non laborant.
units.tr: III. The Church ought not to be governed by such elders, or seniors, as exist today in the Reformed Churches of Belgium, who do not labour in the Word.

units.la: Ab HVG. GROTIO, Pietat. Ord. Holl. pag. 88. Presbyteri autem isti (ne quis antiquitatis magis quam moris nostri ignarus in eâ voce hallucinetur) non sunt qui verbum DEI prædicant, aut Sacramenta exhibent, sed pauci numero delecti ex populo, Pastorum συνέδροι[?], qui unâ cum Pastoribus Ecclesiam regunt. Ibidem. pag. 112. Pastores ac Presbyteri ipsi debebunt saltem συνέδρους[?] illos suos, quos Presbyteros vocant, utpote suum εὔχημα, eligere.
units.tr: From Hugo Grotius, Piety of the Order of Holland, p. 88. Now these presbyters (lest anyone, more ignorant of antiquity than of our custom, be misled by that word) are not those who proclaim the Word of God or administer the sacraments, but a few men chosen in small number from the people, the fellow-councillors [συνέδροι] of the pastors, who together with the pastors rule the Church. Ibid., p. 112. The pastors and the presbyters themselves ought at least to choose those fellow-councillors [συνέδρους] of theirs, whom they call presbyters, as their own boast [εὔχημα].

units.la: ARTICULUS XXXI. De vocatione Ministrorum Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXXI. On the calling of the ministers of the Church.

units.la: CRedimus Ministros, Seniores, & Diaconos debere ad functiones illas suas vocari & promoveri legitimâ Ecclesiæ vocatione 1. adhibita ad eam seriâ DEI invocatione, [atque adhibitis Ecclesiæ suffragijs, ac postea confirmari in muneribus suis per impositionem manuū ] eo ordine & modo, qui nobis in verbo DEI præscribitur. Debent autem imprimis singuli cavere ne illicitis mediis sese ad hæc munia ingerant. Expectandum est enim omnibus, donec a Deo ipso vocentur, ut certum habeant vocationis suæ testimonium, sciantque eam esse a Domino. Cæterum omnes verbi DEI Ministri, ubicunque sint locorum, eandem habent omnes atque æqualem tum potestatem, tum auctoritatem, ut qui sint æque omnes Christi unici illius Episcopi universalis & capitis Ecclesiæ Ministri. [Ac proinde nulla Ecclesia habet autoritatem ullam, sive dominium in alteram, ut illi dominetur.] Porro ne sancta hæc DEI ordinatio, aut violetur aut abeat in contemptum, debent omnes de verbi Ministris & Senioribus Ecclesiæ, propter opus cui incumbunt, honorifice sentire, atque cum iis pacem colere: & a rixis ac contentionibus, quantum fieri potest, invicem abstinere.
units.tr: We believe that ministers, elders, and deacons ought to be called and promoted to those their functions by a lawful calling of the Church, (1) with serious invocation of God for this purpose [and with the votes of the Church added, and afterwards they are to be confirmed in their offices by the laying on of hands], in the order and manner which is prescribed to us in the Word of God. Each person, above all, must take care not to thrust himself into these offices by unlawful means. For everyone must wait until he is called by God himself, so that he may have a certain testimony of his calling and know that it is from the Lord. Moreover, all ministers of the Word of God, wherever they are in place, have one and the same, equal power and authority, since all are equally ministers of Christ, that single universal Bishop and head of the Church. [And therefore no Church has any authority or lordship over another, so as to rule over it.] Furthermore, lest this holy ordinance of God be violated or fall into contempt, all should think honourably of the ministers of the Word and the elders of the Church because of the work to which they are devoted, and should cultivate peace with them, and, as far as possible, abstain from quarrels and contentions with one another.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this Article the following seems to be taught.

units.la: 1. Ministros verbi Dei, Seniores, & Diaconos non debere eligi ab Ecclesia, sed a Magistratu.
units.tr: 1. The ministers of the Word of God, the elders, and the deacons ought not to be chosen by the Church, but by the magistrate.

units.la: Joan. WTENBOGARDO, De Offic. Christ. Mag. in Eccl. pag. 92. Officium Magistratus in regimine Ecclesiæ speciatim se extendere ad votationem atque institutionem Mi-nistrorum Verbi, & reliquorum ministeriorum Ecclesiasticorum, probatur ex exemplis Mosis, qui quâ Magistratus, Aaronem & filium ejus Eleazarum constituit sacerdotes: & Salomonis, qui Abjatharum removit à sacerdotio, & Sadokum in ejus locum substituit.
units.tr: Johannes Wtenbogaert, On the Office of the Christian Magistrate in the Church, p. 92. That the office of the magistrate in the government of the Church extends specifically to the voting for and appointment of the ministers of the Word and of the other ecclesiastical ministries, is proved from the examples of Moses, who as magistrate appointed Aaron and his son Eleazar as priests, and of Solomon, who removed Abiathar from the priesthood and substituted Zadok in his place.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.94. Quod in Novo Testamento post Apostolos, Evangelistas, & Prophetas, postea Pastores & Doctores vocati & constituti fuerunt per suffragia Ecclesiæ Chri-stiana,& impositionem manuum Presbyterij, ita ut Magistratus eo tempore in hoc negotio nullæ fuerint partes, factum fuit quoniam Ecclesiæ tunc sub cruce erant, & à Magistratu non tantum protegebantur, sed etiam persecutionibus gravabantur:inde sequi Magistratum, Christum ejusque ve-ritatem jam amplectentem, in vocatione Ministrorum nullas habere partes, verè & sine magnis absurditatibus dici non potest.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 94. Since in the New Testament, after the Apostles, Evangelists, and Prophets, pastors and teachers were afterwards called and appointed by the votes of the Christian Church and the laying on of hands of the presbytery, so that the magistrate had no part in this business at that time, because the Churches were then under the cross, and were not only protected by the magistrate but also burdened with persecutions: it cannot be truly and without great absurdities said that it follows that the magistrate, now embracing Christ and his truth, has no part in the calling of ministers.

units.la: II. Ministros Verbi DEI non debere esse aequalis potestatis atque autoritatis.
units.tr: II. The ministers of the Word of God ought not to have equal power and authority.

units.la: Ab Hyg. Grotio, Pietat. Ord. Holl. pag. 118. Infirmitatem hanc Puritani putant esse magnam, quod Ecclesiæ regantur per Episcopos. Quid boni multi in nostra Eccle-sia regimine desiderent, quibus modis putent vitia ad ἀναλο-γίαν[?] accedentia commodissimè posse sanari, differere hic non instituì. Neque tamen me contineo, quin fontem & originem tum hujus, tum aliarum πλημμελειῶν indicem. Existimamus tanto nos puriores fore, quanto longius ab omnibus Ecclesia Romana institutis recesserimus: nullo discrimine: neque volumus animadvertere inter multos illius corporis morbos aliquas tamen mansisse Saniorù ævi reliquias.Excesit medicina modum.
units.tr: From Hugo Grotius, Piety of the Order of Holland, p. 118. The Puritans think this weakness is great, that the Churches are ruled by bishops. I do not here undertake to discuss what good many desire in the government of our Church, or by what means they think the faults that depart from due proportion [ἀναλογίαν] can most conveniently be healed. Yet I do not restrain myself from indicating the source and origin both of this and of other faults [πλημμελειῶν]. We think we shall be the purer the further we have withdrawn from all the institutions of the Roman Church, with no distinction made: nor do we wish to notice, among the many diseases of that body, that some remnants of a more wholesome age have nevertheless remained. The remedy has exceeded the measure.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 120. In Synodo Emdanâ multa Ministri de regendis Ecclesijs decrevere. Primum caput est, Ne Ec-clesia una in alteram dominatum exerceat, imò ut omnes à su-spicione quavis & occasione dominatus sibi caveant. Quanquam autem Episcopalis eminentia dominatus non est, his tamen vocibus eam indicari satis manifestum est. Item. Imò vero quot fuere Synodi, toties illis ipsis Emdanæ Synodi verbis stabilita est ἰσοτιμία.[?]
units.tr: Ibid., p. 120. In the Synod of Emden the ministers decreed many things about the governing of Churches. The first chapter is: that one Church should not exercise domination over another, but rather that all should guard themselves against any suspicion or occasion of domination. Although the eminence of a bishop is not domination, it is quite clear that it is indicated by these words. Likewise: indeed, as often as there were synods, equality of honour [ἰσοτιμία] was established by those very words of the Synod of Emden.

units.la: ARTICULUS XXXII. De Potestate Ecclesiæ in condendis Legibus Ecclesiasticis, & in administranda Disciplina.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXXII. On the Power of the Church in Enacting Ecclesiastical Laws and in Administering Discipline.

units.la: INterim credimus quamvis utile quidem sit, ut Gubernatores, qui Ecclesijs præ-sunt, aliquem inter se ordinem constituant, ad conservationem corporis Ecclesiæ, 1. tamen studiosè cavere eos debere, ne quo pacto ab ijs deflectant, declinentve, quæ Christus ipse, unicus Magister noster semel constituit. Quapropter rejicimus omnia humana inventa, omnésque leges, quæ ad DEI cultum sunt introductæ, ut ijs conscientiæ ullo modo illaqueentur, aut obstringantur. Recipimus itaque eas solas, quæ idoneæ sunt vel ad fovendam, alendámque concordiam, vel ad nos in DEI obedientiâ retinen-dos. dos. Ad id verò imprimis necessaria est Excommunicatio, ex præcepto verbi Dei usurpata: & aliæ illi annexæ disciplinæ Ecclesiasti-cæ appendices.
units.tr: Meanwhile we believe that, although it is indeed useful for those who govern the churches to establish some order among themselves for the preservation of the body of the Church, they must nevertheless take careful heed that they do not in any way turn aside or depart from those things which Christ himself, our only Teacher, established once for all. Therefore we reject all human inventions, and all laws introduced for the worship of God, if consciences are in any way to be ensnared or bound by them. We accept, then, only those laws which are suited either to foster and nourish concord or to keep us in obedience to God. Above all, for this purpose excommunication, practised according to the precept of God's Word, is necessary, together with the other ecclesiastical disciplinary measures attached to it.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this article the following is seen to be taught.

units.la: I. Non ad Gubernatorum, qui Ecclesiis præsunt, sed ad Magistratus munus pertinere, ordinem constituere ad conservationem corporis Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: I. That it belongs not to those who govern the churches, but to the office of the magistrate, to establish order for the preservation of the body of the Church.

units.la: AIOAN.WTENBOGARDO, De Offic.Mag.in Eccl.pag.68. Officium Magistratus in regimine Ecclesiæ speciatim se etiam extendit ad condendum leges & Constitutiones Ecclesiasticas. Ibidem.pag.99. Potestatem leges Ecclesiasticas condendi, figendi, & refigendi ad Magistratum pertinere docent exempla piorum Regum, Davidis, Solomonis, Ezechiæ, Iosiæ, & aliorum.
units.tr: Johannes Wtenbogaert, On the Office of the Magistrate in the Church, p. 68. The office of the magistrate in the governing of the Church extends in particular to enacting laws and ecclesiastical constitutions. Ibid., p. 99. Examples of pious kings, David, Solomon, Hezekiah, Josiah and others, teach that the power of enacting, fixing and refixing ecclesiastical laws belongs to the magistrate.

units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Artic.perpend.pag.38. Penes Magistratum est, leges de politiâ Ecclesiasticâ condere.
units.tr: By Arminius, Articles Weighed, p. 38. It lies with the magistrate to enact laws concerning ecclesiastical polity.

units.la: ARTICULUS XXXIII. De Sacramentis.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXXIII. On the Sacraments.

units.la: CRedimus DEUM habita nostræ habitudinis atque infirmitatis ratione, Sacramenta nobis instituisse, ut promissa sua in nobis obsignaret, & ut essent Divinæ erga nos benevolentiæ, gratiæ, donorúmque eius certissima nobis pignora, ad fidem nostram fovendam, & sustentandam comparata{1}. Addidit verò illa ad verbum Evangelii, ut tam ea ipsa quæ nobis externè verbo suo declarat, tum ea etiam quæ ille ipse in cordibus nostris internè operatur, efficacius sensibus nostris proponeret: ac denique ut salutem, quam nobis communicare dignatur, magis magisque in nobis confirmaret. Sunt enim Sacramenta signa, ac symbola visibilia rerum internarum & invisibilium, per quæ, ceu per media, Deus ipse virtute Spiritus Sancti in nobis operatur. Itaque signa illa minime vana sunt, aut vacua: nec ad nos decipiendos aut frustrandos instituta. Ipsorum enim veritas est ipse Iesus Christus, sine quo nullius prorsus essent momenti.Præ-terea sufficit nobis is Sacramentorum numerus, quem Christus ipse verus & unicus Doctor noster instituit. Sunt vero illa duo duntaxat, nimirum Sacramentum Baptismi, & sacræ Cœnæ Domini nostri Iesu Christi{1}.
units.tr: We believe that God, taking into account our condition and weakness, instituted sacraments for us, to seal his promises in us, and to be most certain pledges to us of his goodwill, grace and gifts toward us, prepared for the nourishing and sustaining of our faith. He added them to the Word of the Gospel, so that he might set before our senses, more effectively, both those things which he declares to us outwardly by his Word and those which he himself works inwardly in our hearts, and finally so that he might more and more confirm in us the salvation which he deigns to communicate to us. For sacraments are signs and visible symbols of inner and invisible things, through which, as through means, God himself works in us by the power of the Holy Spirit. Therefore those signs are by no means empty or vain, nor instituted to deceive or frustrate us. For their truth is Jesus Christ himself, without whom they would be of no moment whatever. Moreover, that number of sacraments is enough for us which Christ, our true and only Teacher, instituted. There are indeed two only, namely the Sacrament of Baptism and the Holy Supper of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this article the following is seen to be taught.

units.la: I. Proximum & maxime proprium Sacramentorum finem non esse obsignationem gratia DEI, & confirmationem fidei nostræ, sed solemnem tantum Christi commemorationem.
units.tr: I. That the nearest and most proper end of the sacraments is not the sealing of God's grace and the confirmation of our faith, but only a solemn remembrance of Christ.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. D. 5. Error est Evangelicorum, cum tribuunt cœnæ Dominicæ quod fidem nostram confirmet, quodque in memoriam nobis redigat mortem Christi pro nobis.
units.tr: Welsingius, On the Office of a Christian Man, Sol. D. 5. It is an error of the Evangelicals when they ascribe to the Lord's Supper that it confirms our faith, and that it brings to our memory the death of Christ for us.

units.la: Ibidem. Sacra hæc ceremonia in eum finem a Christo est instituta, ut solemnis ipsius commemoratio fiat; quatenus, videlicet corpus suum pro nobis tradidit, & sanguinem suum pro nobis fudit.
units.tr: Ibid. This sacred ceremony was instituted by Christ for this end, that a solemn remembrance of him might be made, namely insofar as he gave his body for us and shed his blood for us.

units.la: Ibidem.sol.D.6. Nusquam apud sacros scriptores indicium ullum extat, quod ad fidem in nobis confirmandam hic sacer ritus institutus fuerit.
units.tr: Ibid., Sol. D. 6. Nowhere in the sacred writers is there any indication that this sacred rite was instituted for confirming faith in us.
