units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Artic. perpend. pag. 38. Perpendendum, an proximus & maxime proprius ideoque immediatus finis Cœnæ Dominicæ, tum qua institutus, tum qua usurpatus, non sit memoria seu commemoratio vel annunciatio mortis Domini, & quidem cum gratiarum actione, pro eo quod Deus Filium suum pro nobis in mortem dedit.
units.tr: By Arminius, Articles Weighed, p. 38. It is to be weighed whether the nearest and most proper, and therefore immediate, end of the Lord's Supper, both as it was instituted and as it is used, is not the memory or commemoration or proclamation of the Lord's death, and indeed with thanksgiving, for the fact that God gave his Son to death for us.

units.la: A VENATORE, Theol. vera & mera, pag. 16. Cœna Domini est exercitium ad significandam communionem Sanctorum, hoc est, ad commemorationem dilectionis Iesu erga omnes fideles, atque ad præstationem officij debiti & charitatis mutuæ.
units.tr: By Venator, True and Pure Theology, p. 16. The Lord's Supper is an exercise for signifying the communion of the saints, that is, for the remembrance of Jesus' love toward all the faithful, and for the performance of due duty and mutual charity.

units.la: II. Tria esse Sacramenta Novi Testamenti, Baptismum, Cœnam Dominicam, & Lotionem pedum.
units.tr: II. That there are three sacraments of the New Testament: Baptism, the Lord's Supper, and the washing of feet.

units.la: A VENATORE, Theol. vera & mera, pag. 13. Quæst. An non Iesus Discipulis suis etiam instituit ac mandavit externum aliquod & visibile Sacramentum humilitatis, & mu-
units.tr: By Venator, True and Pure Theology, p. 13. Question: Did not Jesus also institute and command for his disciples some external and visible sacrament of humility and mu-

units.la: ARTICULUS XXXIV. De Baptismo.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXXIV. On Baptism.

units.la: CRedimus & confitemur IESUM CHRI-STUM (qui finis legis est) omni alij sanguinis effusioni ad propitiationem peccatorum adhibendæ finem proprio suo sanguine effuso jam imposuisse: & abolita Circum-cisione, quæ fiebat per sanguinem, Baptif-mum illius loco instituisse, 1. quo in Eccle-siam DEI recipimur, & à cunctis alijs gen-tibus & peregrinis alijs religionibus segrega-mur, utpote illi soli consecrati, cujus sym-bolum & insignia gestamus. Est denique Baptismus nobis testimonio, illum ipsum nobis fore DEUM in æternum, qui & Pater nobis est propitius 2. Omnes igitur, qui sui sunt, jussit Dominus aquâ purâ Baptizari in nomine Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus Sancti: ut significaret sanguinem Christi per Spiritum Sanctum idem præstare & efficere interne in anima, quod aqua externe operatur in corpo-
units.tr: We believe and confess that Jesus Christ, who is the end of the law, has already put an end, by his own shed blood, to every other shedding of blood to be employed for the propitiation of sins. And, circumcision, which was performed through blood, being abolished, he instituted Baptism in its place, (1) by which we are received into the Church of God and set apart from all other nations and foreign religions, as belonging wholly to him whose badge and insignia we bear. Baptism is, finally, a testimony to us that he himself will be our God forever, who is also a gracious Father to us. (2) The Lord therefore commanded that all who are his should be baptized with pure water in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, to signify that the blood of Christ, through the Holy Spirit, accomplishes and works inwardly in the soul the same thing that water works outwardly on the body.

units.la: Lotionem pedum: uti nobis prolixè hoc describit Ioannes, cap. 13. à vers. 1. ad 18. corporibus. Sicuti enim aqua in nos effusa, & super corpus baptizati eminens ipsumque irrigans, sordes corporis abluit: sic & sanguis Christi animam abluens, a peccatis illum emundat, nosque filios irae in filios DEI regenerat. Non quod aqua hæc materialis ista efficiat, sed aspersio ipsa pretiosissimi sanguinis Filij DEI, qui nobis est ceu mare illud rubrum, per quod transeundum est, ut e tyrannide Pharaonis, id est, Diaboli, egredi, & in spiritualem terram Chanaan introire possimus. Itaque Ministri quidem præbent nobis Sacramentum, & rem visibilem: at Dominus ipse exhibet quod Sacramento significatur, nimirum dona & gratias invisibiles, abluens, purificans, & mundans animas nostras à cunctis sordibus & iniquitatibus suis: renovans item, & replens corda nostra omni consolatione: largiens denique nobis veram paternæ suæ bonitatis certitudinem, 3. novo homine nos induens, & veterem exuens cum omnibus operibus ejus. Præterea credimus omnem hominem, qui vitam æternam consequi cupiat, debere semel Baptizari, [atque unico hoc Baptismo contentū esse.] qui nunquam postea sit iterandus, cum ne nasci quidé bis possimus. Neque tamen hic Baptismus eo duntaxat momento prodest, quo aqua nobis inhæret, aut quo eâ tingimur: sed per totum vitæ nostræ tempus.: [alioquin necesse foret nos caput nostrum semper aquâ tinctum habere.] Anabaptistarum itaque errorem hic detestamur, qui non modò unico & semel suscepto Baptismo contenti non sunt: sed & Baptismum infantium è fidelibus parentibus natorum damnant 4. Nos vero eos eadem ratione baptizandos, & signo fœderis obsignandos esse credimus, quâ olim in Israële parvuli circumcidebantur, nimirum propter easdem promissiones infantibus nostris factas. Et revera Christus non minus sanguinem suum effudit, ut fidelium infantes, quam ut adultos ablueret. Ideoq; signum seu Sacramentum rei, quam Christus eorum causa est operatus, illos recipere convenit: quemadmodum in Lege iubet Dominus Sacramentum mortis & passionis Christi communicari pueris recens natis, offerendo pro ipsis agnum, qui Sacramentum erat Christi venturi. Præterea quod Circumcisio præstabat populo Iudaico, idem infantibus fidelium nunc præstat Baptismus. Atque hæc causa est, cur Paulus Baptismum vocet Circumcisionem Christi.
units.tr: Washing of feet: as John describes this at length, chapter 13, verses 1 to 18. For just as water poured over us and streaming over the body of the one baptized washes away the filth of the body, so also the blood of Christ, cleansing the soul, purges it from sins and regenerates us, children of wrath, into children of God. Not that this material water effects it, but the very sprinkling of the most precious blood of the Son of God, which is to us like that Red Sea through which we must pass, so that we may go out from the tyranny of Pharaoh, that is, of the Devil, and enter into the spiritual land of Canaan. Thus the ministers indeed offer us the sacrament and the visible thing, but the Lord himself gives what is signified by the sacrament, namely the invisible gifts and graces, washing, purifying and cleansing our souls from all their filth and iniquities; also renewing and filling our hearts with all consolation; and finally bestowing on us the true certainty of his fatherly goodness, (3) clothing us with the new man and stripping off the old with all its works. Moreover we believe that every man who desires to obtain eternal life ought to be baptized once, [and to be content with this one Baptism,] which is never to be repeated, since we cannot even be born twice. Nor, however, does this Baptism profit only at the moment when the water clings to us or when we are dipped in it, but throughout the whole time of our life [otherwise it would be necessary for us always to have our head wet with water]. Therefore we here detest the error of the Anabaptists, who are not only content with one Baptism received once, but also condemn the baptism of infants born of believing parents. (4) We, however, believe that they are to be baptized on the same ground, and sealed with the sign of the covenant, on which in Israel of old little children were circumcised, namely on account of the same promises made to our infants. And indeed Christ shed his blood no less that he might wash the infants of the faithful than that he might cleanse adults. Therefore it is fitting that they receive the sign or sacrament of the thing which Christ has accomplished for their sake, just as in the Law the Lord commanded the sacrament of the death and passion of Christ to be given to newborn boys, offering for them a lamb, which was a sacrament of the Christ who was to come. Moreover, what circumcision afforded to the Jewish people, that same thing Baptism now affords to the infants of believers. And this is the reason why Paul calls Baptism the circumcision of Christ.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: This article seems to be opposed by the following teaching.

units.la: I. Baptismum fuisse tantum ritum temporarium, ex nullo præcepto Iesu Christi ab Apostolis usurpatum.
units.tr: I. Baptism was only a temporary rite, adopted by the Apostles without any command of Jesus Christ.

units.la: A SIM. EPISCOPIO, Disput. privat. de Baptismo. coroll. 1. Negamus nulla solida ratione demonstrari posse, Baptismum ceremoniam & ritum fuisse tantum temporarium, ex nullo præcepto Iesu Christi ab Apostolis tantum usurpatum atque exercitum.
units.tr: FROM SIMON EPISCOPIUS, Private Disputation on Baptism, corollary 1. We deny that it can be shown by any sound reasoning that Baptism was a ceremony and rite only temporary, adopted and practised by the Apostles without any command of Jesus Christ.

units.la: II. Baptismi finem non esse gratiæ Dei de remissione peccatorum per sanguinem Christi obsignationem, sed tantum significationem: nec fidei nostræ de gratia Dei confirmationem, sed tantum professionem.
units.tr: II. The purpose of Baptism is not the sealing of God's grace concerning the remission of sins through the blood of Christ, but only its signifying; nor the confirmation of our faith concerning God's grace, but only our profession.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic.hom.Christ.sol.E.I. Error Evangelicorum circa Baptismum est, quod affirmant eo obsignari divinitus peccatorum remissionem, id quod Coenæ Domini quoque tribuunt, & quemadmodum per Coenam Domini, sic per Baptismum adultorum qui baptizantur, fidem confirmari credunt, cum tamen per Baptismum non quidem obsignetur, sed tantum adumbretur peccatorum remissio.
units.tr: FROM WELSINGIUS, On the Office of the Christian Man, Sol. E.1. The error of the Evangelicals concerning Baptism is that they affirm that the remission of sins is divinely sealed by it, which they also attribute to the Lord's Supper; and they believe that, just as through the Lord's Supper, so through Baptism, the faith of adults who are baptized is confirmed, whereas by Baptism the remission of sins is not indeed sealed, but only foreshadowed.

units.la: Ibidem. De fidei confirmatione, quæ adultis ex Baptismo, quem suscipiunt, contingat, nihil attinet amplius dicere, quam nec ullum indicium huius rei in divinis literis extare.
units.tr: Ibid., on the confirmation of faith, which comes to adults from the Baptism they receive, there is no need to say more than this: that no trace of this matter is found in the divine writings.

units.la: AB EPISCOPO, Desp.privat. de Bapt.thes.8. Finis Baptismi est sola tantum divinæ gratiæ & professionis nostræ significatio.
units.tr: FROM EPISCOPIUS, Private Disputation on Baptism, thesis 8. The sole purpose of Baptism is only the signifying of divine grace and of our profession.

units.la: III. Neminem sine speciali revelatione in hac vitâ posse habere hanc de paterna DEI bonitate certitudinem, DEUM sibi propitium Patrem fore in æternum, quoniam omnes verè fideles ex fide & gratiâ DEI totaliter & finaliter possint excidere.
units.tr: III. No one in this life can have, without special revelation, this certainty of the Father's goodness of God, that God will be a propitious Father to him for ever, since all who are truly faithful can fall away totally and finally from faith and from the grace of God.

units.la: AREMONSTRANTIBUS, Coll.Hag.pag.340. Non videmus doctrinam istam de Perseverantia in fide eorum, qui semel crediderunt, esse fundamentum consolationis filiorum DEI, sed existimamus suâ naturâ atque indole idoneam esse ad ingenerandam hominibus securitatem, ut in medio cursu peccatorum ipsis sit loco pulvinaris, quo semetipsos molliter fovere, suaviterque demulcere, atque ita consolari possint.
units.tr: FROM THE REMONSTRANTS, Collatio Hagiensis, p. 340. We do not see that this teaching concerning the perseverance in faith of those who have once believed is a foundation of comfort for the children of God; rather we think that by its nature and character it is fitted to produce security in people, so that in the midst of a course of sins it serves them as a pillow on which they may softly cherish themselves, gently soothe themselves, and so be able to console themselves.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 346. Dubitare utrumne semper ij futuri si-mus, qui nunc sumus,non est noxium, sed laudabile cum-primis atque utile est.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 346. To doubt whether we shall always be those who we now are is not harmful, but is above all commendable and useful.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.423. Necessariò sequitur, eum qui semel fidem adeptus est, posse eam amittere:ac propterea nullum fidelem posse citra specialem revelationem certum esse, se semper in fide perseveraturum.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 423. It necessarily follows that one who has once obtained faith can lose it; and therefore no believer can be certain, without special revelation, that he will always persevere in faith.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.297. 302. Doctrina de certa verè fidelium perseverantia ex se verâ pietati & bonis moribus noxia est, tum in iis qui eam docent, tum in iis qui eam audiunt: & fideles commonefactiones Spiritus Sancti adversus periculosas technas & machinationes Diaboli inutiles & ineffcaces reddit.
units.tr: Ibid., pp. 297, 302. The doctrine of the certain perseverance of true believers is in itself harmful to true piety and good morals, both in those who teach it and in those who hear it; and it renders the faithful admonitions of the Holy Spirit against the dangerous snares and schemes of the Devil useless and ineffective.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.302. Crebra in Scripturis occurrunt exempla eorum,qui in fide non perstiterunt, sed totaliter & finaliter ab ea defecerunt.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 302. In the Scriptures there frequently occur examples of those who did not persist in faith, but fell away from it totally and finally.

units.la: AJAC. ARMINIO, Artic. perpend. pag. 31. Perpendendum, An verè fideles possint excidere totaliter & finaliter, Item. An reipsa nonnulli totaliter & finaliter a fide excidant.Item. Sententia, quæ negat verè fideles & regenitos vel reipsa excidere a fide totaliter & finaliter, nunquam fuit ab Ecclesiâ, ab ipsis Apostolorum temporibus ad hæc nostra secula, pro Catholica habita, neque quæ contrarium affirmat, pro hæretica æstimata: imò verò affirmans semper plures in Christianismo adstipulatores habuit, quam negans.
units.tr: FROM JACOB ARMINIUS, Articles for Consideration, p. 31. It must be considered whether true believers can fall away totally and finally. Likewise, whether some in fact fall totally and finally from faith. Likewise: the opinion which denies that true believers and the regenerate can in fact fall from faith totally and finally has never been held by the Church, from the very times of the Apostles to our own age, to be Catholic; nor has the contrary affirmation been judged heretical. Indeed, the affirming opinion has always had more supporters in Christianity than the denying one.

units.la: Ibidem. Perpendendum, An quis Fidelis certus esse possit se à fide non defecturum citra specialem revelationem. Item. An Fideles credere teneantur, se à fide non defecturos. Affirmatio utriusque quæstionis nunquam pro Catholico dogmate habita fuit in Ecclesiâ Christi: nunquam etiam negatio utriusque istius quæstionis hæresis judicata est ab Ecclesiâ Catholicâ.
units.tr: Ibid. It must be considered whether a believer can be certain that he will not fall from faith without special revelation. Likewise: whether believers are bound to believe that they will not fall from faith. The affirmation of either question has never been held in the Church of Christ as a Catholic dogma; nor has the denial of either question ever been judged heretical by the Catholic Church.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.32. Persuasio quâ quis Fidelis sibi certò persuadet se à fide deficere non posse, saltem se non defecturum à fide, non tam solatio servit adversus desperationem seu dubitationem, Fidei & spei adversam, quam securitati ingenerandæ, quæ saluberrimo timori, quo salutem nostram operari jubemur; & qui in hoc tentationum loco magnopere est necessarius, directè adversetur.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 32. The persuasion by which a believer firmly persuades himself that he cannot fall from faith, or at least that he will not fall from faith, serves not so much as consolation against despair or doubt, which are adverse to faith and hope, as it produces security, which directly opposes that most salutary fear by which we are commanded to work out our salvation, and which is greatly needed in this place of temptation.

units.la: A NICOL. GREVINCHOVIO, contra Amef.pag.138. Sensum Electionis ad gloriam in hac vita nullum agnosco, quisit absolutis certitudinis, sed tantum conditionatæ. Item. Qualis est certitudo perseverantiæ nostræ, talis & Electionis: utramque verò conditionatam esse qui negaverit, ipsum quoque Evangelium negabit.
units.tr: FROM NICOLAUS GREVINCHOVIUS, against Amesius, p. 138. I recognise no sense of election to glory in this life that is of absolute certainty, but only a conditional one. Likewise: such as is the certainty of our perseverance, such is also that of election; and whoever denies that both are conditional will also deny the Gospel itself.

units.la: A PETRO BERTIO, De Apostasiâ Sanctorum, per totum librum. Præfat. Iudico sententias istas, quibus docetur, 1. Solis illis gratiam à DEO dari, qui absoluto & inconditionato decreto à DEO essent ad vitam electi, cæteris verò non dari. 2. Et dari illis per vim quandam irrefragibilem. 3. Ita ut semel accepta nunquam postea rejici aut excludi possit; esse Sacris Scripturis, naturæ DEI, & bonis moribus inimicas.
units.tr: FROM PETER BERTIUS, On the Apostasy of the Saints, throughout the book, Preface. I judge those teachings, by which it is taught, 1. that grace is given by God only to those who were chosen to life by an absolute and unconditional decree of God, and is not given to the rest; 2. that it is given to them by a certain irresistible force; 3. so that once received it can never afterwards be rejected or excluded: these are hostile to the Holy Scriptures, to the nature of God, and to good morals.

units.la: Ibidem. Enimverò, si nulla est alia Perseverantia, quam quæ fictitio decreto inconditionatæ Electionis nixa est, profiteor palam, & meo more, propositum mihi esse non tantum illam oppugnare, sed etiam evertere, ut quæ divino verbo aduersetur, & sollicitudinem omnem, curamque salutis, mortalibus eripiat.
units.tr: Ibid. Indeed, if there is no other perseverance than that which rests on the fictitious decree of unconditional election, I openly profess, and in my manner, that it is my purpose not only to attack it but even to overthrow it, as being opposed to the divine word and as snatching from mortals all anxiety and care for salvation.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 7. Controversia ista sunt, 1. An qui credit possit fidem suam deferere. 2. An quae deseritur, fuerit vera fides. Nos ad utramque quaestionem respondebimus affirmative.
units.tr: Ibid., p. 7. The questions in this controversy are: 1. whether one who believes can forsake his faith; 2. whether the faith which is forsaken was true faith. We shall answer both questions affirmatively.

units.la: A SIM. EPISCOPIO. Disput.publ.de Pecc.act.corol.1. Negamus aliquod peccatorum horum (inter quod etiam est peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum) dari, in quod is qui vere semel credidit in Christum Iesum, suapte culpa incidere nequeat.
units.tr: FROM SIMON EPISCOPIUS, Public Disputation on Sins committed, corollary 1. We deny that any of these sins (among which is also the sin against the Holy Spirit) can occur such that he who has truly once believed in Christ Jesus could fall into it through his own fault.

units.la: Ibidem.corol.2. Affirmamus eum, qui semel vere credidit ea fide, quae justificans a quibusdam dici solet, ita peccare posse, ut a fide illa sua, & consequenter a gratia & salute aeterna, totaliter & finaliter excidat.
units.tr: Ibid., corollary 2. We affirm that one who has truly once believed with that faith which some are accustomed to call justifying can sin in such a way that he falls totally and finally from that faith of his, and consequently from grace and eternal salvation.

units.la: IV. Infantes foederatorum non esse baptizandos, sed tantum adultos, qui doceri, & fidem profiteri possunt.
units.tr: IV. The infants of covenant people are not to be baptized, but only adults, who can be taught and profess faith.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic.hom.Christ.sol.D.8.[?] Error Evan-gelicorum est, cum statuunt infantium baptismum esse divinam ordinationem, aut certè rem divinae ordinationi consentaneam.
units.tr: FROM WELSINGIUS, On the Office of the Christian Man, Sol. D.8.[?] It is an error of the Evangelicals when they maintain that the baptism of infants is a divine ordinance, or at least a thing agreeing with a divine ordinance.

units.la: Ibidem. Neque vero ullum baptizati infantis exemplum usquam in S.literis extat. Item. sol. B.1. Nullum divinum praeceptum infantes baptizandi, sed ne exemplum quidem ullum alicujus baptizati infantis in sacra historia extat,
units.tr: Ibid. Indeed, no example of a baptized infant is found anywhere in the Sacred Writings. Likewise, Sol. B.1. There is no divine command to baptize infants, nor is there even any example of a baptized infant in the sacred history.

units.la: A VENATORE, Theol.mera & vera,pag.12. Quaest. An Iesus ordinavit ut prius doceantur homines, & postea baptizentur? Resp.Omnino.
units.tr: FROM VENATOR, Pure and True Theology, p. 12, Question. Did Jesus ordain that men should first be taught and afterwards baptized? Answer: Certainly.

units.la: ARTICVLVS XXXV. De Cœnâ Domini.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXXV. On the Lord's Supper.

units.la: CREdimus etiam & confitemur D. Je-sum Christum Seruatorem nostrum, sacrosanctum Cœnæ suæ Sacramentum instituisse, ut in ea nutriat, ac sustentet eos, quos jam regeneravit, & in familiam suam, nempe Ecclesiam insevit. Qui verò regene-rati sunt, duplicem in se vitam habent: unam quidem carnalem & temporariam, quam secum à prima nativitate sua attulerunt, & hæc communis est omnibus hominibus: alteram spiritualem & cœlestem, quæ illis donatur in secunda illa nativitate, quæ fit per verbum Evangelij in unione corporis Christi, & hæc vita non est communis nisi solis Electis Dei 1. Sicuti verò Deus panem terrenum & materialem ad hujus vitæ carnalis & terrenæ sustentationem idoneum constituit, qui ut & ipsa vita, omnibus est communis; ita & ad conservationem illius vitæ spiritualis, & cœlestis, quæ fidelium propria est, DEVS panem vivificum misit, qui de cœlo descendit, nempe Iesum Chri-stum: is nutrit & sustentat vitam fidelium spiritualem, si comedatur, id est, applice-tur & recipiatur spiritu per fidem. Ut autem panem hunc spiritualem & cœlestem Chri-stus nobis figuraret, sive repræsentaret; in-stituit Panem & Vinum terrenum & visibi-lem in Corporis & sanguinis sui Sacramen-tum: ut ijs nobis testificetur, quam verè ac-cipimus & tenemus manibus nostris hoc Sacramentum, illúdque ore comedimus (unde & postmodum vita hæc nostra susten-tatur) tam verè etiam nos fide (quæ animæ nostræ est instar & manus & oris) recipere verum corpus & verum sanguinem Christi, in animis nostris, ad vitam spiritualem in nobis fovendam 2. Certissimum vero est, Christum non sine causa tam solicitè hoc suum Sacramentum nobis commendare, utpote qui perficiat in nobis revera, quæ-cunque ipse nobis his sacris signis repræsen-tat: quamvis modus ipse ingenij nostri captum superet, nec percipi à quoquam pos-sit: quod videlicet operatio Spiritus Sancti occulta sit & in comprehensibilis: [ interim nequaquam erraverimus si dicamus fieri per fidem. ] Dicimus itaq; id quod comeditur esse ipsissimum Christi corpus naturale, & id quod bibitur verum ipsius sanguinem: at instrumentum seu medium quo hæc comedimus & bibimus non est os corporeum, sed spiritus ipse noster, idque per fidem. Christus itaque semper ad dextram Patris in cœlis residet, nec ideo minus se nobis per fidem communicat. Porrò hæc Coena mensa est spiritualis, in quâ Christus seipsum nobis cum omnibus bonis suis participandum offert, efficitque ut nos in illâ, tam illo ipso, quam merito passionis mortisque ipsius fruamur. Animam enim nostram miseram & afflictam, omnique consolatione destitutam, carnis suæ esu ipsemet nutrit, roborat & consolatur: sanguinis item sui potu eam sustentat ac recreat. Præterea quamvis Sacramenta sint conjuncta rei ipsi significatæ, ambæ tamen res istæ non ab omnibus recipiuntur. Impius enim recipit quidem Sacramentum in suam condemnationem, at rem seu veritatem Sacramenti non recipit. Verbi gratiâ, gratia, Iudas & Simon Magus receperunt quidem ambo Sacramentum: Christum ve-rò ipsum, qui illo significabatur, minimè, quoniam solis ille fidelibus communicatur. Postremò huic nos Sacramento sacrosancto in coetu populi DEI cum summa humili-tate & reverentia communicamus, memo-riam mortis Christi Servatoris nostri cum gratiarum actione sanctè celebrantes, & fi-dei, Religionisque Christianæ confessionem publicè ibi profitentes. Nemo itaque ad hanc mensam se sistere debet, qui prius se non probaverit, ne de hoc pane edens, & de hoc poculo bibens judicium ipse sibi & damnationem manducet, ac bibat. Vsu porrò hujus Sacramenti accenditur in nobis fla-grantissimus amor tum in DEVM ipsum, tum in proximum. Itaque nos hic quidem merito omnes hominum ludificationes, & damnanda commenta (quæ illi Sacramen-tis addiderunt & admiscuerunt) tanquam veram profanationem rejicimus: affirma-músque omnes pios unico illo ordine, & ri-tu, quem Christus & Apostoli nobis tradi-derunt, contentos esse, atque de mysterijs eodem modo loqui debere, quo & illi locuti sunt.
units.tr: We also believe and confess that our Lord Jesus Christ, our Saviour, instituted the most holy sacrament of his Supper so that he might nourish and sustain those whom he has already regenerated and has planted in his family, that is, the Church. Those who are regenerated have a twofold life in themselves. The first is carnal and temporal, which they brought with them from their first birth, and this is common to all men. The second is spiritual and heavenly, which is given to them in that second birth, which takes place through the word of the Gospel in union with the body of Christ, and this life is common only to the elect of God. Just as God appointed earthly and material bread to sustain this carnal and earthly life, which is common to all, as life itself is, so too, to preserve that spiritual and heavenly life which belongs to the faithful, God has sent the living bread that came down from heaven, namely Jesus Christ. He nourishes and sustains the spiritual life of the faithful if it is eaten, that is, if it is applied and received by the spirit through faith. Now, so that Christ might portray or represent this spiritual and heavenly bread to us, he instituted bread and wine, earthly and visible, as the sacrament of his body and blood. By these he testifies to us that, just as we truly receive this sacrament in our hands and eat it with our mouths (whereby our life is afterwards sustained), so too, by faith (which is for our soul what the hand and mouth are for the body), we truly receive in our hearts the true body and true blood of Christ, to cherish this spiritual life within us. [Indeed we would not err at all if we said that it happens through faith.] Surely Christ did not commend this sacrament of his to us so earnestly without cause, since he truly accomplishes in us whatever he sets before us through these holy signs, although the manner of it surpasses the grasp of our intellect and cannot be perceived by anyone, namely that the operation of the Holy Spirit is hidden and incomprehensible. We therefore say that what is eaten is the very natural body of Christ, and what is drunk is his true blood; but the instrument or means by which we eat and drink these is not the bodily mouth but our spirit itself, and this through faith. Christ therefore always sits at the right hand of the Father in heaven, and yet he communicates himself to us no less through faith. Moreover, this Supper is a spiritual table, at which Christ offers himself to us to be shared together with all his goods, and he brings it about that we enjoy in it both him himself and the merit of his passion and death. For he himself nourishes, strengthens and comforts our wretched and afflicted soul, which is destitute of all consolation, by the eating of his flesh; likewise he sustains and refreshes it by the drinking of his blood. Furthermore, although the sacraments are joined to the thing signified, these two things are not received by all. For the impious man indeed receives the sacrament to his own condemnation, but does not receive the thing or truth of the sacrament. For example, Judas and Simon Magus both received the sacrament, but certainly not Christ himself, who was signified by it, since he is communicated only to the faithful. Finally, we partake of this most holy sacrament in the assembly of the people of God with the greatest humility and reverence, celebrating devoutly the memory of the death of Christ our Saviour with thanksgiving, and publicly professing there our faith and the confession of the Christian religion. Therefore no one ought to present himself at this table who has not first examined himself, lest he eat of this bread and drink of this cup and eat and drink judgement and damnation to himself. Moreover, by the use of this sacrament a most fervent love is kindled in us, both towards God himself and towards our neighbour. Accordingly, we rightly reject here all the mockeries of men and the damnable inventions (which they have added to and mixed with the sacraments) as a true profanation; and we affirm that all the godly are content with that single order and rite which Christ and the Apostles have handed down to us, and that they ought to speak of the mysteries in the same way as they spoke.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: It seems to be taught against this article.

units.la: I. Non omnes qui vita spiritualis per regenerationem participes sunt, esse Electos D E I, sed hanc vitam etiam communem esse multis Reprobis: quoniam vere regeniti à vera fide & regeneratione totaliter & finaliter excidere possint, & multi etiam exciderint atque excidant; & Electus nemo sit, vel haberi possit, quamdiu ad finem usque vita in fide non perseveraverit.
units.tr: I. That not all who share in the spiritual life through regeneration are the elect of God, but that this life is also common to many reprobate; since those truly regenerated can wholly and finally fall away from true faith and regeneration, and many have indeed fallen away and do fall away; and no one is or can be held to be elect as long as he has not persevered in faith to the end of life.

units.la: A REMONSTRANTIBVS, Coll.Hag.pag.303. In sacrâ scripturâ invenimus diversa exempla eorum, qui in fide non perseverarunt, sed totaliter & finaliter ab eâdem exciderunt.
units.tr: FROM THE REMONSTRANTS, Coll. Hag. p. 303. In Holy Scripture we find diverse examples of those who did not persevere in faith, but wholly and finally fell away from it.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 304. Verè fideles, quia possunt eò prolabi ut opera carnis faciant, possunt etiam fidem amittere & quum opus carnis faciunt, eandem amiserunt ad tempus, si pòst se convertant, & in perpetuum, si se non convertant.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 304. Truly believers, because they can slip so far as to do the works of the flesh, can also lose faith; and when they do the works of the flesh, they have lost that faith for a time if they afterwards turn back, and for ever if they do not turn back.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 384. Non est ineptum dicere hominem bis posse regenerari.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 384. It is not absurd to say that a man can be regenerated twice.

units.la: A BERTIO, De Apostasiâ Sanctorum, pag. 21. 22. Scripturæ narrant, verè justos, fideles, & sanctos à verâ justitiâ, fide, & sanctitate defecisse, & hoc factum in Angelis, in primis nostris parentibus, in Saule, in Hymenæo & Phileto, in Dema, in Nicolao, atque etiam in ipso Salomone librorum Canonicorum autore, Templi dedicatore, & typo Christi.
units.tr: FROM BERTIUS, On the Apostasy of the Saints, pp. 21, 22. The Scriptures relate that men who were truly just, faithful and holy fell away from true righteousness, faith and holiness, and this happened among the angels, among our first parents, in Saul, in Hymenaeus and Philetus, in Demas, in Nicolaus, and even in Solomon himself, the author of the canonical books, the dedicator of the Temple, and a type of Christ.

units.la: A NICOL. GREVINCHOVIO, contra Amef. pag. 136. Electio ex fide præviså includit perseverantiam in fide. Item. Quoties fidelee statuimus objectum Electionis, toties nos fidem & perseverantiam in fide conjungimus. Item. Fideles denominamus ab eâ fide, quæ totum fidei apotelesma, in-itium, progressum, & finem ambitu suo comprehendit.
units.tr: FROM NICOLAUS GREVINCHOVIUS, against Amesius, p. 136. Election based on foreseen faith includes perseverance in faith. Likewise, as often as we set the faithful as the object of election, so often we join faith and perseverance in faith. Likewise, we call men faithful from that faith which comprehends within its compass the whole accomplishment of faith, its beginning, progress and end.

units.la: Ibidem. In Scripturis dupliciter dicuntur Electi.1.incomple-te, secundum statum præsentem, quâ tales, puta fideles hoc tempore, excepto ultimo vitæ termino, in quo 2. Electio completur.
units.tr: Ibid. In the Scriptures the elect are spoken of in two ways: 1. incompletely, according to the present state, in which sense the faithful at this time are such, except at the last end of life, at which 2. election is completed.

units.la: Ibidem. pag. 137. Qui justificationis participes sunt nondum sunt idoneum Electionis peremptoriæ objectum.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 137. Those who are partakers of justification are not yet a fit object of peremptory election.

units.la: Ibidem. Electio peremptoria in objecto prærequirit totam consummatam fidei obedientiam. Item. Electio perem-ptoria actu suo versatur circa fidelem in fide morientem.
units.tr: Ibid. Peremptory election in its object requires the whole completed obedience of faith. Likewise. Peremptory election by its act is concerned with the faithful man dying in faith.

units.la: Ibidem. pag.138. Sensum Electionis ad gloriam in hac vita nul-lum agnosco, qui sit absolutæ certitudinis.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 138. I acknowledge no sense of election to glory in this life that is of absolute certainty.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.141. Multi reprobi ejusdem cum electis, justificationis, sanctificationis, pacis conscientiæ &c. ad tempus consortes fuerunt.
units.tr: Ibid. p. 141. Many reprobate were for a time partners with the elect in justification, sanctification, peace of conscience, etc.

units.la: II. Finem proximum & maximè proprium Cœnæ Dominicæ non esse obsignationem communicationis beneficiorum Christi, ad confirmationem fidei nostræ, sed professionem tantum hujus communicationis, & commemorationem solemnem mortis Christi.
units.tr: II. That the proximate and especially proper end of the Lord's Supper is not the sealing of the communication of the benefits of Christ for the confirmation of our faith, but only the profession of this communication and the solemn commemoration of the death of Christ.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. D. s. Esus & potus in hac sacra ceremonia pertinet ad declarandum eos, qui ex illo pane comedunt, & ex vino illo bibunt, palam & constanter & profiteri animam suam in spem vitæ æternæ Christi corpore pro nobis fracto & sanguine fuso non minus ali & sustentari, quam pane & vino corpus ad caducam hanc vitam alatur & sustentetur. Unde factum est ut Paulus Apostolus dixerit, panem quem frangimus esse communicationem Christi corporis, & poculum, cui benedicimus, communicationem esse ejus sanguinis, hoc est, professionem hujus communicationis.
units.tr: FROM WELSINGIUS, On the Office of the Christian Man, sol. D. s. The eating and drinking in this sacred ceremony serve to declare that those who eat of that bread and drink of that wine openly and constantly profess that their soul is fed and sustained, in the hope of eternal life, no less by the body of Christ broken for us and the blood poured out, than the body is nourished and sustained for this perishable life by bread and wine. Hence it is that the Apostle Paul said that the bread which we break is the communion of the body of Christ, and the cup over which we give thanks is the communion of his blood, that is, the profession of this communion.

units.la: Ibidem..Error Evangelicorum est, cum tradunt finem Cœ-næ Domini esse, ut fidem nostram confirmet, & ut in memo-riam nobis redigat mortem Christi pro nobis.
units.tr: Ibidem. Error of the Evangelicals is when they teach that the purpose of the Lord's Supper is that it confirms our faith, and that it brings to our memory the death of Christ for us.

units.la: Ibidem.sol.D.6. Nusquam apud sacros scriptores indicium ullum extat, quod ad mortem Christi in nobis renovandam, vel ad fidem in nobis confirmandam, fuerit hic sacer ritus institutus.
units.tr: Ibidem, sol. D. 6. Nowhere in the sacred writers is there any indication that this holy rite was instituted either to renew the death of Christ in us or to confirm faith in us.

units.la: Ibidem.sol. E. 1. Cum Cœna domini celebratur, non quidem obsignatur remissio peccatorum, sed illam olim per mortem Christi obsignatam fuisse commemoratur ac prædica-tur.
units.tr: Ibidem, sol. E. 1. When the Lord's Supper is celebrated, it does not indeed seal the forgiveness of sins, but it recalls and proclaims that this forgiveness was once sealed through the death of Christ.

units.la: Ab ARMINIO, Artic.perpend.pag.38. Perpendendum an proximus & maxime proprius, ideoque immediatus finis Cœnæ Dominicæ, tum quâ institutus est, tum quâ usurpatur, non sit memoria, seu commemoratio, vel annunciatio mortis Domini, & quidem cum gratiarum actione pro eo quod DEVS Filium suum pro nobis in mortem dederit, ejusque carnem edendam, & sanguinem bibendum dedit per fidem in illum.
units.tr: From ARMINIUS, Artic. perpend., p. 38. We should consider whether the nearest and most proper, and therefore immediate, end of the Lord's Supper, both as it was instituted and as it is used, is not the memory, or commemoration, or announcement of the Lord's death, and indeed with thanksgiving that God gave his Son for us to death, and gave us his flesh to eat and his blood to drink through faith in him.

units.la: A SIM.EPISCOPIO, Disput.privat.de Cœna Domini, thes.10. Finis celebrationis Cœnæ est sola tantum repræsentatio & significatio mortis, ac beneficij illius ingentis, quod per mortem nobis partum atque comparatum est, per quam fides et-iam ipsa nobis excitari & confirmari solet, animusque noster veluti cibo atque potu quodam nutriri & educari spe vitæ æternæ.
units.tr: From SIMON EPISCOPIUS, Private Disputation on the Lord's Supper, thes. 10. The end of celebrating the Supper is only the representation and signification of the death and of that great benefit which has been obtained and procured for us through death, through which faith itself is usually also aroused and confirmed in us, and our soul is nourished and brought up, as with a certain food and drink, by hope of eternal life.

units.la: A VENATORE, Theol.vera & mera, pag.16. Cœna Domini est ritus ad significandam & commemorandam dilectionem Iesu erga omnes fideles, & ad debitum dilectionis officium erga nos mutuò præstandum.
units.tr: From VENATOR, True and Pure Theology, p. 16. The Lord's Supper is a rite for signifying and commemorating the love of Jesus toward all the faithful, and for mutually performing the due duty of love toward one another.

units.la: ARTICULUS XXXVI. De Magistratu.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXXVI. On the Magistrate.

units.la: Credimus DEUM Optimum Maximum ob generis humani corruptelam ac depravationem, Reges, Principes & Magistratus constituisse: velléque ut Mundus hic legibus ac certa politiâ gubernetur, ad coercenda hominum vitia, & ut omnia inter homines recto ordine gerantur. Idcirco Magistratus ipsos gladio armavit, ut malos quidem plectant pœnis, probos vero tueantur{1}. Horum porro est non modò de civili politiâ conservandâ esse sollicitos, verum etiam dare operam ut sacrum Ministerium conservetur, omnis idololatria & adulterinus DEI cultus è medio tollatur, Regnum Antichristi diruatur, Christi vero Regnum propagetur. Denique horum est efficere, ut sacrum Evangelij verbum ubique prædicetur, ut singuli purè DEUM colere & venerari ex præscripto verbi ipsius liberè possint. Cæterum cuncti homines, cujuscunque sint vel dignitatis, vel conditionis, ac status, legitimis Magistratibus subjici debent, il-lisque vectigalia ac tributa pendere, & ijs in omnibus obsequi ac obedire, quæ verbo DEI non repugnant: preces etiam pro ijs fundere, ut eos DEVS in omnibus ipsorum actionibus dirigere dignetur, nos vero vitam tranquillam ac quietam sub ipsis, cum omni pietate & honestate, ducere possimus. Quamobrem Anabaptistas & turbulentos omnes detestamur, qui superiores Dominationes & Magistratus abjiciunt, jura ac judi-cia pervertunt, bona omnia communia faciunt, ac denique ordines ac gradus, quos DEVS honestatis gratia inter homines constituit, abolent ac confundunt.
units.tr: We believe that God, the best and greatest, because of the corruption and depravity of the human race, has established kings, princes and magistrates, and wills that this world be governed by laws and a certain policy, to restrain the vices of men and so that all things among men are carried on in right order. Therefore he has armed the magistrates themselves with the sword, so that they punish the wicked with penalties, but protect the upright{1}. Moreover, it is their duty not only to be concerned for preserving civil order, but also to take care that the holy ministry is preserved, that all idolatry and adulterous worship of God is removed from the midst, that the kingdom of Antichrist is torn down, and that the kingdom of Christ is spread abroad. Finally, it is their task to see that the holy word of the Gospel is preached everywhere, so that each person may purely worship and venerate God freely according to the prescription of the Word itself. Otherwise, all people, of whatever dignity, condition or rank, ought to be subject to lawful magistrates, pay them taxes and tributes, and obey and submit to them in all things which do not conflict with the word of God. We should also pour out prayers for them, that God may deign to direct them in all their actions, and that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life under them, with all piety and honesty. For this reason we detest the Anabaptists and all troublemakers, who reject higher authorities and magistrates, pervert laws and judgments, make all goods common, and finally abolish and confuse the orders and degrees which God has established among men for the sake of decency.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this article it seems to be taught:

units.la: I. Magistratui Christiano non licere fontes gladio, seu pœnâ capitali punire: neque licere Christianis in bello sanguinem humanum fundere.
units.tr: I. That it is not lawful for a Christian magistrate to punish heretics with the sword, or by capital punishment; nor is it lawful for Christians to shed human blood in war.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. 1. Cum Christi præceptis pugnat, quod apud Evangelicos conceditur, ita vim vi repellere, ut etiam hominem interficere liceat, si aliter vis repelli nequeat: præsertim vero cum bellum injustum nobis infertur.
units.tr: From WELSINGIUS, De Offic. hom. Christ., sol. 1. It is contrary to the precepts of Christ that, among the Evangelicals, it is permitted to repel force with force in such a way that it is even lawful to kill a man, if force cannot otherwise be repelled, especially when an unjust war is waged against us.

units.la: Ibidem. Antiquissimum ac severissimum Dei præceptum humani sanguinis non fundendi, quod habetur Gen. 9.5. nihil in tota Christi & Apostolorum ejus doctrina immutatum invenitur.
units.tr: Ibidem. The most ancient and most severe command of God, that human blood is not to be shed, which is found in Gen. 9.5, is found to have been changed in no way in the whole doctrine of Christ and his Apostles.

units.la: Ibidem.Si dixerint,sub V.T.ubi non minus, quam sub N. præceptum humani sanguinis non fundendi vigebat, licuisse tamen vim hostium,etiam cum ipsorum occisione, propulsare.Resp.Id propterea tum licuisse, quod Deus multis modis declaraverat, se id tum temporis non improbare.
units.tr: Ibidem. If they say that under the Old Testament, where the command that human blood is not to be shed was in force no less than under the New, it was nonetheless lawful to repel the force of enemies even with their slaughter: Reply: this was then lawful for the reason that God had declared in many ways that he did not disapprove of it at that time.

units.la: Ibidem. Deus populo suo sub V.T. vel promiserat, vel jam assignaverat,& dederat,terrenum regnum, terrenamque possessionem, quam ab ipsis defendi & conservari volebat: quod fieri non potuisset,si hostes in se irruentes armis pro-pulsare,& ad internecionem etiam interdum interficere non licuisset. At sub. N. T. nullam suo populo terrenam possessionem dedit;imò terrâ posthabitâ cœlum eos inquirere jussit; & propterea nulla ratione unquam,vel per Christum,vel per ejus Apostolos declaravit, se hostium invadentium propulsationem cum ipsorum nece conjunctam approbare.
units.tr: Ibidem. Under the Old Testament God had either promised to his people, or had already assigned and given them, an earthly kingdom and an earthly possession, which he willed to be defended and preserved by them. This could not have been done if it had not been lawful to repel with arms enemies who rushed against them, and sometimes even to kill them to the point of destruction. But under the New Testament he gave his people no earthly possession; rather, setting aside the earth, he ordered them to seek heaven. Therefore, by no means, either through Christ or through his Apostles, has he ever declared that he approves the repelling of invading enemies when it is joined with their death.

units.la: Ibidem. Remanet hîc firmisimum, nec ulla ex parte immutatum sub Evangelio præceptum humani sanguinis non fundendi,præsertim cum Christus præcepta addiderit,quibus non modò ipsorum etiam hostium sanguinem fundere vetat,sed illis benefacere jubet.
units.tr: Ibidem. The precept that human blood is not to be shed remains here most firm and is changed in no part under the Gospel, especially since Christ added precepts by which he not only forbids shedding the blood of enemies themselves, but commands that good be done to them.

units.la: ARTICULUS XXXVII. De Iudicio extremo, Resurrectio-ne carnis, & Vita aeterna.
units.tr: ARTICLE XXXVII. Of the Last Judgment, the Resurrection of the Flesh, and Eternal Life.

units.la: Postremò credimus ex DEI verbo, Dominum nostrum IESVM CHRISTVM, quando tempus à DEO præstitutum, quod omnibus creaturis est ignotum, advenerit, & numerus Electorum completus fuerit 1. è cœlo rursus venturum, idque corporaliter & visibiliter, sicuti olim illuc ascendit, cum summâ gloriâ & Majestate, ut se declaret judicem vivorum & mortuorum: vetere hoc mundo igne & flammâ succenso, ut illum purificet. Tunc verò omnes creaturæ, tam viri quam mulieres & infantes, quotquot inde ab initio usque ad finem mundi extiterint, coram summo hoc judice comparebunt, eò nimirum voce [& tremendo clamore Angelorum] & Archangeli, & tu-bâ DEI evocati. Omnes enim antea mortui è terrâ tunc resurgent, animâ singulorum conjuncta atque unita proprio suo corpori, in quo vixerat {2}. Qui porrò ultimo illo die superstites erunt, nequaquam morientur more reliquorum, sed in momento & jactu oculi, immutabuntur, à corruptione videlicet in incorruptam naturam. Tunc aperientur libri ( nimirum conscientiae ) & mortui judicabuntur secundum ea, quae in hoc mundo egerint, sive bona sive mala. Quinetiam tunc redditurí sunt homines rationem de omni verbo otioso, quod locuti fuerint, etsi id mundus nunc pro ludo & joco reputet. In summa omnis tunc hominum hypocrisis & abstrusa quaeque cordis corum palam coram omnibus detegentur. Ac propterea sola judicij istius memoria impijs & reprobis merito est horrenda & formidabilis: pijs vero & electis summe exoptanda, & ingentis consolationis. Tunc enim redemptio ipsorum plane perficietur, & suavissimos laborum & dolorum suorum, quos in hac vita pertulerunt, fructus, consequentur: innocentia ipsorum tunc aperte ab omnibus agnoscetur, ipsique vicissim horrendam vindictam conspecturi [?]turi sunt, quam Dominus de ijs sumet, qui eos varijs tormentis & molestijs in hoc mundo tyrannicè afflixerunt. Impij porrò proprio conscientiæ suæ testimonio convicti erunt, & immortales quidem reddentur, sed eâ conditione ut in igne æterno, qui Diabolo & angelis eius paratus est, in sempiternum crucientur.
units.tr: Finally, we believe from the Word of God that our Lord Jesus Christ, when the time appointed by God, which is unknown to all creatures, has come and the number of the elect has been completed, will come again from heaven, bodily and visibly, just as he once ascended there, with supreme glory and majesty, so as to declare himself the judge of the living and the dead, with this present world set on fire with a fierce flame in order to purify it. Then indeed all creatures, men and women and infants alike, as many as have existed from the beginning until the end of the world, will appear before this supreme judge, called forth by the voice [and the dreadful clamour of the angels] and the archangel, and the trumpet of God. For all who have died before will then rise from the earth, each soul being joined and united again to its own body in which it had lived {2}. Those, moreover, who are still alive on that last day will by no means die in the manner of the others, but in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, they will be changed, that is, from corruption into an incorruptible nature. Then the books will be opened (namely, the consciences), and the dead will be judged according to what they have done in this world, whether good or evil. Moreover, men will then give account of every idle word that they have spoken, although the world now regards this as a game and a joke. In sum, all the hypocrisy of men and whatever is hidden in their hearts will then be openly disclosed before everyone. Therefore the mere memory of that judgment is rightly dreadful and terrifying to the impious and the reprobate, but greatly to be desired by the godly and the elect, and a source of immense comfort. For then their redemption will be fully completed, and they will obtain the most delightful fruits of the labours and sufferings they endured in this life; their innocence will then be openly acknowledged by all, and they themselves, in turn, will behold the terrible vengeance which the Lord will take on those who tyrannically afflicted them in this world with various torments and troubles. The impious, moreover, will be convicted by the testimony of their own conscience, and indeed will be made immortal, but on this condition: that they will be tormented forever in the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels.

units.la: Contra vero fideles & Electi coronâ gloriæ & honoris donabuntur: & Filius DEI eorum nomina coram DEO Patre & [sanctis eius atque electis] Angelis confitebitur: & abstergetur omnis lachryma ab oculis eorum. Caussa itaque eorum, quæ non hæreseωs & impietatis à Magistratibus, & judicibus damnatur, caussa Filij DEI esse tunc agnoscetur. Et DOMINUS eos tantâ gloriâ gratis remunerabitur, quantam nullus hominum animo concipere unquam possit. Magnum erga illum Domini diem [retributionis] summo cum desiderio expectamus, ut rebus omnibus à DEQ[?] promissis plenissimè in Christo Iesu DOMINO nostro læti potiamur, & in æternum perfruamur.
units.tr: On the contrary, the faithful and the elect will be granted the crown of glory and honour, and the Son of God will confess their names before God the Father and [his saints and elect] angels: and every tear will be wiped from their eyes. Thus the cause of those who are condemned by magistrates and judges not as heretics and impious persons, but as those who are for the sake of the Son of God, will then be recognised as the cause of the Son of God. And the Lord will reward them with such glory, freely given, as no man could ever conceive in his mind. We await with the greatest longing the great day of the Lord [of retribution], so that we may fully and joyfully enjoy all the things promised by God in Christ Jesus our Lord, and may delight in them forever.

units.la: Apocal.22.20. Etiam veni Domine IESV.
units.tr: Rev. 22.20. Yes, come, Lord Jesus.

units.la: Contra hunc Articulum doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against this Article the following seems to be taught.

units.la: I. Non esse certum aliquem numerum Electorum, qui compleri debeat.
units.tr: I. That there is no certain number of the elect that must be completed.

units.la: A WELSINGIO, De Offic. hom. Christ. sol. B. 3. Decretum Electionis non ad certos ac definitos homines, nominatim hos vel illos, sed potius ad certum hominum genus referri debet.
units.tr: From WELSINGIUS, On the Duties of the Christian Man, Book 3. The decree of election ought not to refer to certain and definite men, by name these or those, but rather to a certain kind of men.

units.la: A SIM.EPISCOPIO, Disput.privat.de Prædest.opere, thes.2.& 4. Falsa est atque erronea sententia, quæ statuit DEVM ab a-terno certum quendam numerum, sine ullo fidei aut obedientiæ respectu, ex reliqua turba seligere, ut in iis salvandis misericordiam suam declararet.
units.tr: From SIMON EPISCOPIUS, Private Disputation on Predestination, theses 2 and 4. False and erroneous is the opinion which holds that God from eternity selects a certain number out of the rest of the crowd, without any regard to faith or obedience, in order to display his mercy in saving them.

units.la: Ibidem.Disp.de Eccl. thes.12. Electio quarundam singularium personarum ad Ecclesiam Christi spiritualem constituendam adhiberi recte non potuit, nec adhibita fuit.
units.tr: Ibid., Disputation on the Church, thesis 12. Election of certain individual persons could not rightly be, and was not, employed to constitute the spiritual Church of Christ.

units.la: II. Homines non resurrecturos cum iisdem[?] corporibus in quibus vixerunt, sed in futura vita habituros alia corpora, quæ, quoad substantiam, spiritualia erunt.
units.tr: II. That men will not rise with the same bodies in which they lived, but in the future life will have other bodies, which, as to substance, will be spiritual.

units.la: A CONR.VORSTIO, Disput.de Deo, pag.200. Si & nos spirituale corpus habituri sumus in futuro seculo, quanto magis DEVM spiritum esse censendum est. Spiritus autem carnem & ossa non habet, nec videri nec tangi potest. Ex quo apparet DEI substantiam prorsus esse spiritualem, & ab omni materia, seu crassa corpulentia penitus alienam.
units.tr: From CONRAD VORSTIUS, Disputation on God, p. 200. If we too are to have a spiritual body in the future age, how much more must God be judged to be spirit. But spirit does not have flesh and bones, nor can it be seen or touched. From this it appears that the substance of God is wholly spiritual and entirely alien from all matter, or gross corporeality.

units.la: Ibidem.In futuro seculo jam non amplius caro & sanguis erimus: sed ἰσάγγελοι[?], & spirituales.
units.tr: Ibid. In the future age we shall no longer be flesh and blood, but equal to the angels [isángeloi], and spiritual.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: END.

units.la: Omissa pag. 95.
units.tr: Omitted, page 95.

units.la: Contra Articulum xxv doceri videtur.
units.tr: Against Article XXV the following seems to be taught.

units.la: VI. Hominem regenitum posse in hac vita legem DEI, seu praecepta omnia moralia, perfecte servare.
units.tr: VI. That a regenerate man can in this life perfectly keep the law of God, or all the moral precepts.

units.la: Ab Arminio, Resp. ad 31. Artic. pag. 164.165. Non repugno isti sententiae Augustini, qua statuit hominem sine peccato esse posse in hac vita.
units.tr: From Arminius, Response to the 31 Articles, pp. 164–165. I do not oppose that opinion of Augustine by which he held that a man can be without sin in this life.

units.la: Respons. ad 9, Artic. pag. 176. Praestatio legis secundum mentem postulantis est aestimanda: qui cum aut rigide velit in summo perfectionis gradu illam observari, aut secundum ἐπιείκειαν tantum, respondebitur bifariam, ad quaestionem, An fideles sub gratia N. T. possint in hac vita Legem Dei perfecte servare? Nempe, si postulet secundum ἐπιείκειαν, & vires quas contulit proportionatae sint postulato, non posse hominem talem Legem Dei perfecte praestare, si consideretur ut praestanda juxta rigorem. Si vero postulet secundum ἐπιείκειαν, & vires collatae sint proportionatae, quod dicendum est, cum Evangelico foedere postulet; respondendum est posse perfecte praestari.
units.tr: Response to the 9th Article, p. 176. The fulfilment of the law is to be estimated according to the mind of the one who demands it: whoever wishes it observed either rigidly, in the highest degree of perfection, or only according to equity (epieíkeia), will be answered in two ways to the question, Can the faithful under the New Testament keep the law of God perfectly in this life? Namely: if he demands it according to equity, and the powers conferred are proportionate to the demand, then it must be said that a man cannot perfectly fulfil such a law of God if it is considered as to be fulfilled according to strict rigour. But if he demands it according to equity, and the powers conferred are proportionate, which must be said, since he demands it in accordance with the Evangelical covenant, then the answer must be that it can be perfectly fulfilled.

units.la: Artic.perpend.pag.30. Qui dicit regenitos posse per Christi gratiam Legem perfecte praestare in hac vita, ille non Pelagianus est, neque gratiae Dei facit injuriam, neque justificationem ex operibus stabilit.
units.tr: Article Weighed, p. 30. Whoever says that the regenerate can, through the grace of Christ, perfectly fulfil the law in this life, is neither a Pelagian, nor does he do injury to the grace of God, nor does he establish justification by works.

units.la: A Vorstio, Apolog.Exeg.iii. Obedientia in Lege Dei requisita secundum, quid & per accidens, nobis est impossibilis, nempe quatenus extra gratiam Dei, tum justificantem, tum regenerantem, adhuc versamur: & quamdiu ita prout jam corrupti sumus, in nobis ipsis spectamur. Interea verum manet, DEUM nihil omnino praecipere quod non per illam integram ipsius Dei voluntatem eatenus saltem praestare possimus, ut Deus ipsegratiose in hac obedientia tandem acquiescat. Ibidem.pag.112. DEus in nobis efficit,ut,nisi sponte nobis desimus,praecepta ipsius, per hanc ejusdem gratiam ,praestare & possimus & velimus,adeoque reipsa praestemus:ita saltem ut DEus in hac praestatione clementer acquiescat.
units.tr: From Vorstius, Exegetical Apology, iii. The obedience required in the law of God is, in a certain respect and by accident, impossible for us, namely insofar as we still live outside the grace of God, both justifying and regenerating, and as long as we are regarded in ourselves, as we are now corrupted. Meanwhile it remains true that God commands nothing at all which we cannot, by that whole will of God itself, at least so far perform, that God himself may at last graciously acquiesce in this obedience. Ibid., p. 112. God works in us so that, unless we willingly fail him, his precepts, through this same grace of his, we both can and will perform, and so in fact do perform: at least so that God in this performance graciously acquiesces.

units.la: A VENATORE, Declar.pag.174. Non credo DEum jure posse ab hominibus exigere, quod à nativitate ipsa praestare non potuerunt : atque ad hoc praestandum vires dare non velle, & quod tamen propterea velit eos condemnare, quod bonum impossibile non praestiterint, & peccatum inevitabile non omiserint.
units.tr: From VENATOR, Declaration, p. 174. I do not believe that God can justly require of men what they could not perform from birth itself, and that he is unwilling to give them strength to perform it, and yet that he will therefore wish to condemn them because they did not perform an impossible good or did not avoid an unavoidable sin.

units.la: Ibidem.pag.177. Nullo modo assentiri possum DEum ab homine exigere quod praestare non possit, & ad quod praestandum vires non conferat , neque unquam conferre ve-lit.
units.tr: Ibid.</i, p. 177. In no way can I agree that God requires of a man what he cannot perform, and for the performance of which he does not confer strength, nor ever will be willing to confer it.
