units.tr: There are chiefly four orders of the ministry in the Church, namely, those of ministers, teachers, elders and deacons.

units.la: CAP. I. De Ministris verbi Dei.
units.tr: CHAPTER I. Concerning the Ministers of the Word of God.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Ad verbiMinisterium nemo admittatur, sine legitimâ Vo-catione, Electione, justoque Examine doctrinæ, vitæque anteactæ.
units.tr: No one is to be admitted to the ministry of the Word without lawful calling, election, and a just examination of doctrine and of his previous life.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Cavendum sibi est à νεοφύτοις[?], & Monachis vel Presbyteris à Papatu conversis, ne admittantur ad S. Ministerium, nisi seria & diuturna præcesserit exploratio.
units.tr: Care must be taken regarding neophytes [νεοφύτοις], and monks or elders converted from the Papacy, that they not be admitted to the holy ministry unless a serious and lengthy testing has preceded.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Vt autem idonei ad hoc munus reperiantur viri, hoc agant Ecclesiæ, ut adolescentes ingenui, & bonæ spei in studio Theologico educentur.
units.tr: So that suitable men may be found for this office, the Church shall take care that young men of good birth and good hope be educated in the study of theology.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Ad Electionem Ministri requiruntur sequentia, ut 1. Celebretur jejunium. 2. Nominetur à Presbyterio & Classe. 3. Examinetur ab utrisque. 4. Sistatur coram Magistratu & totâ Ecclesiâ, ut intra dies quatuordecim tacitis fidelium suffragijs comprobetur. 5. Subscribat Catechismo Heydelbergensi & fidei Confessioni Hispaniarum Regi Anno 1578. exhibitæ. 6. Confirmetur coram Ecclesiâ cum oratione ad Deum, manuum impositione, (si ita ferat consuetudo) & exhortatione ad populum; postquam ad ista interrogata pu-blicè responderit. I. An se legitimè sentiat ad hoc ministerium vocatum. II. An sola Biblica scripta pro Dei verbo recipiat. III. An ea fideliter populo prædicare velit, vitâ inculpatâ præeundo. IV. An se subjiciat Ecclesiasticæ Disciplinæ.
units.tr: For the election of a minister the following are required: (1) a fast is to be observed; (2) he is to be nominated by the consistory and the classis; (3) he is to be examined by both; (4) he is to be presented before the magistrate and the whole Church, so that within fourteen days, by the silent suffrages of the faithful, he may be approved; (5) he is to subscribe to the Heidelberg Catechism and to the Confession of faith presented to the King of Spain in the year 1578; (6) he is to be confirmed before the Church, with a prayer to God, the laying on of hands (if custom so bears), and an exhortation to the people, after he has publicly answered these questions: (I) whether he feels himself lawfully called to this ministry; (II) whether he receives only the canonical writings as the Word of God; (III) whether he is willing to preach these faithfully to the people, going before them in a blameless life; (IV) whether he submits himself to ecclesiastical discipline.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Qui semel legitimè in S.Ministerio sunt confirmati,illud dum vivunt non deserent, nisi legitima incidat occasio, de quâ judicium erit penes Synodum Provincialem vel Nationalem.
units.tr: Those who have once been lawfully confirmed in the holy ministry shall not abandon it while they live, unless a lawful occasion arises, concerning which judgment shall rest with the provincial or national synod.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Nemo ab aliâ vocatus Ecclesiâ ad eam se conferet, nisi cum Ecclesiæ suæ consensu & Classis approbatione.
units.tr: No one called by another Church shall transfer himself to it, except with the consent of his own Church and the approval of the classis.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Fidi Pastoris & Ministri officia sunt:
units.tr: The duties of a faithful pastor and minister are:

units.la: 1. Verbum Dei cum reverentiâ & simplicitate prædicare.
units.tr: (1) to preach the Word of God with reverence and simplicity;

units.la: 2. Sacramenta administrare.
units.tr: (2) to administer the sacraments;

units.la: 3. In Oratione perseverare.
units.tr: (3) to persevere in prayer;

units.la: 4. Disciplinam Ecclesiasticam exercere.
units.tr: (4) to exercise ecclesiastical discipline;

units.la: 5. Et procurare ut omnia decenter & ordine peragantur.
units.tr: (5) and to take care that all things are done decently and in order.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Si Minister donum habet aliquid ad ædificationem conscribendi,illud typis non mandabit, quin prius à Classe examinetur & probetur.
units.tr: If a minister has a gift for writing something for edification, he shall not commit it to print unless it has first been examined and approved by the classis.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Honesta & justa merces Ministro danda est.
units.tr: An honest and just reward is to be given to the minister.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Si quis senio vel morbo fiat ad Ministerium inutilis, ab Ecclesiâ nihilominus alendus est.
units.tr: If anyone becomes unfit for the ministry through old age or sickness, he is nonetheless to be supported by the Church.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: De Ministrorum viduis & orphanis similiter habenda est ratio.
units.tr: Likewise, provision is to be made for the widows and orphans of ministers.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Cæcus in Ministerio non est confirmandus : attamen si confirmatus sit, non ideò deponendus.
units.tr: A blind man is not to be confirmed in the ministry; yet if he has been confirmed, he is not on that account to be deposed.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Studiosi Theologiæ cum bonâ Classis venià, publicè quandoque exercitij causâ concionari poterunt, non tamen Sacramenta administrare, donec in ministerio plenè sint confirmati.
units.tr: Students of theology may, with the good permission of the classis, sometimes preach publicly for the sake of practice, but they may not administer the sacraments until they have been fully confirmed in the ministry.

units.la: XIV.
units.tr: XIV.

units.la: Nullus Minister in Ministros alios primatum aut dominatum obtinebit, sed æqualiter Ecclesiasticum onus ferent.
units.tr: No minister shall obtain primacy or lordship over other ministers, but all shall bear the ecclesiastical burden equally.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Si minister in S. hoc munere se non condignè gesserit, adeò ut infamiæ notam sibi inusserit, à Ministro suspendatur vel deponatur, idque Magistratus consensu.
units.tr: If a minister has not conducted himself worthily in this holy office, so that he has brought upon himself a mark of infamy, he shall be suspended or deposed by the minister, and this with the consent of the magistrate.

units.la: CAP. II. De Doctoribus & Scholis.
units.tr: CHAPTER II. Concerning Teachers and Schools.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Hæc Ecclesiarum sit cura, ut in Academiâ sint Doctores Theologiæ, eruditionis & pietatis nomine præstantes.
units.tr: It shall be the care of the Churches that in the university there be teachers of theology, outstanding in learning and in piety.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Habeat unaquæque Ecclesia ad erudiendam iuventutem suos Ludimagistros.
units.tr: Let each Church have its own schoolmasters for the instruction of the young.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Præscribat Ecclesia Ludimagistris preces in Scholis concipiendas, & libros ad institutionem puerilem maximè idoneos.
units.tr: Let the Church prescribe to the schoolmasters the prayers to be recited in the schools, and the books most suitable for the instruction of children.

units.la: CAP. III. De Senioribus.
units.tr: CHAPTER III. Concerning the Elders.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Eligantur Seniores à verbi Ministris & conventu Eccle-siastico, cum jejunio & oratione ad Deum, & confirmentur in Ecclesiâ consuetis interrogationibus.
units.tr: Elders are to be chosen by the ministers of the Word and the ecclesiastical assembly, with fasting and prayer to God, and are to be confirmed by the usual questions in the Church.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Munus Seniorum est: 1. Cum verbi Ministris gregi invigilare, 2. Ecclesiae membra invisere. 3. Ægros consolari. 4. Scandala ad consistorium deferre. 5. Cum verbi Ministris de scandalis judicare, & quantum poterunt, ex Ecclesiâ tollere.
units.tr: The office of the Elders is: (1) to watch over the flock together with the ministers of the Word; (2) to visit the members of the Church; (3) to console the sick; (4) to report scandals to the consistory; (5) to judge scandals together with the ministers of the Word and, as far as they can, to remove them from the Church.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Numerus Seniorum sit pro arbitrio & necessitate cujusque Ecclesiae.
units.tr: The number of Elders is to be left to the judgment and need of each Church.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Seniores electi ex Ecclesiae consuetudine, munus illud in se recipere non recusent, nisi gravis subsit causa.
units.tr: Elders chosen according to the custom of the Church should not refuse to take up that office, unless a serious cause stands in the way.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Singulis annis dimidia pars Seniorum Electione renovabitur: quamvis magis è re Ecclesiae esset in prædicto munere continuatio, siquidem commodè id fieri posset.
units.tr: Each year half of the Elders shall be renewed by election; although it would be more to the advantage of the Church if continuance in that office were allowed, provided this could conveniently be done.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: De Diaconis.
units.tr: Concerning Deacons.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Diaconi sunt eligendi & confirmandi eo modo quo Se-niores.
units.tr: Deacons are to be chosen and confirmed in the same manner as the elders.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Diaconorum munus est. 1. Eleemosynas & alia pauperum bona diligenter colligere. 2. Fideliter & discretè distribuere. 3. Pauperes & ægros amanter invisere & consolari. 4. Ne inutiliter Eleemosynæ consumantur prospicere vigilanter.
units.tr: The office of deacons is: (1) to diligently collect alms and the other goods of the poor; (2) to distribute them faithfully and with discretion; (3) to visit and comfort the poor and the sick with love; (4) to watch vigilantly that the alms are not spent to no purpose.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Collectæ & expositæ pecuniæ rationem singulis mensibus coram Synedrio Ecclesiastico reddent.
units.tr: They shall render an account of the money collected and disbursed to the ecclesiastical consistory every month.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Mulieres ætate provectæ, spectatâ fide ac probitate ad hoc etiam munus Apostolorum exemplo rectè adscisci pos-sent[?].
units.tr: Women of advanced age, whose faith and uprightness are well attested, may also rightly be admitted to this office, following the example of the Apostles.

units.la: CAP. V. De Prophetiâ. Ex Synodis Wesaliensi & Embdanâ.
units.tr: CAP. V. On Prophecy. From the Synods of Wesel and Emden.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: In omnibus Ecclesijs sive nascentibus, sive vegetis, Prophetiæ ordo ex Pauli instituto observetur.
units.tr: In all churches, whether newly founded or well established, the order of prophecy laid down by Paul is to be observed.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Ad hoc collegium cooptentur, non modo Ministri, sed etiam Doctores, ac ex Senioribus & Diaconis, atque adeo ex ipsa plebe, si qui sint qui donum suum à Domino acceptum in communem Ecclesiæ utilitatem conferre velint: Ita tamen ut prius Ministrorum atque aliorum probentur judicio.
units.tr: To this college there should be co-opted not only ministers but also teachers, and from among the elders and deacons, and indeed from the common people itself, if there are any who are willing to contribute to the common benefit of the church the gift they have received from the Lord; provided, however, that they are first approved by the judgment of the ministers and of others.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: In hoc Collegio ad ædificationem omnium liber aliquis Scripturarum rato ordine explicetur. Ubi autem is, cujus erunt partes, vices suas expleverit, licebit ijs qui subsellijs eum insequuntur, siquidem visum erit, adjicere quod ad ædificationem pertineat: Actum demum, concepta oratione, ab eo, cujus erunt partes, cætus claudatur.
units.tr: In this college some book of the Scriptures is to be expounded in due order for the edification of all. When the one whose task it is has completed his turn, those who follow him from the benches may, if it seems fitting, add whatever pertains to edification. Finally, when a prayer has been offered by the one whose task it is, the assembly is to be closed.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Prophetandi forma, quæ quæstionibus & responsionibus constat, à Pauli instituto est aliena, & simulatum contentionumque persæpe est occasio.
units.tr: The form of prophesying, which consists of questions and answers, is foreign to the institution of Paul, and has very often been an occasion of pretence and of contentions.

units.la: CAP. VI. De Ecclesiasticis Conventibus.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI. Of Ecclesiastical Assemblies.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Ecclesiasticus conventus est quadruplex.1. Cujusque Ecclesiæ Consistorium. 2. Classis. 3. Synodus Provincialis. 4. Synodus Nationalis.
units.tr: There are four kinds of ecclesiastical assembly: (1) the consistory of each church; (2) the classis; (3) the provincial synod; (4) the national synod.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Hi Conventus oratione ad Deum inchoëntur, & gratia-rum actione terminentur.
units.tr: These assemblies are begun with prayer to God and concluded with thanksgiving.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: In hisce conventibus nullae nisi res Ecclesiasticae tracten-tur idque Ecclesiastico modo.
units.tr: In these assemblies only ecclesiastical matters are treated, and that in an ecclesiastical manner.

units.la: CAP. VII. De Consistorio.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII. On the Consistory.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Unaquaeque Ecclesia suum habeat Consistorium, ex ver-bi Ministro vel Ministris, & Senioribus dictæ Ecclesiæ con-sistens; qui singulis septimanis ad minimum semel conve-niant, ad res incidentes pertractandum.
units.tr: Each congregation shall have its own consistory, consisting of the minister or ministers of the Word and the elders of that congregation, who shall meet at least once a week to deal with the matters that arise.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Verbi Ministri per vices præsideant, designetur Scriba, qui notatu digna scripto consignet.
units.tr: The ministers of the Word shall preside in turn, and a clerk shall be appointed to commit to writing whatever is worthy of note.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Sint etiam in Ecclesiâ libri chartacei, in quibus scribantur nomina eorum, qui Sacro Baptismate tinguntur, nec non parentum & patrimorum nomina. Item eorum, qui nomen dant Ecclesiæ, matrimonio junguntur, & moriuntur.
units.tr: There shall also be paper registers in the congregation, in which are written the names of those who are baptized with holy Baptism, together with the names of their parents and sponsors; likewise the names of those who join the congregation, who are married, and who die.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Præsidis officium est. 1. Ex ordine sententias rogare. 2. Loquacibus silentium imponere. 3. Et ex collectis suffragiis res concludere.
units.tr: The duty of the president is: (1) to ask for opinions in order; (2) to impose silence on the talkative; (3) and to bring the matter to a conclusion from the votes collected.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Ecclesiæ membra, quæ alio se conferre volunt, à Consistorio testimoniales litteras petant.
units.tr: Members of the congregation who wish to go elsewhere shall ask the consistory for letters of testimony.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Quod in Consistorio commodè terminari non potest, ad Classicum conventum deferatur.
units.tr: Whatever cannot conveniently be settled in the consistory shall be referred to the classical assembly.

units.la: CAP. VIII. Classis, seu Synodus Diœcesiana.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII. The Classis, or Diocesan Synod.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Classicalis Conventus consistat ex verbi Ministris, & Se-nioribus vicinarum aliquot Ecclesiarum.
units.tr: The classical assembly shall consist of the ministers of the Word and the elders of several neighboring churches.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Fiat initium ab oratione ad Deum, per Ministrum qui praesederat conventui praecedenti, vel per Pastorem loci.
units.tr: The beginning shall be made with prayer to God, by the minister who presided over the previous assembly, or by the minister of the place.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Oratione finita fiat Electio Praesidis & Scribae, secretis suf-fragijs.
units.tr: When the prayer is finished, a president and a scribe shall be elected by secret vote.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Praesidi tradantur literae missionis seu testimoniales cujusque Consistorij, legantur Acta praecedentis Colloquij, & tempus locusque conventui designetur.
units.tr: The letters of sending, or testimonials, of each consistory shall be handed to the president; the acts of the previous colloquy shall be read; and the time and place of the assembly shall be appointed.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Huic conventui, Ministris & Senioribus etiam non desig-natis interesse liceat, & sententiam dicere, Interim desig-natorum sententiae suffragij vim tantum obtineant.
units.tr: Ministers and elders, even if not appointed, shall be permitted to attend this assembly and to give their opinion; meanwhile, the votes of those appointed shall alone carry weight.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Quod in conventu Classicali commode decidi non po-terit, ad Synodum Provincialem deferatur.
units.tr: What cannot conveniently be settled in the classical assembly shall be referred to the Provincial Synod.

units.la: CAP. IX. Synodus Provincialis.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX. The Provincial Synod.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Synodus Provincialis est conventus vicinarum Classium.
units.tr: The Provincial Synod is an assembly of neighbouring classes.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Ex unaquaque Classe duo Ministri & Seniores duo designentur, qui singulis annis ad minimum semel conveniant.
units.tr: From each class two ministers and two elders shall be appointed, who shall meet at least once a year.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Qui superiori conventui præfuit, aut qui Loci est Pastor, preces concipiat ad Præsidis, Assessoris & Scribæ electionem.
units.tr: The one who presided over the previous assembly, or the minister of the place, shall offer prayers for the election of the President, the Assessor and the Clerk.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Præses electus 1. Habebit preces ad totam actionem ac-commodatas. 2. Literas testimoniales postulabit. 3. Suffra-gia colliget. 4. Majoris & sanioris partis sententiam exponet.5.Eam Scriba excipiet; exceptam diserte leget, ut omnium calculis probetur. 6. Omnes sessiones gratiarum a-ctione claudet.
units.tr: The elected President shall: (1) offer prayers suited to the whole proceeding; (2) demand letters of testimony; (3) collect the votes; (4) set out the opinion of the greater and sounder part; (5) have the Clerk take it down, and read it out clearly, so that it may be approved by everyone's vote; (6) close all sessions with thanksgiving.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Quæ ad Doctrinam primùm, deinde quæ ad Disciplinam Ecclesiasticam pertinebunt, distinctè scriptis consigna-buntur, & legentur.
units.tr: Matters pertaining first to doctrine, and then those pertaining to ecclesiastical discipline, shall be written down distinctly, and read out.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Præsidis officium est: 1. Iubere ut quisque ordine suo lo-quatur. 2. Silentium contentiosis & acrioribus imperare. 3. Nisi taceant ut egrediantur præcipere, & fratrum judicio condignè reprehendere.
units.tr: The duty of the President is: (1) to order that each speak in his turn; (2) to impose silence on the contentious and the more heated; (3) if they do not keep silent, to order them to withdraw, and to rebuke them appropriately by the judgement of the brethren.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Totius conventus Provincialis consensu eligetur Ecclesia proximo conventui commoda.
units.tr: By the consent of the whole Provincial assembly, a congregation convenient for the next assembly shall be chosen.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Absolutis Synodi negotiis celebrabitur Sacra Cœna inter Ministros & Seniores, qui ad Synodum convenerunt, & Ecclesiam loci in quo collecta est.
units.tr: When the business of the Synod is concluded, the Lord's Supper shall be celebrated among the ministers and elders who have come to the Synod, and the congregation of the place where it has been gathered.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Ecclesiæ, in quâ Synodus habetur, cura incumbet, ut ad proximam Synodum acta seu constitutiones illius Synodi mittat vel adferat.
units.tr: It shall be the care of the congregation in which the Synod is held to send or bring the acts, or the constitutions, of that Synod to the next Synod.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Quod in Synodo Provinciali commodè decidi non po-terit, ad Synodum Nationalem deferetur.
units.tr: Whatever cannot conveniently be settled in the Provincial Synod shall be referred to the National Synod.

units.la: CAP. X. De Synodo Nationali.
units.tr: CHAPTER X. Concerning the National Synod.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Synodus Nationalis est conventus à Belgij Provincijs designatorum.
units.tr: The National Synod is an assembly of deputies designated from the Provinces of the Netherlands.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Eadem in hac Synodo, ut supra, est observanda ratio.
units.tr: The same order as above is to be observed in this Synod.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Unaquæque Provincia ad Synodum mittet duos verbi Ministros, & Seniores duos.
units.tr: Each province shall send two ministers of the Word and two elders to the Synod.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Aderunt etiam ab Ecclesijs Belgij Wallonicis deputati.
units.tr: Deputies from the Walloon churches of the Netherlands will also be present.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Quin etiam summi Magistratus delegati sunt postulandi, ut in ipsorum præsentiâ eorumque suffragio Synodi acta concludantur.
units.tr: Indeed, delegates of the highest magistrates are to be requested, so that the acts of the Synod may be concluded in their presence and with their vote.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Hoc autem, si fieri potest, agendum est, ut singulis tri-ennijs dicta Synodus celebretur.
units.tr: This, if it can be done, is to be arranged so that the said Synod is held once every three years.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Ut rite instructi veniant designati, unaquæque Provincia tempestive monebitur.
units.tr: So that the designated deputies may come properly prepared, each province will be advised in good time.

units.la: CAP. XI. De Exercitÿs Ecclesiasticis in sacro con-ventu peragendis.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI. Concerning the ecclesiastical exercises to be carried out in the sacred assembly.

units.la: I. Lectio.
units.tr: I. Reading.

units.la: Cultus divinus in Ecclesiâ à lectione unius aut alterius Capitis ex Scriptura incipiendus est.
units.tr: Divine worship in the Church is to begin with the reading of one or another chapter from Scripture.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Fiat oc[?] per Seniorem vel Diaconum, vel alium quemvis ad hoc ab Ecclesiâ constitutum.
units.tr: Let it be done by an elder or a deacon, or by anyone else appointed to this by the Church.

units.la: III. Concio.
units.tr: III. Sermon.

units.la: Concio sacra à Psalmorum cantu, & precibus ad Deum devotis inchoabitur.
units.tr: The sacred sermon shall begin with the singing of Psalms and with prayers devoutly offered to God.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Utile erit certum Sacræ Scripturæ librum ordine pro concione explicare,idque ex Synedrij consilio.
units.tr: It will be useful to expound a certain book of Holy Scripture in order for the sermon, and this by the counsel of the Synod.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Conciones funebres nusquam introducendas, & ubi in usu sunt commodè tollendas censet Synodus.
units.tr: The Synod judges that funeral sermons are nowhere to be introduced, and where they are in use, they are to be suitably abolished.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Concionibus nimis prolixis auditorum memoria ne oneretur, sed (si fieri potest) ad unius horæ spatium sermo temperetur.
units.tr: The memory of the hearers is not to be burdened by overly long sermons, but (if it can be done) the discourse is to be kept within the space of one hour.

units.la: VII. Psalmi.
units.tr: VII. Psalms.

units.la: In Cantu Ecclesiastico retinebuntur Psalmi à Petro Dathenò conversi per omnes Belgij Ecclesias.
units.tr: In ecclesiastical singing the Psalms translated by Peter Dathenus are to be retained in all the churches of the Belgic lands.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Utile erit aliquem designare cantorem qui populi cantum moderetur, & Psalmodiâ præeat.
units.tr: It will be useful to appoint some precentor who will regulate the singing of the people and preside over the psalmody.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: In Ecclesiæ cuiusque arbitrio erit, Psalmos ordine conti-nuo,vel pro re natâ decantare.
units.tr: It shall be left to the discretion of each Church to sing the Psalms in continuous order or as occasion arises.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: In hebdomade dies, pro cuiusque Ecclesiæ commodo, solennibus precibus consecrabitur, quo publica ac submissa peccatorum pro populo fiat deprecatio ante vel post con-cionem.
units.tr: One day of the week, as suits the convenience of each Church, shall be set apart for solemn prayers, so that public and private supplication for the sins of the people be made before or after the sermon.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Minister preces vel dictante Spiritu, vel certâ sibi propositâ formulâ concipiet.
units.tr: The minister shall frame the prayers either as the Spirit dictates or from a fixed form set before him.

units.la: XII. Ieiunia.
units.tr: XII. Fasts.

units.la: Tempore Belli, Famis, Pestis, Persecutionis & afflictionis graviores dies jejunij publicè Domino sanctificabuntur, Ma-gistratus auspicijs & consensu.
units.tr: In times of war, famine, pestilence, persecution and heavier affliction, days of fasting shall be publicly consecrated to the Lord, under the auspices and with the consent of the magistrate.

units.la: XIII. Catechesis.
units.tr: XIII. Catechesis.

units.la: Catechizandi consuetudo ab Apostolis accepta in omnibus Ecclesijs observanda censetur.
units.tr: The custom of catechizing, received from the Apostles, is judged to be observed in all the Churches.

units.la: XIV.
units.tr: XIV.

units.la: Belgicis Ecclesijs commendatur Heydelbergensis formula, ut cum Ecclesiis Germanicis unanimis & Christiana declaretur consensio.
units.tr: The Heidelberg formulary is commended to the Belgic Churches, so that a unanimous and Christian agreement may be declared with the German Churches.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: In explicandâ Catechesi sermone familiari & ad juniorum captum accommodato est utendum.
units.tr: In explaining the catechism, a familiar style of speech, adapted to the grasp of the young, is to be used.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Parentes & Ludimagistri sunt monedi, ut domi & in scholis juventutem diligenter in Catechesi instituant, & simul ac ætas liberorum patitur Ecclesiæ catechizandos offerant.
units.tr: Parents and schoolmasters are to be admonished to instruct the young diligently in the catechism at home and in the schools, and, as soon as the age of the children allows, to bring them to be catechized by the Church.

units.la: CAP. XII. De Sacramento Baptismi.
units.tr: Chapter 12. On the Sacrament of Baptism.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Sancti Baptismi Sacramentum, non ab alio quam à verbi Ministro rite conferri posse censetur.
units.tr: It is held that the sacrament of holy Baptism may be duly administered by no one other than a minister of the Word.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Hoc gratiæ sigillum etiam ad Christianorum liberos pertinet, eoque sine diuturniori dilatione Ecclesiæ sistentur baptizandi.
units.tr: This seal of grace also pertains to the children of Christians, and therefore they are to be presented to the Church for baptism without any lengthy delay.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Initio nascentis Ecclesiæ infirmorum habenda est ratio, eoque ad evitandum scandalum pueros valetudine adfli-ctos domi Baptizare licebit, præsentibus ut minimum quatuor aut quinque fidelibus.
units.tr: At the beginning of the newly born Church, regard was to be had for the sick, and therefore, to avoid giving offence, it shall be lawful to baptize at home children afflicted with sickness, with at least four or five believers present.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Administretur baptismus formâ usitatâ, & in Ecclesiasti-cis constitutionibus expressâ.
units.tr: Baptism is to be administered in the customary form, and as expressed in the ecclesiastical constitutions.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Unica vel trina tinctio censetur ἀδιάφορος[?].
units.tr: A single or a threefold immersion is considered indifferent [ἀδιάφορος].

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Parentes & Testes, qui ad Baptismum pueros adferent, ijs verbis, quæ in formâ Baptismi expressa sunt, interroga-buntur.
units.tr: Parents and witnesses who bring children to Baptism are to be questioned in the words that are expressed in the form of Baptism.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Curandum est ut Testes sint justæ ætatis & sanæ Religi-onis.
units.tr: Care must be taken that the witnesses be of mature age and of sound religion.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Infantibus non sunt danda nomina Divina, Barbara, Supersti-tiosa, sed in sacris literis (quantum fieri potest) ex-pressa, & à sanctis usitata.
units.tr: Infants are not to be given divine, barbarous or superstitious names, but names expressed in the sacred writings (as far as may be) and in use among the saints.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Nomina Infantum, Parentum, ac Testium publicis tabulis consignari tum Ecclesiæ, tum Reipub. conducet.
units.tr: It will be useful both for the Church and for the commonwealth that the names of infants, parents and witnesses be recorded in public registers.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Si adultus nondum Baptizatus Baptismum postulet, is prius publicam confessionem fidei suæ reddet in Ecclesiâ.
units.tr: If an adult who has not yet been baptized asks for baptism, he shall first make a public confession of his faith in the Church.

units.la: CAP. XIII.
units.tr: Chapter XIII.

units.la: De Sacramento Cœna Dominica.
units.tr: On the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Sacra Domini Cœna à solis verbi Ministris est admi-nistranda.
units.tr: The Holy Supper of the Lord is to be administered by the ministers of the Word alone.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Cœnæ celebrandæ tempus ante quartum decimum diem ad populum referri judicatur utile: tum ut Ecclesiæ membra se maturè præparent; tum ut Seniores suas vices obeant, & infirmiores moneant & consolentur.
units.tr: It is judged useful to announce to the people the time for celebrating the Supper before the fourteenth day: both so that the members of the Church may prepare themselves in good time, and so that the elders may discharge their duties and admonish and comfort the weaker members.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Nemo ad Cœnam Dominicam admittatur, nisi qui fidei confessionem ante reddiderit, & Disciplinæ Ecclesiasti-cæ se subjecerit, & vitæ inculpatæ testes fideles produxerit.
units.tr: No one is to be admitted to the Lord's Supper unless he has first made confession of faith, has submitted himself to the church discipline, and has produced faithful witnesses to an blameless life.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Sub utraque specie Panis sc. & vini S. Cœna est celebranda.
units.tr: The Holy Supper is to be celebrated under both kinds, namely of bread and of wine.

units.la: V. Panis sit communis, non peculiaris quis azymus, aut qui superstitionem resipiat.
units.tr: V. The bread shall be common, not some special unleavened bread, or bread that smacks of superstition.

units.la: VI. Fractio panis (quia à Christo manifestè est instituta, ab Apostolis totaque Ecclesiâ vetustiori observata) necessaria omninò censetur.
units.tr: VI. The breaking of the bread (since it was plainly instituted by Christ, and observed by the apostles and the whole of the more ancient Church) is judged wholly necessary.

units.la: VII. Verba S. Coenæ Christi præcepto & Apostoli Pauli declaratione consentanea sunt retinenda.
units.tr: VII. The words of the Holy Supper are to be retained, in keeping with Christ's command and with the declaration of the apostle Paul.

units.la: VIII. Liberum est stando, sedendo, vel eundo Coenam celebrare, non autem geniculando ob ξενολατρείας[?] periculum.
units.tr: VIII. It is free to celebrate the Supper standing, sitting, or walking, but not kneeling, because of the danger of [?] idolatry (ξενολατρείας).

units.la: IX. Utile erit tunc pro concione de S. Coena argumentum tractare, à Concione formulam constitutam Ecclesiæ prae-legere, & dum Coena celebratur S. Scripturam legi, vel Psalmos decantari.
units.tr: IX. It will be useful then to treat of the Holy Supper as the subject of a sermon, to read aloud from the pulpit the form set down by the Church, and, while the Supper is being celebrated, to read Holy Scripture or sing the Psalms.

units.la: X. Ecclesiæ Belgicæ in Pace constitutæ singulis bimestribus Coenam celebrabunt, quod liberum relinquitur Ecclesiis sub Cruce gementibus.
units.tr: X. The Churches of the Belgic lands, established in peace, shall celebrate the Supper every two months; this is left free to those Churches which groan under the cross.

units.la: XI. Ante Coenæ Dominicæ diem fiat concio præparatoria, & à concione inter Ministros, Seniores & Diaconos frater-na exerceatur Censura.
units.tr: XI. Before the day of the Lord's Supper a preparatory sermon shall be held, and brotherly censure shall be exercised by the ministers, elders and deacons together.

units.la: XII. Siquis literis testimonialibus ab aliâ Ecclesiâ venerit, si-ne confessione fidei iteratâ admittendus est.
units.tr: XII. If anyone comes from another Church with letters of testimony, he is to be admitted without a second confession of faith.

units.la: CAP. XIV. De Disciplina Ecclesiasticâ.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIV. On Ecclesiastical Discipline.

units.la: I. Vigilandum est ne ulla Ecclesia, neglectâ Ecclesiasticâ Disciplinâ, instituatur.
units.tr: I. Care must be taken that no church is established while ecclesiastical discipline is neglected.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Necesitas Disciplinæ docetur ex Domini nostri instituto, ex Apostolorum & vetustioris Ecclesiæ usu, & quotidianâ rerum experientiâ.
units.tr: The necessity of discipline is taught from the institution of our Lord, from the practice of the Apostles and of the more ancient Church, and from the daily experience of affairs.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Constat autem Disciplina, tum in Censurâ doctrinæ, tum in legitimâ morum correctione, id est, in justo Clavium à Domino Ecclesiæ datarum usu.
units.tr: Discipline consists both in the censure of doctrine and in the lawful correction of morals; that is, in the just use of the keys which the Lord has given to the Church.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Hæc Censura & Correctio nequaquam delinquentem liberat, à Civili judicio, & Magistratus gladio.
units.tr: This censure and correction by no means frees the offender from the civil judgment and the sword of the magistrate.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Si quis in Doctrinæ puritate sive morum sanctitate peccaverit, si occultum id sit, & à Scandalo publico remotum, observabitur Regula quam præscribit Christus, Matth. 18. nisi sit in casu proditionis aut perniciei publicæ.
units.tr: If anyone has sinned against the purity of doctrine or the holiness of life, provided the sin is hidden and not a public scandal, the rule that Christ prescribes in Matt. 18 shall be observed, unless it is a case of treachery or public ruin.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Si privatâ admonitione fratrem lucratus es, noli ejus crimen ad Consistorium deferre. Sed si duos aut tres fideliter admonentes non audierit, deferatur, ut in viam reducatur.
units.tr: "If you have gained your brother by private admonition, do not bring his crime before the consistory. But if he does not listen to two or three who admonish him faithfully, let it be reported, so that he may be brought back to the right way."

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Peccata suâ natura publica, aut per admonitionis privatæ contemtu publicata, ex Consistorij totius arbitrio, modo & formâ ad ædificationem maximè accómodatis sunt corrigeda.
units.tr: Sins which are public in their nature, or have been made public by contempt of private admonition, are to be corrected at the discretion of the whole consistory, in the manner and form most suited to edification.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Qui pertinaciter Consistorij admonitiones rejecerit, à S. Cœnæ communione suspendetur.
units.tr: Whoever stubbornly rejects the admonitions of the consistory shall be suspended from communion in the Holy Supper.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Si suspensus post iteratas admonitiones nullû pœnitentiæ signum dederit, ad Excommunicationem procedet Ecclesia.
units.tr: If the suspended person, after repeated admonitions, gives no sign of repentance, the Church shall proceed to excommunication.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Processus autem ad Excommunicationem hic erit.
units.tr: The process toward excommunication shall be as follows.

units.la: 1. Minister è suggestu (peccatoris nomine occultato) quid cum gravi quodam peccatore actum sit, significabit, & Ecclesiam, ut pro peccatore impœnitente sedulo oret monebit.
units.tr: 1. The minister, from the pulpit (the name of the sinner being withheld), shall state what has been done with a certain grave sinner, and shall admonish the Church to pray diligently for the impenitent sinner.

units.la: 2. Peccatoris impœnitentis nomen pro Cætu publicabit.
units.tr: 2. He shall make the name of the impenitent sinner known to the congregation.

units.la: 3. Significabit nisi resipiscat, Excommunicandum esse.
units.tr: 3. He shall declare that, unless he repents, he is to be excommunicated.

units.la: 4. Si ne sic quidem ad resipiscentiam adduci poterit, coram Ecclesia pertinacis ejusmodi peccatoris, a corpore Ecclesiæ fiet Excommunicatio & abscissio.
units.tr: 4. If he cannot be brought to repentance even in this way, excommunication and cutting off from the body of the Church shall take place before the Church, against such a stubborn sinner.

units.la: 5. Monebuntur fideles ne familiarem & non necessariam cum excommunicato consuetudinem habeant, sed ejus consortium vitent, hoc præcipuè consilio, ut pudore suffusus Excommunicatus de resipiscentia serio cogitet.
units.tr: 5. The faithful shall be warned not to keep up a familiar and unnecessary association with the excommunicated person, but to avoid his company, chiefly with this purpose, that the excommunicated person, overcome by shame, may seriously think about repentance.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Qui gravia & Ecclesiæ probrosa commisit peccata, etiamsi verbis pœnitentiam testetur, à Cœnæ tamen communione aliquot vicibus pro Consistorij arbitrio suspendetur.
units.tr: Whoever has committed grave sins that bring disgrace upon the Church shall, even if he professes repentance in words, be suspended from communion in the Lord's Supper for a number of times, at the discretion of the consistory.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: In recipiendo excommunicato serio resipiscente, ea observanda est ratio, quæ ad cujusque Ecclesiæ ædificationem maximè faciet.
units.tr: In receiving an excommunicated person who is seriously repentant, that method shall be observed which will most contribute to the edification of each church.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Si Minister, Senior, aut Diaconus publico aliquo crimine (quod Deus avertat) se contaminaverit, ab officio erit movendus: Si autem crimine aliquo occulto teneatur, à Classico conventu Censuram expectet pro criminis magnitudine vel levitate.
units.tr: If a minister, elder, or deacon has defiled himself with some public crime (which God forbid), he is to be removed from office. If, however, he is held by some hidden crime, he shall await the censure of the classical assembly, according to the greatness or lightness of the crime.

units.la: XIV.
units.tr: XIV.

units.la: Crimina quæ in Ministris nequaquam tolerari debent, ea ferè sunt hujusmodi, Hæresis, Schisma, Manifestus ordinis Ecclesiastici contemtus; Blasphemia manifesta & animadversione civili digna, Simonia, inhonestus ambitus ad alterius locum invadendum, Desertio sui muneris, suæque Ecclesiæ, sine legitimo consensu: Crimen falsi, Perjurium, Scortatio, Furtum, Ebriositas[?], Vis armata, omnisque vis correctione civili digna; Fœnus illicitum; Alea, cæterique ludi inhonesti, ac legibus interdicti: Manifesta affectatio tyrannidis in Ecclesiam ac Collegas, cæteraque alia hujusmodi, quæ vel inurunt infamiam, vel separationem ab Ecclesia merentur.
units.tr: The crimes which must by no means be tolerated in ministers are generally these: heresy, schism, manifest contempt of ecclesiastical order; manifest blasphemy worthy of civil punishment; simony; dishonourable ambition to seize another's place; desertion of one's office and of one's church without lawful consent; the crime of forgery, perjury, whoredom, theft, drunkenness[?], armed violence, and any violence worthy of civil correction; illicit usury; dice, and other dishonourable games forbidden by law; manifest striving after tyranny over the Church and colleagues; and other things of this kind which either bring infamy or deserve separation from the Church.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Delicta quæ quidem tolerantur, sed tamen reprehensioni & censuræ sunt obnoxia, ea fere sunt ejusmodi, inanis quædam quæstionum inutilium curiositas: ingenij ostentatio intempestivis allegorijs: in scripturarum studijs remissio: novarum consuetudinum quarundam pro libidine introductio: facetiæ indecoræ: verbum contumeliosum: temeritas: inanis gloriolæ cupiditas: plus æquo acres objurgationes, &c. quæ verbi divini Ministrum dedecent.
units.tr: The faults which are indeed tolerated, but nonetheless are liable to rebuke and censure, are generally of this sort: a certain empty curiosity about useless questions; display of wit by untimely allegories; negligence in the study of the Scriptures; the introduction of certain new customs at one's own whim; indecent jokes; abusive language; rashness; desire for empty glory; reproofs more bitter than is right, etc., which disgrace a minister of the divine Word.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: In levioribus vitijs, quæ ne judicio quidem confessus digna videbuntur, servetur ea quæ est in cæteris omnibus à Christo præscripta ratio.
units.tr: In lighter faults, which seem not even worthy of judgment by confession, the method prescribed by Christ in all other cases shall be observed.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Vt hic Censuræ ordo commodius observetur, utile erit in binos, vel ut minimum in ternos menses, Classis cuiusque conventum habeπ, in quo de huiusmodi rebus diligens fiat.
units.tr: So that this order of censure may be observed more conveniently, it will be useful for the classical assembly of each district to meet every two or at least every three months, at which careful attention is given to such matters.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Classis conventus non semper uno est habendus loco: tum ut Ecclesiarum alterius in alteram dominatus impediatur, tum vero ut singularum Ecclesiarum exploratio fiat diligentior, de verbi doctrinâ, vitâ, Ceremoniis ac disciplinæ ratione.
units.tr: The classical assembly should not always be held in one place: partly so that the domination of one church over another may be prevented, and partly so that each church may be examined more carefully as to the teaching of the Word, life, ceremonies, and the manner of discipline.

units.la: CAP. XV. De Matrimonio.
units.tr: CHAPTER XV. On Marriage.

units.la: Matrimonium initiari debet inter marem & fœminam ætatis justæ ex Reip. legibus.2. Consensu mutuo & Parentū, Tutorum vel aliorum, quorum interest.3. In præsentia ministri verbi, nominis divini invocatione.4. Verbis de præsenti & obligatoriis, quæ omnes excludunt conditiones.
units.tr: Marriage ought to be entered into between a man and a woman of lawful age according to the laws of the commonwealth; (2) with mutual consent and that of parents, guardians, or others whose interest is involved; (3) in the presence of a minister of the Word, with invocation of the name of God; (4) by words of the present tense and binding, which exclude all conditions.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Clandestina promissa, & contra voluntatem Parentum præstita, illegitima sunt & nullius valoris.
units.tr: Clandestine promises, and those given against the will of parents, are illegitimate and of no validity.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Verbi Minister ab initiandis in matrimonio interrogabit. 1.An sint ab omni promissione liberi.2.An parentes consen-tiant.3.An non sint consanguinei. 4. An sint Ecclesiae membra,aut saltem Reformatae religioni addicti, eoque Ecclesiae nomen dabunt.
units.tr: The minister of the Word shall question those about to enter marriage: (1) whether they are free from every promise; (2) whether their parents consent; (3) whether they are not related by blood; (4) whether they are members of the Church, or at least adhere to the Reformed religion, and will give their name to the Church.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Si parentes Religionis odio, aut alijs de causis iniustis se difficiles præstiterint, penes Consistorium erit, aut Magistratum, rem explorare & diiudicare.
units.tr: If parents prove difficult out of hatred of the religion, or for other unjust reasons, it shall be for the Consistory, or the magistrate, to examine the matter and judge it.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Peregrini & ignoti in matrimonio non sunt initiandi, nisi prius legitimo testimonio probent se ab omni promissione aliena esse liberos. Si pars alterutra vel utraquę ante ma-trimonio iuncta fuerit, de morte priorum coniu um[?] testimonium exhibebit legitimum.
units.tr: Strangers and unknown persons are not to be admitted to marriage unless they first prove by lawful testimony that they are free from every promise to another. If one or both parties have previously been joined in marriage, they shall produce lawful testimony concerning the death of the former spouses.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Sponsalia legitimè contracta ne utriusque quidem partis consensu dissolui poterunt.
units.tr: Betrothals lawfully contracted cannot be dissolved even by the consent of both parties.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Matrimonio conjungendorum nomina Tabulis publicis consignabuntur, & trinis diebus Dominicis, aut alioquin per tres vices iustis intervallis pro concione edentur, iisim-primis locis ubi habitant & noti sunt.
units.tr: The names of those to be joined in marriage shall be recorded in public registers and announced from the pulpit on three Lord's Days, or otherwise on three occasions at proper intervals, especially in the places where they live and are known.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Quovis die matrimonia confirmari & celebrari poterunt, modo concio ad populum habeatur, exceptis Cœnæ diebus, & ieiunio sacratis.
units.tr: Marriages may be confirmed and celebrated on any day, provided a sermon is preached to the people, except on the days of the Lord's Supper and those set apart for fasting.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Si matrimonij vinculum adulterio fuerit ruptum, ut partium fiat reconciliatio, serio est laborandum: Quod si frustra tentetur, & pars innocens alio velit iungi matrimonio, declarabit Synedrium (ubi adulterium coram Magistratu fuerit probatū[?]) ex verbi Dei norma illud ipsum esse legitimum.
units.tr: If the bond of marriage has been broken by adultery, serious effort must be made to bring about a reconciliation of the parties. But if this is attempted in vain, and the innocent party wishes to be joined in marriage to another, the Synod (where the adultery has been proved before the magistrate) shall declare that this very marriage is lawful according to the norm of the Word of God.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Viduæ (imprimis iuniores) ante quartum cum dimidio mensem novo non iungantur coniugio: postulat autem hoc necessitas & muliebris verecundia.
units.tr: Widows (especially younger ones) should not enter a new marriage before four and a half months have passed; necessity and feminine modesty require this.

units.la: Conclusio.
units.tr: Conclusion.

units.la: Articuli hi ad legitimum Ecclesiæ ordinem spectantes, ita mutuo consensu sunt constituti, utsi[?] utilitas Ecclesiarum aliud postulet, mutari, augeri, & minui possint & debeant.
units.tr: These articles, which pertain to the lawful order of the Church, have been so established by mutual consent that they may and should be changed, increased, and diminished if the usefulness of the Churches requires otherwise.

units.la: Non erit tamen privatæ alicuius Ecclesiæ id facere, sed dabunt omnes operam, ut illos observent, donec Synodo aliter constituatur.
units.tr: It will not, however, be for any single Church to do this; rather all shall take care to observe them until the Synod decides otherwise.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: FINIS.
